articleTitle: Quasi-canonization of motion equations of a two wheeled cart
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The modeling of a two wheeled cart models based on the quasi-canonization method is studied in this paper . For a two wheeled cart model, a set of suitable quasi-coordinates and quasi-momentums are defined according to the geometric characteristics of its configuration space, so that the motion differential equations of the two wheeled cart model is written in the form of Hamilton.. s canonical equation. In this way, the nonholonomic constraining force disappears from the motion differential equations of the wheeled cart model. And the number of the motion differential equations is also reduced due to the nonholonomic constraints on the cart. Moreover, the quasi-canonization means that the wheeled cart model has a special symplectic structure described by quasi-coordinates and quasi-momenta. This lays a foundation for applying numerical calculation methods and control methods based on the symplectic geometry to the study of the wheeled cart model.

articleTitle: Multi-feature based LSTM rolling bearing remaining useful life prediction
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Bearings are the key component of rotating machinery. Moreover, their performance directly affects the health of the whole machine. Bearing failure can lead to abrupt shutdown of rotating machinery, resulting in economic losses and even casualties. Bearing remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is a recognized method to address bearing failure and improve the safety and reliability of machinery. To realize the remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearings, this article used a data-driven research method, selects five full life cycle data of bearings under working condition 1 in the XJTU-SY rolling bearing acceleration degradation experimental vibration data set of Xi'an Jiao-Tong University as the database, takes the rolling bearing of model LDKUER204 as the research target to research the remaining life prediction of bearings. First, the life prediction characteristics of the bearing were computation, including the time domain characteristics of the bearing vibration signal, the Fourier transform of the vibration signal to get its energy characteristics, and the Shannon entropy of the vibration signal. Next, the normal and degradation stages determined according to the root-means-square (RMS) of the vibration signal, while the time domain features filtered by using the Wilson correlation coefficient to calculate the correlation coefficient between each time-domain feature and the RMS, and the above life prediction features normalized; finally, a life prediction model built using long short-term memory (LSTM) to predict the remaining useful life of the bearing. The results show we can predict well the remaining life of the bearing using the method in this article, and the prediction results are consistent with the decreasing trend of the remaining life of the bearing and the remaining life value.

articleTitle: Study on structural design and deployment performance of a new anti-UAV net bullet
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The security issues caused by the unmanned aerial vehicle(UAV) “black flying” are becoming serious, and the demand for anti-drone technology research is increasing. In this paper, a new single-barrel anti-UAV net gun that can be launched continuously is proposed. The performance of the anti-UAV net bullet is studied based on the finite element software ABAQUS. The corresponding finite element model is established to simulate the single-barrel anti-UAV net bullet's high-speed rotation and separation process. The influence of the material, thickness, and width of the bourrelet and bullet hoop on the deployment performance of the anti-UAV net bullet is analyzed. The simulation results show that nylon and copper can make the anti-UAV net bullet unfold successfully. In addition, as the width and thickness increase, the higher the rotation speed required for the separation of the projectile. This paper could provide a valuable reference for the research and design of the anti-UAV gun.

articleTitle: Study on flow field characteristics of V-shaped supersonic ash removal nozzle of armored vehicle trapezoidal filter element
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Pulse-jet air filter is a maintenance-free filter suitable for high dust environment of armored vehicles, which is often installed with a narrow trapezoidal filter element to achieve modular design of the intake system and high power density of the powertrain. In order to solve the difficult problem of ash removal in the narrow structure of trapezoidal filter element, a new supersonic nozzle with Laval nozzle and V-shaped deflector is designed based on the ash removal theory and the demand characteristics of ash removal force distribution of trapezoidal filter element. By computational fluid dynamics, the flow field characteristics of the supersonic nozzle jet and ash removal airflow is studied, the influence of the key nozzle parameters on the ash removal effect is analyzed, and the influence of the key parameters of the new supersonic nozzle on the ash removal characteristics is obtained, which provides a new idea and reference for the design of pulse-jetair filter of high power density armored vehicles.

articleTitle: Study on solution method of elasticplastic low-speed repeated impact between sphere and plate
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: To investigate the problem of elastic-plastic repeated impacts between sphere and plate, a solution method combining theoretical contact model and numerical solution method is proposed. Based on the Stronge's contact model, which some parameters are corrected, the repeated contact model between sphere and plate is deduced. A dynamic substructure model is established to simulate the dynamic deformation response of the plate. The solution method can predict the contact force, contact time, residual deformation and local stress of plate under low-speed repeated impacts. A three-dimensional finite element (FE) model of elastic-plastic wide plate repeatedly impacted by steel sphere was established. By comparing the simulation results, the calculation accuracy and efficiency of the solution method were verified, and the prediction of various key impact parameters was correct, which can save a lot of simulation resources and simulation time compared with the FE software. This solution method can be used to simulate a large number of examples and study the characteristics of repeated impact of elastic-plastic plates.

articleTitle: Location and inventory optimization model of spare parts warehouse based on uncertainty theory
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In equipment integrated logistics support, support activities and support resources have a vital impact on the availability of equipment system. Spare parts warehouse location and inventory strategy will directly affect spare parts supply, and finally affect the system operation. Therefore, this paper establishes an optimization model of spare parts warehouse location considering inventory strategy. In order to deal with the epistemic uncertainty of spare parts demand, the uncertainty theory is introduced. The model aims at reducing the comprehensive support cost, adds the supportability parameters to the model constraints, and optimizes the inventory control and spare parts warehouse location as a whole. The genetic algorithm is used to solve the model, and the optimal location scheme and inventory strategy meeting the supportability constraints are obtained. Based on the proposed model and calculation results, the accuracy of equipment support can be improved and the support cost can be reduced as much as possible on the premise of ensuring equipment availability.

articleTitle: Research on dynamics software of transfer matrix method for multibody systems
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The general and fast programmed dynamics modeling, computation and design method of complex mechanical multibody system have become the theoretical and technical problems that must be solved in the development of modern industry. The transfer matrix method for multibody systems (MSTMM) has become a powerful tool for dynamics modeling and simulation of multibody systems by virtue of its flexible modeling, such as no need for global dynamics equation, low matrix order, fast computational speed, automatic derivation of overall transfer equation and high degree of programming. In order to apply MSTMM to practical engineering problems quickly, the MSTMM is taken as the core theory of dynamics modeling and computation, and the visualization dynamics software of MSTMM is established by combining OpenCascade, Qt and other open source software. The software realizes the automatic derivation of the overall transfer equation and the fast computation of system dynamics. The engineering example of a tracked vehicle verifies the effectiveness of the software.

articleTitle: Experimental research on the influence of damping liquid viscosity on the dynamic parameters of steel spring isolator
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Based on the superposition theory, the dynamic restoring force can be decomposed into two parts, the nonlinear elastic restoring force and the nonlinear damping force, and a dynamic model of the steel spring isolator is proposed. Then the least square method is used to identify the stiffness and damping parameters represented in the hysteresis curve. The model reconstruction verifies the effectiveness of the established dynamic model to identify single load condition. The results show that under the same load conditions, the dynamic to static ratio and loss factor of the rubber isolator are greater than those of the steel spring isolator, indicating that the energy dissipation capacity of the steel spring isolator is insufficient. In addition, the viscosity of the damping fluid, the excitation frequency, and the load range have little effect on the dynamic to static ratio and loss factor of the steel spring isolator.

articleTitle: Operational effectiveness analysis of space reconnaissance equipment from the perspective of system dynamics
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: With the space reconnaissance equipment playing an increasingly important role in the process of future operations, how to effectively deal with the effectiveness of space reconnaissance equipment system has become a crucial problem. In this paper, a method for effectiveness analysis of aerospace reconnaissance equipment system from the perspective of system dynamics is proposed. The space reconnaissance equipment is divided into three subsystems according to its functions. The basic tree entry model of the reconnaissance subsystem is established by using the SD flow rate basic tree entry modeling method, and finally the SD model for the evaluation of space reconnaissance equipment is formed, and the combat effectiveness of space reconnaissance equipment system is analyzed. The simulation results show that SAR imaging reconnaissance satellite has a prominent impact on reconnaissance and surveillance capability, and electronic reconnaissance satellite plays a vital role in the whole combat process. This method can provide constructive suggestions for the future development of aerospace reconnaissance equipment system.

articleTitle: Basic problems and test verification of micro-vibration test in vacuum tank
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The disturbance sources of the spacecraft ground micro-vibration test, including both the structural transmission part and the air transmission part, are obviously different from the real disturbance sources. The micro-vibration test in vacuum tank avoids the disturbance caused by air propagation and is an alternative way for high performance spacecraft to conduct ground micro-vibration test. In this paper, the analysis of test data shows that under the condition of good vibration isolation of spacecraft, the disturbance caused by noise on spacecraft is obvious. In such cases, the response caused by airborne noise should be considered. In this paper, a series of verification tests are designed to give the environmental level of microvibration in conventional vacuum tanks, and through data analysis, the degree of vacuum to eliminate the influence of acoustic vibration in such vacuum tanks is proposed. Based on the above test results, this paper discusses how to isolate the vibration of the existing vacuum tank facilities and how to apply the existing in-orbit free boundary condition simulation device in vacuum tank to meet the demand of micro-vibration test.

articleTitle: Image guidance technology of rocket sub-stage landing based on strapdown inertial navigation
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In view of the full ballistic flight characteristics of the launch vehicle sub-stage, a strapdown inertial navigation model in the launch inertial system is established for the rocket sub-stage and the strapdown solution is realized in this coordinate system. In order to improve the reliability and accuracy of the autonomous landing of the rocket sub-stage under the shaking state, the guidance technology based on image recognition is introduced at the end of the landing. For the task of detecting and tracking multi-scale cooperative targets in complex backgrounds, we propose a target detection model based on the balanced attention feature pyramid and an improved DeepSort algorithm on the basis of the acceleration motion model, which have achieved the accurate detection and tracking of cooperative targets under the condition of shaking the rocket.

articleTitle: A rate-dependent peridynamic model for concrete under blast loading
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Explosion accidents and terrorist attacks seriously threaten the safety of concrete structures. To study the anti-explosion performance of concrete structures, a rate-dependent peridynamic model of concrete suitable for explosive load is established by introducing the strain rate effect of materials into the original peridynamic theoretical framework. In this model, the relationships between the stretch rate and the dynamic critical stretches of concrete are established. In addition, the strainsoftening effect of concrete and different fracture characteristics under tension and compression are considered in the model. To verify the correctness of the proposed model, the dynamic failure of concrete slabs under contact explosion is investigated, and the failure mode and crack propagation path consistent with the experimental results are obtained.

articleTitle: Penetration dynamics of asteroid exploration landing based on DEM
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Asteroid exploration is one of the hot areas of deep space exploration in recent years. In this paper, a landing attachment system for asteroid landing detection is proposed, which can complete the landing and attachment of the lander on the asteroid surface. Based on the discrete element method, this paper analyzes the landing impact and penetration dynamics in the process of land penetration. In this paper, the triaxial compression performance of simulated lunar soil is tested, and the physical and mechanical parameters of simulated lunar soil are studied, so as to realize the parameter matching between meso parameters of bulk medium and macro mechanical properties of soil. The penetration process of the detached body is studied. The penetration characteristics under different incident angles, velocities and shapes of the spear body are studied. The characteristics of the depth, velocity and acceleration of the anchor body with time are obtained. The landing impact dynamic characteristics of the anchoring device are obtained. This study provides a new analysis method for the study of asteroid detection anchoring and attachment, and has reference significance for the design of asteroid and other planetary landing and attachment detection.

articleTitle: Dynamic modeling and vibration analysis of milling robots
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: To deal with the situations where the complex dynamics modeling methods and the high computational cost, a method of rapid dynamic modeling and vibration response analysis of milling robot is proposed. Taking the influence of joint flexibility into account, the transfer matrix method for multibody system is applied to establish the rigid-flexible coupling multibody system dynamic model of milling robot in this paper, and its vibration characteristics and dynamic response are dissected. First, the robot system and milling dynamics model are established to form a dynamics numerical simulation system. Then, the vibration characteristics and dynamic response of the robot system are solved, and the relationship between the dynamic parameters of the robot body and the processing process parameters and the dynamic response is revealed. Finally, a dynamic test and a robot milling test were designed to verify the accuracy of the dynamic model.

articleTitle: Research on the mechanism of suppressing flutter of cascade with frequency mistuning
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Flutter is an aero-elastic problem that must be avoided in aero-engines. As the most effective method to suppress flutter, frequency mistuning has been widely concerned and studied. However the current understanding of the mechanism of frequency mistuning to suppress flutter is limited, so the exploration of its mechanism is of great significance in practical engineering. In this paper, the influence coefficient method is used to study the effect of frequency mistuning forms and frequency difference on the aerodynamic damping coefficient and cumulative work of the mistuned cascade, and the limitation of the definition of the aerodynamic damping coefficient of the mistuned cascade is pointed out. Besides the mechanism of frequency mistuning to suppress flutter is explored. In addition, this paper also combines the resonance theory to study the method of calculating the minimum frequency difference to stablize the cascade. The results show that the frequency mistuning suppresses flutter by reducing the aerodynamic coupling between the blades in the cascade, and the frequency mistuning of the adjacent blade on the suction surface of the reference blade plays a decisive role in the aero-elastic stability of the reference blade. Moreover, the greater the frequency difference, the smaller the amplitude of the reference blade cumulative work, the better the effect of frequency mistuning on improving the aero-elastic stability of the cascade. Furthermore, it is feasible to use the reference blade resonance band to calculate the minimum frequency difference to stablize the cascade.

articleTitle: Research on the theory of interaction between shipboard equipment and foundation under shock condition
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The shock response of shipboard equipment under Underwater Explosion (UNDEX) is directly affects the combat capability of ship. In order to accurately predict the dynamic response of shipboard equipment under UNDEX, based on transfer function and wave theory, the transfer of explosive shock loads in the hull structure was studied. By comparing the similarities and differences between structural shock and vibration, combining with the equipment shock test data, based on the mechanical impedance theory, a shock impedance theory suitable for explosion shock conditions was proposed. Based on this theory, the dynamic response of shipboard equipment under UNDEX was predicted and compared with the relevant standard data. The results show that the method is in good agreement with the experimental data. The method in this paper gives the theory of load transfer in the hull structure and the interaction between the equipment and its installation foundation, which provides a theoretical basis for the shock resistance of shipboard equipment.

articleTitle: Model and simulation of the launching process of cased telescoped ammunition
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In order to study the dynamic characteristics of the launching process of cased telescoped ammunition (CTA) and optimize its internal ballistic performance, a theoretical model of the launching process of CTA is given based on secondary ignition and propellant programmed combustion control technology. Numerical simulation is carried out for the firing experiment of 35 mm CTA, and its correctness is verified. On this basis, the launching process of 45 mm cased telescoped ammunition armorpiercing projectile is numerically predicted, and the effects of loading parameters such as weight and impetus of propellant and projectile weight on the interior ballistic performance of CTA are analyzed. The research results provide a theoretical basis for the experimental research of cased telescoped ammunition.

articleTitle: Iterative feedback design of de Laval nozzle
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The cold gas propulsion through de Laval nozzles is a convenient way to enable position and attitude manoeuvres of groundbased satellite simulators. A parametric model of a de Laval nozzle is established base on the theory of one-dimensional isentropic flow, and the methodology of Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) is adopted to guide the iterative feedback design process. In the process of design, the effect of design factors on the nozzle performance are evaluated, such as nozzle shape, length of convergent and divergent section, inlet and outlet diameters, and throat diameter. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate the improvement of the nozzle performance through iterative feedback design.

articleTitle: Controllability and observability of transfer matrix method for linear controlled multibody system
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The research on vibration characteristics and control of multi-body system is a research focus in the field of mechanical system dynamics and control engineering. For the controlled multibody system, the transfer equation of controlled element and the total transfer equation of the controlled system are derived in this paper, and the controllability and observability of the transfer matrix method for linear controlled multibody system are analyzed. An example simulation shows that the transfer matrix method for linear controlled multibody system is effective, The engineering application of controlled multibody system transfer matrix method has important theoretical and practical significance to solve a series of major engineering problems in the field of controlled multibody system dynamics and control.

articleTitle: Effects of working conditions on the nonlinear dynamic performances of a rigid rotor for air journal bearing
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The vibration of the rotor for an air journal bearing is extremely complicated, which always exhibits nonlinear dynamic performances. In this paper, the transient Reynolds equation is solved by the finite element method so that the pressure distribution of air film can also be obtained, which determines the transient force acting on the rotor. The dynamic equation of rotor motion with mass eccentricity and external harmonic force is derived. The trajectory of the rotor can be acquired by solving the two equations continuously through the weak-coupling solution method. Effects of working conditions including supply pressure and rotational speed on the nonlinear dynamic performances of an air journal bearing are studied based on the trajectory, Poincaré map, frequency spectrum diagram and bifurcation diagram. The results show that increasing the supply pressure can reduce the rotor vibration amplitude. The vibration amplitude shows an upward trend as the rotational speed increases. There always exists a vibration frequency corresponding to the external harmonic force, while the vibration amplitude is small.

articleTitle: Study on transmission characteristics of torsion spring-loaded double-gear anti-backlash mechanism
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Torsion spring-loaded double-gear anti-backlash mechanism (anti-backlash mechanism) has been widely used in the gear transmission mechanism of weapon equipment, because of its advantages of being simple in structure, easy to implement and high reliability. In order to provide theoretical analysis for improving the meshing stiffness of the anti-backlash mechanism, this paper takes the torsion spring-loaded double-gear anti-backlash mechanism of tank armored vehicles as the research object. The dynamics model of the research object is established. Based on the dynamics model, the influence mechanism of the gear contact ratio and tooth profile parameters on the meshing stiffness of the anti-backlash mechanism is analyzed, and the law of the anti-backlash mechanism meshing stiffness change is studied during gear reversal motion.

articleTitle: Compensation of the coupled vibration and viscoelastic nonlinearity of dielectric elastomer actuators through closed-loop input shaper and direct inverse hysteresis control
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In this work, we present a control approach to remove the coupled vibration and viscoelastic nonlinearity of DEAs. To this end, we firstly characterize the dynamical responses of DEAs, demonstrating complex nonlinearities, including vibration, viscoelastic creep and hysteresis nonlinearities. Then, a closed-loop input shaper is designed to remove the vibration phenomenon and viscoelastic creep nonlinearity. Finally, based on a phenomenological hysteresis model, a direct inverse hysteresis controller is further developed to eliminate the viscoelastic hysteresis nonlinearity of the compensated system. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed control approach, several static and periodical trajectories tracking experiments are conducted. The experimental results demonstrate that: with our control approach, DEA can precisely track sinusoidal trajectories with different frequencies, and the maximum tracking error and the root mean square error decrease from 63.56% to 19.81% and 29.02% to 9.58%, respectively. This work is the early attempt to remove the coupled vibration and viscoelastic nonlinearity, which capable of improving the working bandwidth of DEAs and may pave the way for practical applications

articleTitle: Dynamic modeling of a rotating coupled bending-torsional beam by a transfer matrix method
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The vibration characteristics of rotating blades take an important position in the structural reliability of rotating machinery. To perform rapid and accurate vibration characteristics analysis, the Transfer Matrix Method of Multibody System (MSTMM) is proposed to study the multibody dynamics model of rotation blade. The blade is considered as the coupled bending-torsional beam, and the computational modelling challenge lies in the derivation of rotating coupled bending-torsional beam. The model is verified by comparison with finite element method (FEM) results. By computing the vibration characteristics with varying rotating speed, the influence of the blade rotation is illustrated. The computational results show that, due to stiffening, the natural frequencies increase with the rotation speeding up, especially the flapwise bending mode. The modeling process is simple and rapid, only assembling the transfer matrix of each element like building blocks. This proposed model can be applied to compute coupled bending-torsional frequencies of helicopter and wind turbine blades, and the results can provide useful guidance for the modeling of rotating machinery.

articleTitle: Fluid topology optimization of gas-turbine-related components
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Fluid topology optimization has higher design freedom than traditional shape and size optimization methods. Its design parameters are represented by a porosity parameter defined at each grid node in the design domain. Hence, the topology optimization has superiorities in creating novel and high-performance structures or flow ducts. Considering this, this method is adopted in this work to design gas-turbine-related flow passages, which mainly include an abrupt pipe, and U-bend channel and the contouring profile of a rotor blade tip. The objective for all cases is to improve the duct aerodynamic performance. To do this, both a quasi-sensitivity and an adjoint sensitivity approaches are utilized. In addition, flow fields in all optimized flow ducts are predicted using CFD simulations. Results clarifies the mechanism in improving the aerodynamic performance of the designed structures.

articleTitle: Integrated evaluation method of simulation and test of firing precision for multiple launch rocket system
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The firing precision is one of the important indexes to measure the tactical and technical performance of multiple launch rocket system (MLRS). Reducing the ammunition amount used in precision test of the MLRS is a major problem to be solved urgently at home and abroad, which has attracted extensive attention. A nonlinear dynamics model of the MLRS including wheels, vehicle body, releveling body and pitching body is established by using Riccati transfer matrix method for multibody system (RMSTMM). With the above dynamics model, the MLRS firing precision dynamics simulation system is constructed and then the credibility comprehensive evaluation method is given. Finally, a test scheme design method of firing precision for the MLRS based Bayesian method is proposed, which provides a theoretical basis and effective technical means for reducing the ammunition amount used in test and improving the test evaluation level.

articleTitle: Modelling and simulation of the 3D surface topography in ultra-precision flycutting machining
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: A simulation model of the 3D surface topography in ultra-precision flycutting machining is built in this paper. The influences of the cutting parameters, the cutting interference phenomenon, the relative vibration between the tool tip and the workpiece and the workpiece shape are analysed. The formation mechanism of the stripes along the cutting direction and the feed direction is explained. The simulation model can be used to optimize the cutting process of the ultra-precision flycutting machining, which avoids time and money consuming cutting experiments, and can also provide new ideas for tracing the source of the stripes on the surface topography.

articleTitle: Study on parallel algorithm for engineering calculation of jet force on multiple launch rocket system
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Multiple launch rocket system (MLRS) is a kind of modern conventional weapon with very important military status. Impact of the jet force is an important factor affecting the firing dispersion of the MLRS. It is necessary to find a method to accelerate the calculation of the jet force on the rocket launcher because of its large amount of calculation and time consuming. This paper took the model described in a paper as an example and used CUDA parallel computing model to design a parallel algorithm for calculating the jet force on the front side of the rocket launcher. The relationship between the speed-up ratio of this algorithm and hardware conFig.uration was analyzed. The results show that the parallel algorithm described in this paper significantly accelerates the calculation of the jet force on the rocket launcher and has certain adaptive ability.

articleTitle: A design of magnetorheological-fluid elastomer damper for engine mount
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In this paper, a magnetorheological fluid-elastomer damper is designed, which is mainly used to reduce the vibration of tank and armored vehicle engines. The structure of the damper is simple, the stiffness and damping are controllable, and the parameters of the damper can be adjusted in real time under different vibration conditions to achieve the best damping effect. The magnetic circuit of the damper is simulated and optimized by ANSYS software. The prototype of the damper is manufactured and assembled, and the performance of the damper prototype is tested by using the dynamic test system.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of the extrusion forming dynamic process of polymer material
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The extrusion forming process plays an important role in the production of polymer material. In order to study the status of the internal flow field of an extrusion die of polymer material during the extrusion forming process and the extrusion deformation of this polymer material, a dynamic model of the extrusion forming process of polymer material was established based on the extrusion die of this polymer material used in production. The finite element method was used to simulate the extrusion forming dynamic process, and the distribution of pressure field and velocity field in the extrusion die was studied and the cause of extrusion deformation of this polymer material was analysed. Result shows that the deformation of formed material is due to the elastic recovery effect.

articleTitle: Research on target positioning algorithm and error analysis of the target positioning system
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of using the target positioning system to locate moving target, we propose a method that can locate moving target by using radar ranging and the target positioning system information. The article first introduces the coordinate system used in the process of the seeker's positioning of the moving target, then analyzes the use of the Vincenty formula in the process of solving the moving target, and analyzes the source and error of the seeker's target positioning in the flying test. Finally, the target positioning results based on the seeker's flying data are analyzed. The results show that the positioning of the moving target by the seeker has high accuracy, indicating that the use of the seeker to locate the moving target has certain engineering application value.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis on dynamic wave responses of hydrogels
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: As a liquid-containing porous media, the microstructure of hydrogels is composed of solid framework and flowing fluid. There is a mutual coupling effect between the diffusion of pore fluid and the elastic deformation of the solid framework, so the solution of hydrogel dynamic responses is more complicated. Based on the Biot's theory, the wave propagation model of hydrogels is developed. The two-phase coupled wave governing equation of hydrogels is established, and then it is derived into equivalent weak forms to facilitate the next numerical computation. The dynamic responses of hydrogels analysed by the method in this paper is compared with the semi-analytical solution, and the result shows a good agreement with each other, which proves reasonability and feasibility of the method proposed. Furthermore, the transient responses of hydrogel block under impact load and periodic load are investigated to accurately analyse soft matters. According to the wave propagation model in this paper, the propagation and reflection process of waves in hydrogels can be captured by convenient numerical analysis.

articleTitle: Rebound plate design for flip-flow screen and effects on screening process of material group
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: With the 30-50g ejection acceleration of screen panels, the flip-flow screen provides an effective solution for fine coal screening. However, the high ejection acceleration prolongs material particles residence time in the air, which leads to insufficient contacts between particles and screen panels, and finally resulting in the aggravation of particles mismatches. To decrease the mismatch rate, the idea of introducing secondary collisions for particles is proposed, thus, the rebound plate is designed for the flip-flow screen. Firstly, the co-simulation of the screening process is built to investigate the height distributions of material group particles. Then, the installation structure and height range of the rebound plate is determined according to particles motion laws. Moreover, the motion trajectory comparison of a single particle on flip-flow screens with and without the rebound plate is performed to evaluate effects of secondary collisions. Finally, influences of rebound plate installation heights on material group motions, particle-screen panel contacts and screening performances are studied. Results indicate that the installation of the rebound plate increases contact probabilities and penetrate probabilities of material group particles. When the installation height is 120-150 mm, the screening efficiency can be significantly improved at less expenses of the productivity loss.

articleTitle: Modelling of cake filtration in centrifugal dewatering by finite difference
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: A theoretical study of cake filtration in centrifuge dewatering is presented in this paper. The one-dimensional solid/liquid system is obtained by Darcy's law and mass balance. The spatial and temporal governing equations in is discretized by finite difference method. Newton iteration method is chosen to solve these conservation equations. The comparison between the calculation of Peter in their case shows that solution in this paper is accurate and reliable. The result shows that both solid sedimentation velocity and liquid velocity reduce at filling process, and the reduction of solid velocity is less than that of liquid velocity.

articleTitle: On graphical method of mechanical dynamics based on balance equation of rotating moment around moving point
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Graphical method is an effective method to verify the results of analytical method. However, the research on graphical method of mechanical dynamics can not be carried out until the moment balance equation of rigid body rotating around moving point (practical equation A) is given in our open paper. The main reason is that the connecting rod is not a body rotating around a fixed point, and its moment balance equation contains too many unknowns. Practical equation A is derived based on the research idea of Fangyan equation. 1) Our 8 previous research results in mechanical dynamics were summarized. The instantaneous centre between two bodies is velocity instantaneous centre. After analysis, there is not necessarily acceleration instantaneous centre between two bodies. 2) A rotation moment balance equation (qualitative equation B) of a rigid body around a moving point was proposed based on qualitative analysis. 3) A crank rocker mechanism is taken as an example. The moment of rotation of a rigid body around the centroid (ordinary equation C) was practiced too. Practical equation A is as correct as ordinary equation C. Practical equation A makes the results of the graphical method of mechanical dynamics feasible.

articleTitle: Global mapping analysis tools for asteroid exploration
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Evaluating the performance of mapping orbits is significant to the design of the mapping plan for asteroids. The global mapping analysis tool is developed to help the engineers analyse the possible mapping plans for different types of asteroids. This software provides support on the trajectory propagation and observation geometry analysis, including the asteroid shape modelling, occultation checking, and simulation visualizing. This paper briefly introduces the global mapping analysis tool using several asteroids as examples.

articleTitle: Influence of propellant charge structure parameters on the intergranular compression stress at projectile bottom
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The chamber explosion caused by propellant charge is essentially the large-scale fragmentation of the propellant charge at the projectile bottom, and the inter-granular compression stress is crucial to the fragmentation. In order to figure out the influence of propellant charge structures on the inter-granular compression stress between propellant particles, an interior ballistic twophase flow model and simulation system is established with a large caliber howitzer as the research object. Then the effects of ignition hole diameter, hole breaking pressure, arc thickness and charge amount on the inter-granular compression stress between propellant particles are studied respectively. The results show the significant effects of arc thickness and charge amount on the inter-granular compression stress between propellant particles, but the little effect of ignition hole diameter and hole breaking pressure. By improving the aforementioned propellant charge structure, the inter-granular compression stress can be effectively reduced by more than 5%while the original ballistic performance is guaranteed. The method presented in this paper provides a certain theoretical basis for improving the launch safety of the propellant charge.

articleTitle: Analytical solution for initial error propagation model of vehicle launched on moving base
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The analytical solution for initial error propagation model of vehicle launched on moving base is proposed by regular perturbation theory. First, in order to deal with the complex nonlinear time-varying system that cannot been solved by traditional method such as Laplace transform, a method based on the regular perturbation theory is developed to decompose the nonlinear time-varying solving problem into a sequence of linear problems to solve in order. Second, the spectral decomposition method (SDM) is put forward to solve the zeroth-order subsystems. Third, by substituting the zeroth-order solutions into the first-order subsystem and making some skilfully simplifications, the first-order solutions can be obtained by SDM as well. Then, higher order solutions can be calculated by the same method as in step three. The simulation results show that the analytical solutions truncated after 3rd term are in good agreement with the numerical solutions. Even though the flight time is as long as 3000s, the estimated guidance errors by the proposed analytical solutions are less than 6% compared with those by the numerical solutions.

articleTitle: Dynamic characteristics of an inflatable space structure with distributed control moment gyroscopes
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In this paper, the influence of control moment gyroscope (CMG) on the dynamic characteristics of an inflatable space structure is studied. The absolute nodal coordinate formulation (ANCF) and the natural coordinate formulation (NCF) are used to describe the flexible components and rigid satellite in the inflatable space structure system. A model of CMG based on NCF is proposed, in which the gyro base is regarded as rigid body, and the gimbal and rotor as gyroscopic factors in the gyro base model. The dynamic equations of the gimbal and rotor are obtained by Lagrange equation. Positions of the gimbal and rotor are set by defining inertia parameters of the rigid base. The accuracy of the dynamic model of inflatable space structure is verified via commercial finite element, including the coupling dynamics between the gyro and the inflatable structure. Compared to the CMG output term and the particle-moment equivalent model, it can be concluded that the gyro output moment conforms to the physical law. The results show the feasibility of dynamic model of the rigid-flexible coupling multibody system.

articleTitle: Magnetic and dynamic analysis of a new type of wall-climbing robot
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Wall-climbing robots are a promising enabling technology for a wide range of high-altitude operations in industrial production, including cleaning, descaling and spraying of large ships, inspection, flaw detection and maintenance of thermal power boilers, etc. This is due to their high work efficiency and high safety when compared with traditional manual operations. However, existing wall-climbing robots still remain some challenges that limit their development. Here, we propose a new type of wall-climbing robot capable of achieving floating obstacle-climbing by using springs and linear bearings and realizing magnetic adjustment by using electric push rods. We develop a theoretical model to analyze statics and dynamics of the wall-climbing robot, and then use Ansoft and Adams to analyze the process of obstacle crossing, magnetic attraction force, driving force and speed change. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed wall-climbing robot can achieve the effect for floating to overcome obstacle crossing and adjustable magnetic force.

articleTitle: Uncertainty analysis in measurement of contact friction parameters of bolted joint interface
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In the literature [1,2], a test apparatus was proposed for high-precision measurement of contact friction parameters based on piezoelectric actuator and laser vibrometer. Based on this test apparatus, five pairs of nominally identical bolted joint specimen were fabricated according to the same drawings and process, and they were assembled and tested using four test plans under two bolt preloads. The reassembly uncertainties of the test apparatus were taken into account to assess the variability of the test results and to analyse error sources. Then the influence of part-to-part differences of nominally identical specimen pairs on the contact friction parameters was investigated. Finally, the variability of contact parameters for rough surfaces and smooth surfaces were studied, which indicates that roughness has an important effect on the uncertainty of test results. The results in this paper suggest that the micro morphology of the contact interface has a significant effect on the tangential contact stiffness, followed by energy dissipation, and has less impact on the friction coefficient. Differences in mechanical properties of nominally identical joint structures caused by differences in micromorphology should be considered in the actual analysis.

articleTitle: Structural design of hydraulic pipeline secondary source in active pulsation control system
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Pressure pulsation always produces harmful vibration and noise, which can be effectively reduced by active pulsation control system. The key component in the active pulsation control system is secondary source, which is used to generate secondary pulsation to offset the primary pulsation. However, the static pressure in the hydraulic pipeline is extremely high and makes it difficult to design the secondary source. The pipeline secondary source includes non-intrusive and intrusive structures. The pulsation output capabilities of the two structures are different, but the difference has not been well studied and resolved at present. In this paper, theoretical models of the pulsations generated by the non-intrusive and intrusive secondary sources are established, and the difference in power consumption of the secondary source is compared. In the hydraulic pipeline experimental system, secondary pulsations generated by the two secondary sources are measured. Theoretical and experimental results show that under the same input power, the pulsation output capability of the intrusive secondary source is much higher than that of the non-intrusive secondary source. Using the designed intrusive secondary source to control the pressure pulsation in the hydraulic pipeline system, the amplitudes of the three single-frequency pulsations within 250 Hz are attenuated by more than 25 dB.

articleTitle: Research on vehicle engine dynamics simulation based on transfer matrix method for multibody systems
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The engine is the core component of a vehicle, its dynamical characteristics are directly related to the performance of the vehicle. In order to simulate the dynamical characteristics, engine can be modelled as a shell and a crank-connecting rodpiston mechanism. Transfer matrix method for multibody systems is used to deduce the mathematical equations and develop the simulation program code. The time history curves of displacement, velocity and acceleration of the engine mechanism are plotted. Compared with the results by the ADAMS software, the agreeable datum show that this method can accurately calculate the motion characteristics of the engine. It provides a reference for the optimal design of various engines.

articleTitle: Vibration and hypervelocity gouging of sliding pairs in electromagnetic railguns
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Hypervelocity gouging has been observed over several decades in engineering applications involving rocket sled, electromagnetic railgun and light-gas gun. In this paper, numerical simulations using explicit finite element method were carried out to investigate the gouging mechanism in railguns. Two models were constructed and discussed: one is the non-uniform contact model under magnetic pressure, and the other is the transverse swing impact model. The former shows that, the non-uniform contact under the action of magnetic pressure will not cause gouging, but will form grooves, although the armature slides parallel to the rail at a high speed. The latter shows that, the lateral swing of the armature at a high speed can lead to oblique impacts on the interface, forming pressure cores, and eventually gouging.

articleTitle: Analysis of submarine mast vibration response by transfer matrix method for multibody systems
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The submarine mast will bend and vibrate under the impact of the current, and the serious vibration will affect the mast performance and even damage the mast. Therefore, the dynamic characteristics of submarine masts are critical in their design. In this paper, the multi-supported mast of a submarine is modeled using transfer matrix method for multibody systems (MSTMM). The element transfer equations are derived for rigid body sheet, spring, beam and rigid body sheet coupled spring, respectively. Considering the rigid body sheet and spring as one element or two independent elements, two modeling ways are proposed, and the system overall transfer equation is deduced separately. The modal superposition method is used to calculate the forced vibration response by establishing the body dynamic equations and augmented eigenvectors. Without deducing system global dynamics equation and with simplicity, efficiency and versatility. Two numerical examples are used to demonstrate MSTMM's modeling flexibility. It provided a theoretical basis for the structural analysis and optimization design of the submarine mast.

articleTitle: Research of spacecraft vibration test data statistics and application
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Spacecraft vibration test data is a significant reference to spacecraft performance evaluation. For a typical spacecraft platform, the frequency drift and the response peak drift of the dynamic response of the spacecraft in the vibration test are extracted as the feature data, and the statistical rule of the feature data is analyzed. And then two vibration test success envelopment model based on 3σ interval and polynomial fitting are proposed. The vibration test success envelopment model are applied to spacecraft structure performance evaluation and fault diagnosis analysis. The results indicate that the feature data of the vibration test are in accord with the normal distribution law, the frequency drift distributes mainly in −2.9%∼2.1%, and the response peak drift distributes basically in −18.3%∼17.5%. And the method of vibration test success envelopment provides theoretical and practical support for the spacecraft vibration test data mining analysis and application.

articleTitle: Effect of strain rate on microstructure and mechanical properties of martensitic steel
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Martensite steel is one kind of unique ultra-high strength steel, which is widely used in aerospace, automotive, weaponry, etc. mechanical systems. The strain rate is known to have significant effect on mechanical properties and microstructure of steel materials. This study focused on the mechanical properties and microstructure evolution of martensitic steel under different strain rates. The results showed that the yield strength and tensile strength increase with the increasing strain rate, but the elongation is the opposite. The electron backscatter diffraction results exhibited that as the strain rate decreases, the content of substructures decreases while the content of deformed structure increases. Moreover, the Schmidt factor decreases as the strain rate increases. The geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) densities calculated indirectly through the kernel average misorientation diagram reached a maximum value of 18.55×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup> m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The GNDs can hinder the slip of dislocations and thus improve the strength of the material. The fracture morphology observed by scanning electron microscopy showed that the high strain rate resulted in small and shallow dimples, bringing high strength; while the dimples formed by low strain rate were large and deep, contributing to the optimal plasticity. Our research reveals the relationship between strain rate and structure and properties of martensitic steel, providing guidance for its application on complicated mechanical systems under varying loads.

articleTitle: Research on the control strategy of tracked vehicle semi-active suspension based on improved particle swarm algorithm
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: To improve the driving comfort of armored vehicles, a semi-active suspension control strategy for armored vehicles based on an improved particle swarm (PSO) algorithm is proposed. Taking a tracked armored vehicle as an example, firstly, based on the Matlab/Simulink module, the 1/2 vehicle suspension system model, the ideal sky-hook, and the actual sky-hook control model are established respectively. Then, the improved PSO algorithm is used to optimize the control parameters. Finally, the simulation results of the semi-active suspension with the sky-hook control strategy and the traditional passive suspension are compared and analyzed in the time domain. The results show that the sky-hook control parameter optimization based on improved PSO algorithm can significantly improve the dynamic performance of suspension, which proves the correctness of the control parameter optimization results and the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Numerical study of wind shear effects on the aerodynamics and wake field of wind turbines
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Inhomogeneous and unsteady inflow wind speed caused by wake to the downstream wind turbine impairs its aerodynamic performances inevitably. To attenuate the adverse effects of the wake, the underlying flow mechanism of three-dimensional unsteady and rotational wake should be understood in depth. This paper investigates wind shear effects on the wake profile and the aerodynamic characteristics of wind turbines. Aerodynamic performances and wake flow of a scaled-down NREL 1.5 MW wind turbine are predicted numerically. Unsteady Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes equations, the k-. SST turbulence model and the sliding mesh method are used. The calculated velocity profiles of the wake are validated against the windtunnel experimental data. The simulation results show that the combined effects of wind shear and tower shadow can produce periodic fluctuations of the aerodynamic thrust and the torque of rotating blades. When the wind shear coefficient increases from 0 to 0.2, its thrust and torque are reduced by 0.4% and 1.4% respectively. On the other hand, the tower also leads to the asymmetry velocity profile of the wake. This implies that the combined effects of wind shear and tower shadow significantly complicate the wake flow. This work might contribute to improving the aerodynamic modelling of the three-dimensional wake flow.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a simple anti-UAV device
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Since the “black flight” problem of “low, slow, and small” aircraft are becoming more and more serious, this paper proposes a capture net anti-UAV device based on the electromagnetic emission principle. In this paper, a coil-type electromagnetic auncher is designed, which consists of three parts: launch structure, control structure, and capture net structure. In this paper, the characteristics of the designed launcher are taken as the experimental parameters, and the internal ballistic model of the launcher is established by Maxwell software. The relationship between the electromagnetic force, displacement, and velocity of the projectile during the discharge process is analysed. The results show that the ideal firing velocity of the projectile can reach 30m/s.. and the launch velocity can reach 20m/s. In this paper, the force analysis of the flying process of the projectile is carried out, and the outer ballistic model of the projectile is established by MATLAB software. The results show that the projectile can achieve the target capture within the 40m range after firing at 20m/s speed. In this paper, a method of controlling SG90 steering gear based on 51 single chip microcomputers is proposed, and the steering gear rotation Angle is controlled by C language, to change the launching direction. The experimental results show that the control strategy can realize the free control of the steering gear in the horizontal and vertical directions. The design idea of the anti-UAV device proposed in this paper has higher stability and portability, which provides a broader basis for the application of the anti-UAV device.

articleTitle: Sensitivity analysis of multiple launch rocket system based on the response surface method
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: With the advantages of fast firing speed, sudden and fierce firepower, low cost, strong mobility and quick response, multiple launch rocket system (MLRS) has become one of the main weapons in modern war. The optimization design is an important method to improve the performance of MLRS, and the sensitivity analysis of MLRS dynamics is an important way to improve the efficiency of optimization design. With the linear transfer matrix method for multibody systems (the linear MSTMM), the launch dynamics response of MLRS was simulated. The modeling and simulation results were validated by the test results. Due to the collision between the rocket and the launch tube, the response simulation is not differentiable. Analytic method for sensitivity analysis, such as the direct differentiation method, can not be used directly. The responce surface method is a combination of mathematical method and statistical method. Its basis idea is establishing an agent function to replace the orignal objective function for fast calculation. Based on the responce surface method, an agent function of initial disturbance of MLRS were established, and the agent function were validated by the test group data. By differentiation of the agent function, the sensitivity analysis results of initial disturbance of MLRS were obtained. The proposed method is easy to implement for engineering. The main factors affecting the initial disturbance of MLRS are pointed out. This paper provides theorectical basis and technical support for the design, development, and improvement of firing density of MLRS.

articleTitle: DEM simulation of cylindrical particle's dispersion characteristics for single modular charge ignition and flame-spreading
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The Discrete element method (DEM) simulation of cylindrical particles is performed based on the three-dimensional unsteady-state model in order to investigate the distribution and packing characteristics of cylindrical propellant grains during ignition and flame-spreading process of single modular charge, with cylinder-shaped particles being modelled by multi-element particle. The numerical measurements indicate good agreement with experiments, and it is more accurate than the simplified spherical particle model. The simulation results suggest that under the four simulated working conditions that the initial loading position of the modular cartridge is 10, 40, 70 mm and 100 mm from the primer respectively, the particles are finally distributed in the chamber on the right side of the cartridge showing horizontal and slope stacking from primer side to pressure control diaphragm side. The axial length of horizontal stacking decreases from 293.3 mm to 203.8 mm, and the angle of the sloped stacking decreases from 22.01° to 19.82° when the distance between the initial loading position of the modular cartridge and the primer increases from 10 mm to 100 mm. In other words, as the modular cartridge moves to the right, the axial length of horizontal stacking becomes shorter because the starting point moves to the right, and the stacking thickness increases slightly. However, the axial length of slope accumulation is almost unchanged, and the slope becomes flat.

articleTitle: Suppression of the primary resonance vibrations of a Jeffcott rotor using a preloaded snubber ring
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In rotating machinery, suppressing large-amplitude resonances in the vicinities of the major critical speeds has been a challenging problem. A finite element model of a Jeffcott rotor with a preloaded snubber ring subjected to unbalance excitation has been developed. An initial gap is reserved between the snubber ring mounted on the support and the rotating shaft, and the nonlinear stiffness characteristic is achieved by using laminated springs with preload. When passing through the critical speed, the rotor is supported by additional discontinuous stiffness once it contacts the preload snubber ring, completing the switch from one regime to another by reserved clearance. Therefore, the resonance amplitude is suppressed by system switching. In this paper, we focus on the effects of the snubber ring inertia and the reserved clearance on the vibration characteristics and damping performance of the hybrid dynamical system. Finally, it is verified by experiments that the designed backup support with a preloaded snubber ring can provide good vibration suppression for the primary resonance vibrations of the rotor system, and the maximum amplitude suppression rate can reach about 80%.

articleTitle: Predefined-time attitude tracking control for uncertain rigid spacecraft with guaranteed performance
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: This brief tackles the predefined-time guaranteed performance attitude tracking problem of rigid spacecraft in presence of uncertain inertia and disturbances. Primarily, a novel non-singular predefined-time terminal sliding mode (NPTSM) surface with the prescribed performance attitude tracking errors is constructed. Secondly, a robust NPTSM control (NPTSMC) is developed to tackle the predefined-time attitude tracking problem for uncertain spacecraft. It is proved that the designed NPTSMC can assure that the attitude tracking errors satisfy the prescribed performance boundaries and globally converge to a predefined small region centered on the equilibrium point in predefined time and then converge to the equilibrium point asymptotically. The advantage of the NPTSMC is predefined-time stability with quantified transient, steady-state and settling time performance. The effectiveness performance of the exploited approach is verified numerical simulation results.

articleTitle: Optimization for dynamic compression and fracture test of propellant charge
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The excessive fracture of propellant charge is the key to reveal the breech blow caused by propellant charge. The dynamic compression and fracture test of propellant charge is the only existing simulation approach to reproduce the propellant charge fracture process under launch environment. However, the simulation of the compression stress of propellant charge is essentially a process with trial and error, meantime, the dispersion of the compression stress obtained under the constant experiment condition is a stumbling block in launch safety research. To solve them, this paper attempts to establish a regression model of compression stress of propellant charge through several machine learning methods, and then the optimal model with high generalization ability is demonstrated by experiment. On account of the distribution test of model error, this method can predict the compression stress test results as well as the corresponding range with high confidence. Overall, this method makes it feasible to provide an effective reference for test conditions to acquire the target compression stress of propellant charge, which can significantly optimize the dynamic compression and fracture test of propellant charge and shorten the research cycle.

articleTitle: Intelligent diagnosis for bearing fault using dynamic ensemble extreme learning machine
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Extreme Learning Machine (ELM), as a model with simple structure, fast calculation speed, and great generalization performance, can be combined with ensemble learning algorithms in classification tasks to further improve its comprehensive performance. The calculation cost of the original AdaBoost ensemble algorithm is too high to stretch the advantage of ELM on speed. Therefore, the Dynamic Ensemble Extreme Learning Machine (DE<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>LM) is proposed for bearing fault intelligent diagnosis in this paper. In addition, the autocorrelation transform is used to preprocess the signals to highlight the fault features. Autocorrelation Constrained ELM (ACELM) is developed and embedded in DE<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>LM as the base classifier. Compared with the original AdaBoost, the proposed method dynamically obtains the training dataset for each training round and re-weights them. Therefore, some more distinguishing and continuously improved base classifiers can be obtained to integrate into a stronger classifier, that considers both the diagnosis speed and accuracy. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively reduce the training time and accelerate the convergence process of the model in comparison with AdaBoost.M2, and meanwhile, it can improve the identification accuracy of the faulty samples and reduce the training time compared with the constrained ELM.

articleTitle: Analysis and tests of magnetorheological adaptive shock mitigation systems
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Minimizing the impact load transmitted to the sensitive structures or human bodies is one of the major areas of interest within the field of shock absorption. The key to the adaptive shock mitigation systems based on magnetorheological energy absorbers (MREAs) to minimize the impact load is to make full use of the MREA piston stroke to achieve the control goal of “softlanding”. The essence would be the accurate description of the nonlinear hysteresis force of MREAs. In this work, with the mentioned objectives, a shock mitigation control algorithm for MREA-based drop-induced shock mitigation system is theoretically and experimentally studied. Dynamic responses of the MREA under the drop-induced shock excitation are analyzed and tested to evaluate the control strategies and nonlinear models of the MREA.

articleTitle: High-speed collision dynamics of the tethered space net robot and parameter analysis to the collision disturbance
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Tethered Space Net Robot (TSNR) is one of the efficient technologies in Active Debris Removal, it can maneuver in orbit automatically and capture multiple space debris continuously. However, the steady increase of the space debris greatly increases the collision risk of the TSNR in orbit. If threads of the net are broken by high-speed debris, the DOF of the TSNR will change and the maneuver of the TSNR will also be unstable. Moreover, TSNR is a classic underactuated system, the complex collision disturbance during the collision will increase more difficulty in controller design. Based on the improved net collision model, the collision dynamics of the TSNR with high-speed debris is studied, and a series of collision cases are designed to investigate the influence of the following three parameters, the collision position of the net, the size and mass of debris on collision disturbance. Results show that: TSNR is affected by several impulsive collision disturbances, which cause the rebound of the TSNR and the breakage of the local threads. The collision position of the net has a significant impact on the collision disturbance, and can be divided into three sensitive areas, central area, edge area and corner area, under the structure of the net and simulation results. The influence of both the size and the mass of the space debris on collision disturbance are piecewise and non-linear. This paper provides references for the structure design and dynamic control of the TSNR.

articleTitle: Active lateral vibration control in a shaft-plate coupled system with power flow analysis
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Power flow analysis is recognized as a powerful tool for controlling vibrations since the magnitudes and directions of power flow inside a system are directly associated with the vibration intensity. In a shafting system, the bearings are important paths for the lateral vibration of the shaft transmitting to the hull structure and induces underwater sound. In order to lower the radiated sound, a proof-mass actuator is utilized to suppress the lateral vibration transmission. A dynamic model of a shaftplate coupled system is established using the wave propagation method. Power flow analysis is performed to exhibit the power flow characteristics and distinguish the dominant path for the vibration power transmitting from the shaft to the plate. The feasibility of the active control with the proof-mass actuator is numerically evaluated. The results indicate that the reduction of the power injected into the system leads to the decrease of the plate vibration, and the power flow directions in the shaft-plate coupled system are changed as well.

articleTitle: Fatigue life estimation of purchase cable based on rain-flow counting method and K-means theory
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The purchase cable transfers the kinetic energy of aircraft to arresting gear in landing process, which can realize the short- distance deceleration and stopping of aircraft. Purchase cable is in a complex stress condition in the working process, especially at the joint root. Therefore, the fracture of the steel wire due to fatigue at the root of joint is of the main failure mode for purchase cable. In this paper, the rain-flow counting method and the K-means clustering theory are used to extract cyclic stress load spectrum under different working conditions based on the tension data of purchase cable joint in arresting test. Finally, the fatigue life calculation is carried out by using Palmgren-Miner linear damage accumulation theory. The predicted lifetime of purchase cable obtained under different working conditions is in a good agreement with the actual service life of purchase cable. In conclusion, it is clearly shown that the above two prediction methods can estimate the service life of purchase cable with high accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on energy capture characteristics based on acoustic hole curved beam structure
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Acoustic black hole(ABH) structure design is a new bending wave control technology. ABH can restrain the bending wave inside the structure near the edge of the structure, thus forming a local high energy density area, which provides favorable conditions for energy recovery. A large number of studies have confirmed that one-dimensional ABH straight beam has excellent energy recovery potential, but only a few attention is paied in energy capture of various ABH curved beam structures which is widely used in aerospace field . In this paper, firstly, the vibration behaviour of a curved beam embedded in an acoustic black hole structure is analyzed and the local energy accumulation characteristics of the structure are verified. Then, a semi-analytical model of coupling between piezoelectric layer and girder structure is established and its validity is verified by numerical analysis. The influences of curvature, truncation thickness and load resistance on energy capture efficiency are discussed, which provides valuable reference for the design of energy recovery device based on ABH curved beam structure.

articleTitle: Active vibration control of structure in time-varying ambient temperature using adaptive gain regulator
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Macro fiber composite (MFC) has been widely investigated in the active vibration control. Yet, the actuation performance of MFC is a function of temperature. For the active vibration control system using MFC based on the linear piezoelectric equation, if the actuation parameters of MFC are variable, it is easy to cause insufficient control force or control spillover, which degrades the performance of control system. Therefore, an adaptive gain adjustment approach for the active vibration control system is developed, which ensures that the active control system can maintain the expected performance of vibration suppression under the time-varying ambient temperatures. The variation of actuation performance of MFC with temperature is measured by the experiment. The polynomial fitting method is utilized to obtain the functional relationship between the regulator parameters and ambient temperature. The performance of the proposed adaptive gain regulator is verified by the experiment in the temperature environment chamber. In the experiment, a scaled vertical tail model attaching the MFC actuator is as an example, and the fractional order positive position feedback control system is as a representative of the control system without temperature adaptability. When the temperature is −60°C, compared with the control system without regulator, the reduction ratio of response RMS of the control system with adaptive gain regulator is increased by 17.26%.The results indicate that the proposed adaptive gain regulator can avoid the adverse influence of the time.varying ambient temperature on the performance of the control system.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a MEMS inertial switch with the time delay characteristic
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: A novel MEMS inertial switch with the time delay characteristic was proposed, which can distinguish between two typical impact loads in SAD (15000 g - 0.3 ms and 6000 g - 1 ms) by friction between the movable parts. The switch is composed of an outer mass-spring served as a movable electrode, a pair of flexible electrodes, an inner mass-spring, and a pair of friction bars.
