Its dynamic response under the action of impact load is divided into three phases, and theoretical models for each phase were established by Duhamel integration. Finite element analysis was performed to verify the time delay characteristic and that it is capable of distinguishing between a typical accidental drop load and a normal launching load. Under the action of impact loads of 6000 g - 1 ms and 6000 g - 1.2 ms, the switch has a delay time of 340 μs and 402 μs, respectively, and a holding time of over 365 μs and 480 μs, respectively.

articleTitle: An efficiency spacecraft structural damage detection method based on statistical and wavelet analysis
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: An efficiency spacecraft structural damage detection method based on statistical and wavelet analysis was presented in this paper. The structural response of normal and damaged structures were analyzed via data statistics, and feasible damage diagnose indices were proposed. In actual application, firstly, full samples of spacecraft vibration test acceleration data were rapidly checked through statistical analysis, and then allowed frequency and acceleration response variation values were given through normal tolerance limit estimation. At last, wavelet analysis was applied to response data beyond the normal tolerance limit and the damage location was obtained. Experiment validation on real spacecraft had proved the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Model parameter identification of bolted structures based on credibility optimization
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The structures assembled by bolted joints may have complex nonlinear characteristics that should not be neglected, especially in aerospace applications. The Bouc-Wen model is employed to describe the bolted joint, and the parameters of which are further updated via test data. In the process of optimization, the credibility concept is introduced and the credibility evaluation method based on Theil's Inequality Coefficient is used to design the object function. The credibility of the optimized model is significantly improved. The results indicate that the Bouc-Wen model has a higher confidence level than the linear model.

articleTitle: Absolute displacement transmissibility of vibration isolator with the quasi-zero stiffness
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: A vibration isolator with quasi-zero stiffness (QZS) is proposed, which is composed of positive stiffness mechanism and negative stiffness mechanism in parallel. Considering the nonlinear stiffness and nonlinear damping, the equation of motion is derived and further solved by the average method. Subsequently, the amplitude-frequency equation relationship and the expression of absolute displacement transmissibility (ADT) are deduced. Then, the effects of nonlinear coefficient, excitation amplitude, horizontal and vertical damping on dynamic response characteristics and ADT are analyzed. The results indicate that there are many ways to reduce the peak value of ADT, such as increasing vertical and horizontal damping, reducing the nonlinear coefficient or excitation amplitude. In addition, by decreasing the nonlinear coefficient or excitation amplitude can minish initial vibration isolation frequency. The higher vertical and horizontal damping may expand the isolation frequency bandwidth. The low frequency vibration isolation performance of the vibration isolation system of the horizontal spring with decreasing stiffness is better than that with increasing stiffness. Contrasted by the equivalent linear system, the QZS isolation system possesses the advantages of smaller transmissibility peak, lower initial frequency of vibration isolation and larger isolation frequency bandwidth.

articleTitle: Research on optimization method of spacecraft stiffness based on variable section Timoshenko beam
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Thin-walled cylindrical or truncated conical structures are main load support segments in spacecrafts and rockets (including upper stages). The stiffness of these structures has to meet the requirements especially to avoid resonance with fundamental frequencies which may cause catastrophic destruction during the launch and aviation, limiting the reduction of the structure weight. Unlike cylindrical structures, the stiffness matrix of a truncated conical structure is strongly correlated to the variation of the cross section geometries. Timoshenko beam theory with variable cross section was applied to obtain an analytical solution of the stiffness matrix of a thin-walled truncated cone as a function of material and geometrical parameters. Considering a structure consisted of connecting thin-walled cylinders and truncated cones, the overall stiffness matrix was assembled by each of its sub-components and was used, together with the overall mass matrix, to calculate the fundamental frequencies rapidly. We verified the correctness of our analytical model by finite element analyses, showing a small deviation of less than 5.2%. With the preceding frequency-calculation method based on variable-cross-section Timoshenko beam theory, we proposed an optimization process by tuning geometrical parameters including thickness, height, diameters of cylindrical and truncated conical parts, aiming at minimizing the structural weight under given restrained fundamental frequencies. In a launch mission with an upper stage carrying two satellites, we applied the optimization with the particle swarm algorithm (PSO) and obtained optimal thicknesses for each sub-components. Several cases with different initial conditions showed consistent results, demonstrating the robustness of the optimization process. We believe it tends to be a potential and powerful tool for accelerating the structural prototype design of spacecrafts and rockets.

articleTitle: An improved Hamiltonian finite element method for three-dimensional nonlinear dynamics of towed system
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: An improved Hamiltonian nodal position finite element method without any coordinate transformation is developed to numerically analyse the three-dimensional nonlinear dynamics of towed system, in which the dynamic equation of towed system is derived and built in global system. The medium resistance effect is taken into consideration, the deformation of towing cable is modelled using logarithmic strain theory, the coupling force between towed system and the surrounding medium is modelled by Morison formulation. The dynamic canonical equations of towed system would be updated for each time step due to the strong nonlinearity of the flexible towing cable. A first-order Symplectic difference scheme is formulated and applied to solve the canonical equations. The Symplectic conservation and high efficiency features of the proposed method are firstly validated by the solution of a U-turn towed system dynamics, the results are compared with the ones retraced by LS-DYNA. A linear towed system experiment in air environment is reconstructed and calculated to further validate the robustness of the proposed method, in which the air resistance influence is of the essence.

articleTitle: Eigen-sensitivity analysis of a two-stage planetary transmission
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: A lateral-torsional coupling dynamics model of a two-stage planetary transmission is established based on lumped parameter method. The inherent frequency as well as vibration mode of studied planetary transmission are analysed, and the vibration mode can be classified into four categories, they are rigid body vibration mode, central component translational vibration mode, central component torsional vibration mode as well as planet gear vibration mode. In order to find out the main parameters affecting the inherent characteristics, the perturbation method is used to calculate the eigen-sensitivity of mass parameter as well as stiffness parameter on inherent frequency. The simulation results showed that the main mass parameter affecting the inherent frequency is the mass of planet gear. While as for the stiffness, the main parameters are different according to the different orders.

articleTitle: Study on contact mechanical properties of reticulated hydrophilic polymer soft materials under vertical action of cylindrical indenter
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Grid hydrophilic polymer soft materials show great potential in the field of soft robots [1]. Soft robots often need to clamp or contact objects, among which cylindrical objects are more common and representative. Therefore, it is of great significance to study the contact mechanical properties of this material under the vertical action of cylindrical indenter. Hydrogel is a typical grid hydrophilic polymer soft materials [2], therefore, this paper takes hydrogel as the research object, study on material nonlinearity of hydrogels and its contact mechanics under the vertical action of cylindrical indenter. Therefore, the uniaxial tension and compression experiments, the vertical contact test between hydrogel and cylindrical indenter, the measurement of water content and porosity of hydrogel and the compression experiment of anhydrous hydrogel are carried out. It is found that the variation curve of elastic modulus of hydrogel is like an exponential function related to strain. However, the elastic modulus of anhydrous hydrogel has no obvious change and shows brittleness in the compression test. At the same time, it is found that the traditional formula of circular head vertically pressing into the elastic half-space of solid contact mechanics is not applicable in the case of large deformation of hydrogel.

articleTitle: Research on vibration characteristics of aircraft based on MSTMM
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The vibration seriously affects the safety and stability of aircraft in flight. With the increase of slenderness ratio of aircraft, the bending stiffness and natural frequency of transverse vibration are gradually decreasing. In this paper, the aircraft dynamics model is established by using MSTMM. The aircraft body is equivalent to Euler-Bernoulli beams with variable cross sections, the rudder system is equivalent to a rigid body, and the connecting part between these is regarded as a space elastic hinge. The overall transfer equation, overall transfer matrix and characteristics equation of the aircraft are derived. The vibration characteristics of aircraft with tail axial thrust in flight are calculated. The correctness of results is verified by the finite element software and show that thrust has a great influence on the vibration characteristics of aircraft. This paper provides an effective method for calculating the vibration characteristics of aircraft.

articleTitle: Low-velocity impact response of the beam with global plastic deformation
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: This paper investigates the low-velocity impact response of the beam with global plastic deformation. A simplified theoretical model of quasi-static global plastic impact based on the dimensional analysis and quasi-static theory is presented to predict the impact response of the beam. The analytical expression of the quasi-static global plastic impact is derived from the distribution of elastoplastic stress in the cross-section of the beam. The limit of the quasi-static global plastic impact is defined and obtained according to plastic yielding at bottom of the structure. The simplified theoretical model of the quasi-static global plastic impact is verified by FE simulations of the sphere-beam impacts with different impact energies. It is shown that the simplified theoretical model provides very good approximations of the quasi-static global plastic impact.

articleTitle: Analysis of multi-impacts phenomenon between elastic-plastic sphere and elastic-plastic beam
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In this paper, the multi-impacts phenomenon between elastic-plastic beams and elastic-plastic spherical indenters is investigated by a hybrid model with high computational efficiency. The hybrid model is derived by a two-dimensional finite difference beam model and a refined Strong contact model. This refined Strong contact model has a modified contact force formula for unloading phase. The multi-impacts phenomenon is observed under different impact parameters conditions. To study the multi-impacts phenomenon occurrence mechanism, intensive simulations are obtained for different impact parameters. Two dimensionless parameters are adopted for researching: relative mass ratio and relative stiffness ratio of the beam to the indenter. Intensive simulations of low-velocity impact responses are performed for different relative mass ratio and relative stiffness ratio of the beam to the indenter. The circumstance of large mass indenter and large flexibility beam are also under consideration. These simulation data are validated by Finite element method, and the simulation date matches well with the finite element results under all parameter circumstance. The characters of the impact response and displacement response in the multi-impacts cases are studied in-depth. This numerical-analytical model is validated by the finite element method, and shows incomparable efficiency to the finite element method.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of fluid-thermal structure coupling of the hypersonic wing
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Taking a wing of the hypersonic aircraft as the research object, a fluid-thermal-solid coupling analysis of a two-dimensional flow around circular pipe model was simulated in MpCCI platform, which combining Fluent and Abaqus. The result was verified by the typical hypersonic flow around two-dimensional round tube unsteady experiment. It shows that the position of the shock wave and the density distribution of the flow field can be accurately calculated based on the k - ω SST turbulence model in the simulation of flow field outside the tube. The stagnation temperature of the tube is 378.7 K when T was 2s, and the relative error is 2.6% compared with the experiment. On that basis, the temperature and the stress distributions of the wing is simulated under the 2 seconds aerodynamic heating time at different Mach numbers. The results show that the wall temperature and Mises increased gradually with the increasing velocity, but the rising trend of temperature and Mises decreased gradually, and the maximum temperature appears near the leading edge of the wing, Mises decreased gradually along chord and span directions. The maximum deformation appears at the trailing edge of the wing and the elastic deformation of the whole structure is positively correlated with the temperature, and the deformed area is located at the wing tip.

articleTitle: Factors causing installation failure of special polyimide insulating sleeves
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The influencing factors causing fracture failure while installing a fastening device's YS20 polyimide insulating sleeve were addressed using a combination of simulations and experiments to study the influence of the friction coefficient and additional bending moments caused by installing the breaking torque. The results showed that the neck is subject to the highest stress during the breaking process of the polyimide sleeve and is prone to fracture. The insulating sleeve's breaking torques are 5.6 and 8.1 N˙m when the friction coefficients are 0.2 and 0.3, respectively, and the breaking torque shows an increasing trend when the friction coefficient is 0.2 to 0.3. The additional bending moment in the installation process can decrease the breaking torque up to 44%, therefore, additional bending moments should be avoided. The maximum wrenching torque should be controlled at ≤7.5 N˙m, and the recommended installation torque is 4.5 N˙m.

articleTitle: Vibration analysis of wedge beam with variable thickness based on energy finite element method
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The variable thickness beam structure is widely used in various engineering structures due to its superior mechanical properties. However, the problem of high-frequency vibration is also quite obvious. Energy Finite Element Analysis (EFEA) is very effective for high frequency vibration response analysis. In order to apply the energy finite element analysis to accurately predict the high-frequency vibration response of a wedge beam structure with variable thickness, in this paper, the energy flow model of wedge beam with variable thickness is established. Firstly, the governing equation of energy density of wedge beam with variable thickness is derived by geometric acoustic approximation method, and the energy finite element matrix equation of the obtained governing equation of energy density is obtained by Galerkin variational method. The energy transfer characteristics of the structure coupled with the uniform beam at the coupling boundary are studied. Based on the energy transfer coefficient, the energy transfer relationship at the coupling boundary is established, and the overall finite element equation of the coupled beam structure is further obtained. The established analysis model can be used to analyze and predict the energy density of the wedge beam structure and the structure coupled with uniform beam.

articleTitle: Investigation on precursor flow of cased telescoped ammunition coupling interior ballistic process
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The Cased Telescoped Ammunition (CTA) adopts a new launching technology, which has the advantages of short projectile feeding distance, fast launching speed, compact structure. In the process of weapon launching, due to the continuous acceleration of the projectile, the gas in front of the projectile is compressed to form a shock wave. After the shock wave exits the muzzle, it expands rapidly and forms a precursor flow. In order to study the characteristics of shock waves and the formation of precursor flow, the two-dimensional axisymmetric muzzle flow field model of a 6mm CTA bullet is established. Based on the charge characteristics of CTA, a two-stage zero-dimensional interior ballistic mathematical model is established. The zero-dimensional interior ballistic model is coupled with the muzzle flow field model by the user-defined functions (UDF) of CFD code FLUENT. The model is numerically calculated and the mesh independence is verified. The numerical results are in good agreement with the experimental results, which shows the accuracy of the model. From the numerical results, it can be found that compared with conventional ammunition, the shock wave formation process of CTA is later, and the muzzle velocity is increased by 4.2%.

articleTitle: Study on effects of the air gap on the actuation performance of a variable reluctance electromagnetic actuator
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The magnetic circuit analysis method based on analytical method and finite element method is proposed, and the influence of air gap on net actuating force and suction of the variable reluctance electromagnetic (VRE) actuator is analyzed. A single-axis prototype of VRE actuator is utilized for experimental verification. The experimental results indicate that the increase of ampere turns lead to the increase of net actuating force under the condition of unsaturation and the phenomenon of saturation can be easily observed.

articleTitle: Fluid structure interaction analysis of a two-dimensional NACA0009 hydrofoil
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Vortex induced vibration (VIV) is frequently observed in marine engineering structures, especially propeller blades, rudders, risers , etc. Under specific circumstances, the vortex shedding frequency is locked to the natural frequency of the structure, resulting in severe VIV, causing structural fatigue. This research addresses the effects of hydrofoil the trailing edge thickness on the wake dynamic with a special focus on the vortex shedding frequency, vortex-induced vibration and special lock-in phenomenon. A finite volume solid stress method was employed to simulate the solid stress. An SST k-omega turbulence model was conducted to simulate the transient flow. The vortex shedding characteristics and hydrodynamic performance of two-dimensional NACA0009 hydrofoils are studied. The frequency domain analysis of hydrodynamic parameters is implemented by fast Fourier transform.It was founded that the effect of reducing VIV and avoiding lock-in phenomenon can be achieved rapidly by adjusting the hydrofoil trailing edge thickness.

articleTitle: Study on vibration reduction performance of one-dimensional acoustic black hole with different thickness functions
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The acoustic black hole structure is used for high-frequency vibration and noise reduction of the structure. It uses the gradient change of the geometric parameters of the thin-walled structure or the material characteristic parameters to gradually reduce the propagation speed of the wave in the structure and cannot reach the boundary. Realize vibration reduction and noise reduction of elastic waves and energy recovery. As an effective method to deal with many vibration and noise reduction problems, acoustic black holes are currently being studied by many scholars as a hot topic. Most of the studies are based on the thickness variation law as a power function. However, more in-depth research has not been carried out on the acoustic black hole structure whose thickness variation law is other functions. In this paper, the finite element simulation method is mainly used to study the vibration reduction effect of the acoustic black hole structure with four function laws: the traditional quadratic power function, the trigonometric function, the exponential function and the logarithmic function, and compare the four function laws. Vibration reduction effect of one-dimensional acoustic black hole beam structure. The research and calculation results show that in the one-dimensional acoustic black hole beam structure with four function laws, the logarithmic function has a better vibration reduction effect in the low frequency range, while the power function is the best choice in the middle and high frequency range. It provides a certain reference value for the design and selection of acoustic black hole structures in different frequency bands in the future.

articleTitle: Flight dynamics analysis of dual-mass poins samara model
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Samaras are interesting tree seeds that automatically rotate around a vertical axis when they fall, and use autorotation as the main technique of lift creation. The induced autorotation is caused by asymmetrical weight distribution and asymmetrical aerodynamics, which does not require any propulsion system. In present work, we established a dual-mass point (DMP) model to theoretically analyze these interesting adaptive flight characteristics of samara. Among them, one mass point for the seed and the other for the leading edge. The DMP model provides theoretical guidance for subsequent falling experiments of samara model.

articleTitle: Mechanical characteristics analysis of corner tensioned rectangular thin membranes
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: This paper presents the calculation of the stress distribution of corner tensioned rectangular thin membrane based on the stress superposition method (SSM). By comparing with the results of finite element simulation, the theoretical results of stress distribution of tensioned membrane structure are verified. Based on SSM and free vibration calculation theory, the effects of tension boundary parameters on membrane stress distribution and models are investigated. The influence of corner tension on the mechanical characteristics is analyzed for the corner tensioned rectangular membranes with different aspect ratios. The formula for each order's fundamental frequency ratio of atmospheric to spatial environment is proposed. Conducting the dynamics experiment of a rectangular tensioned membrane, the theoretical analysis is verified by the experimental modal results.

articleTitle: Abnormal grain growth induced by cyclic heat treatment in TiAL alloy
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: TiAl alloys are light-weight structural materials developed for high-temperature applications in the field of aeronautic, aerospace, automobile etc. Single crystal or coarse grain structure is beneficial to the high-temperature performance of metallic materials. We report here a cyclic heat treatment (CHT) method to prepare large-sized grains based on abnormal grain growth (AGG) process for TiAl alloys, through which TiAl grains with a maximum length of 70mm was obtained. It was revealed that the subgrain boundary energy introduced by CHT dominates the driving force during AGG. The dynamic process of high-angle grain boundaries migration behavior of AGG was investigated by electron backscatter diffraction, which revealed that the abnormally grown grains had no orientation deviation during the CHT. We have established a kinetic model of α-phase growth. Our result is of great significance to the development of TiAl alloys, providing possibility to prepare large-sized TiAl single crystals and benefiting the design of light-weight mechanical systems. Furthermore, this CHT method is important theoretical guiding significance for the preparation of single crystals or coarse crystals from other metals or ceramic materials.

articleTitle: Dynamic simulation analysis of inertial pendulum energy converter for underwater power generation
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The inertial pendulum energy converter for underwater power generation can convert the marine kinetic energy into electrical energy which can promote the utilization of marine kinetic energy and the development of marine equipment. In recent years, this energy converter method gets more and more attention since it is no need to consider the underwater sealing which is hard to realize in the deep sea. To further clarify the energy conversation mechanism of energy converter and improve its power generation capacity, this paper establishes the electromechanical coupling dynamic model of the inertial pendulum energy converter based on Matlab. In this model, a torque balance equation was employed to describe relationship between the motion characteristics of the pendulum and the output characteristics of the DC generator. The influences of pendulum angle, pendulum length and generator load on the power generation performance are simulated and analyzed with the established model. The results show that power generation capacity of the inertial pendulum energy converter increases with the increase of the pendulum angle and pendulum length, while increases firstly and then decreases with the increase of generator load. These results provide theoretical basis for the further optimization design of the inertial pendulum energy converter.

articleTitle: Vibration characteristics analysis of the complex structure system based on the transfer matrix method for multibody system
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In order to meet the particular environment and requirements of launch, the model and vibration characteristics of a complex launch structure system need to be analyzed. In this paper, the complex structure system is regarded as a multi-rigid-flexiblebody system using the transfer matrix method for multibody systems (MSTMM). By establishing the transfer relationship between various components, the overall transfer matrix and overall transfer equation of this system are obtained, and then the natural frequencies are computed. Compared with the finite element computed results, the effectiveness of the model is verified. By putting the transient load on the bottom of a cylinder during the projectile moving, the dynamics responses of the cylinder under a single fire are yielded, which provides influential research means for dynamics model and vibration characteristic analysis of the complex structure system.

articleTitle: Simulation of dynamic compression and fracture of propellant charge in bore
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: After many years of research, the main reason of breech blow caused by propellant charge is the large scale fracture which leaded by the compression of propellant. The description of the dynamic compression and fracture process involves not only the large motion of granular system consisting of large numbers of propellant particles, but also the deformation and fracture of every propellant particle. Hence, it has become a big problem all over the world. The discrete element method is used to study the compression and fracture process of propellant charge in bore in this paper. The results show that the fragmentation degree of the propellant charge at the bottom of projectile is the highest when launching, and the mechanism of breech blow caused by propellant charge is proved.

articleTitle: Trajectory planning of a rigid-flexible manipulator for residual vibration suppression
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Residual vibration after point-to-point motion is one of the main factors affecting the working performance and service life of flexible link manipulators. In this paper, a trajectory planning method based on the transfer matrix method of multibody system (MSTMM) is proposed to suppress the residual vibration of a two-link rigid-flexible manipulator. Firstly, the dynamic model of the system is established by MSTMM. Secondly, the boundary value of the joint trajectory and the system dynamics model are used as constraints to construct an objective function, which is the average minimum value of the tip deformation of the flexible connecting rod after the point-to-point movement of the manipulator. Finally, the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is used to solve the trajectory optimization. Numerical simulation is used to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The method proposed in this paper uses MSTMM to describe the dynamic characteristics of the manipulator, which not only effectively improves the efficiency of trajectory optimization, but also provides theoretical support for the vibration suppression of the spatial multi-flexible link manipulator.

articleTitle: High temperature plastic flow of polysynthetic twinned TiAl single crystal
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Polysynthetic twinned (PST) TiAl single crystal possesses great potentials for high-temperature applications. The research on high temperature mechanical behavior and wrought process of PST TiAl single crystal have great significance for application in aeroengine blades. In this paper, PST TiAl single crystal was compressed at high temperature to study the dynamic plastic flow behavior. The strength decreased with the increase of temperature and the decrease of strain rate. The processing map of PST TiAl single crystal was calculated using dynamic material model. It is revealed that the wrought temperature of PST TiAl single crystal should be high, whereas the strain rate should be low. The hot deformation activation energy of PST TiAl single crystal was then kinetically calculated to analyse the constitutive equation, which has been verified to be reliable. These paraments and models can guide the selection of hot wrought process and the prediction of high temperature service performance for PST TiAl single crystal, thus providing database to the application of PST TiAl single crystal for designing mechanical systems.

articleTitle: Fluid-structure coupling characteristics of highly-skewed propellers in the wake of the submarine
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Highly-skewed propeller (HSP) is widely used in submarine propulsion due to its excellent noise reduction performance. However, thinner blade and larger skew makes it vulnerable to respond to the hydrodynamic loading, which may even lead to structural damage. Therefore, it is advised to analyze the hydro-elastic performance of the HSP in the wake of the submarine accurately, which is beneficial to the propulsion of the submarine as well as the performance prediction of the propeller.

articleTitle: Effect of tooth crack on mesh stiffness and vibration response of a spur gear system with clearance nonlinearity
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The mesh stiffness and vibration characteristics of a spur gear system are investigated when the crack propagates beyond the central line of the tooth. The time-varying mesh stiffness (TVMS) in the single-tooth engagement region and in the double-tooth engagement region for a spur gear with tooth crack is obtained based on the potential energy principle. A 4 DOF gear system considering the tooth backlash and the clearance of supporting system in the radial direction is established, and the effect of different crack sizes on the response of the system is studied.

articleTitle: Feasibility study on application of material point method in multiphase flow calculation
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The material point method (MPM) performs well in the field of computational solid mechanics with nonlinearity, large deformation as well as fracture and fragmentation. In order to improve the calculation ability and efficiency of the complex interface in the fluid-solid coupled problem, the MPM is extended to the numerical simulation of multiphase fluid dynamics. The MPM solution format for Euler equations with source terms is constructed in this paper, and the accuracy of which is verified by calculating a typical example with analytical solutions. Furthermore, this paper studies the complex gas-solid twophase flow dynamics process of the dust-gas shock tube by introducing two sets of material points, and analyzes the influence of different factors on the corresponding flow characteristics. The simulation results show that the dissipation effect is enhanced with the increase of particle mass concentration ratio, and the length of the relaxation also increases with the increase of particle diameter. It can be seen that it is feasible to apply the MPM to the calculation of multiphase fluid dynamics.

articleTitle: Research on the influence of geometric parameters on the natural frequency of the lattice sandwich structure
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The lattice sandwich structure has the advantages of lightweight and high specific stiffness, and the natural frequency is an important index to characterize the quality and stiffness of the structure. Therefore, studying the changing law of the natural frequency can guide the engineering design of the lattice sandwich structure to exert its excellent performance. Since the multilayer lattice sandwich structure has good designability, the natural frequency can vary by changing the relevant geometric parameters of the multilayer lattice sandwich structure. Therefore, this article carries out specific work from the above perspective. This article first takes the two-layer lattice sandwich structure sample as the object, and conducts finite element modal analysis and experimental modal analysis to verify the accuracy of the finite element model. On this basis, the finite element software is used to study the influence of panel thickness, lattice sandwich rod diameter and the number of lattice sandwich layers on the low-order natural frequencies of the multilayer lattice sandwich structure. The results show that the natural frequency of the multilayer lattice sandwich structure is variable due to the different geometric parameters. Therefore, the lattice sandwich structure can obtain higher specific stiffness and better load-bearing capacity by selecting the geometric parameters reasonably. The above will bring new ideas and inspirations for the lightweight applications of lattice sandwich structures in aerospace, weaponry, automotive industry and other related fields.

articleTitle: Vibration control of cantilever structures based on finite element method and active-passive hybrid piezoelectric network
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: As a form of passive control, electrical circuit can dissipate electrical energy. As a form of mechanical and electrical conversion device, piezoelectric material can transform mechanical energy into electrical energy, and vice-vesa. In this paper, an active-passive hybrid piezoelectric network(APPN) is employed to realize the vibration control of cantilever structures. Piezoelectric material is used to sense and control dynamic strains induced by structural vibration. The input voltage in the circuit is conceived as a function relying on the vibration velocity of the structure, playing the role of active control source. The resistance and inductance values in the circuit are carefully designated so as to maximize the dissipation of the vibration energy injected into the circuit. Passive control based on resistance-inductance circuit, active control based on voltage control, and a closed-loop control policy based on APPN are carefully investigated with a cantilever finite element model obtained by Hamilton principle. The corresponding control effects of these three methods are analyzed and compared, and simulation results have proven the superiority of this closed-loop APPN control policy over a pure passive or a pure active control policy in control efficiency and energy consumption.

articleTitle: Research on the application of instantaneous extrinsic rectification method
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The external parameter of binocular camera is one of the most important parameters in the measuring system, and its accuracy directly determines the measuring precision to a certain extent. The instantaneous extrinsic rectification method uses the spatial position relationship between the optical center of binocular camera and the projection points of objects on the left and right camera images to determine the external parameters of the measuring system of binocular camera. In the test of an armored vehicle, the instantaneous extrinsic rectification method is used to calculate the launch vibration parameters of tank and projectile, and the accuracy of the instantaneous extrinsic rectification method is proved by the simulation.

articleTitle: Research on measurement technology of sound transmission loss in variable temperature environments
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: A new experimental technique of sound transmission loss (STL) is proposed to investigate the influence of temperature on the STL characteristics of composite panels in this paper. The advantages and disadvantages of acoustic transmission loss measurement methods currently being used in aerospace are compared. Considering the practicability of engineering applications, the sound pressure method is chosen as the experimental method of this study. Based on the principle of the sound pressure experiment method, the experimental process of STL in a variable temperature environment is designed. The effect of adiabatic and humidity conditions involved in temperature control is considered, and an experimental scheme of STL is constructed. Accordingly, a mobile, temperature-controlled, and moisture-controlled reverberation simulator is designed and produced. Then, an STL experiment of a composite aircraft panel is carried out at different temperatures by using this device. The feasibility of the technology is verified and the phenomenon that the STL of the composite panel is affected by temperature is found in this experiment. The development of this technology provides a new tool for the acoustic design of composite structures in the present and future.

articleTitle: Effect of directional heat treatment on microstructure evolution for TiAl alloys
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: TiAl alloy is a new lightweight structural material developed for high-temperature applications. Acquiring directional structure with columnar crystals is an effective way to improve its service temperature. We report here a low-cost directional heat treatment (DHT) method to prepare columnar grain structure for TiAl alloy. To reveal the dynamic process of grain boundary migration during DHT, influence of heating temperature and withdraw rate on the microstructure evolution were investigated. The results showed that the columnar crystals can be acquired under heating temperature of 1250°C and 1300°C. The aspect ratio of the columnar crystals changed both with heating temperature and directional withdraw rate, and there existed an optimal withdrawal rate under which the maximum aspect ratio of columnar crystals can be obtained. This optimal withdrawal rate was found to be in accordance with the grain boundary migration velocity at specific temperature. Therefore, if the withdrawal rate was too fast or too slow, the grain boundary migration cannot match with it, under which condition only equiaxed grains can be formed. In addition, the lamellar spacing of TiAl alloys was found to be inversely proportional to the withdrawal rate, which provided the basis for controlling lamellar structure through DHT. Our results can be valuable guide for the development of high-temperature TiAl alloys, therefore benefiting the design of lightweight mechanical systems.

articleTitle: Research on the dynamic loads of the airborne missile launching system based on the ADAMS and MATLAB combined simulation model
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In this paper, using MATLAB and ADAMS software platform, a combined simulation model of airborne missile high-pressure gas launching system has been established. The model can simultaneously solve the gas dynamics process of gas combustion and its expansion in gas cylinder and the structural dynamic process of the missile launching. Calculations show that, this combined simulation method can analyse and obtain gas state parameter variations in the gas cylinder, motion parameter variations of each moving part and load transfer and deformations among the parts in the launching system. Compared with the traditional method of solving the internal and external trajectory separately and independently, this model can simulate the whole launch process more realistically, and the calculation efficiency of this model is higher. The missile motion characteristics and dynamic loads of each component obtained by simulation using this method will serve as important design basis for launching system and airframe support structures.

articleTitle: An evaluation method of explosive charge of deflagration-to-detonation transition based on shock wave overpressure
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The difficulty of deflagration-to-detonation transition (DDT) is an important index to evaluate the safety of explosives. If the DDT occurs during the production, transportation and storage of explosive, the hazard consequences are unimaginable. Previous studies lack quantitative evaluation of the damage capability of the DDT in explosives, leading to the insufficiency of accurate guidance in safety prevention and control. Shock wave overpressure is the important parameter to measure the explosive damage efficiency. To study the change rule of shock wave overpressure produced by DDT and estimate its explosive charge, this paper combines the simulation of DDT with the shock wave overpressure formula of explosives. The DDT of explosive charge is simulated by the finite element software Autoodyn, and the effects of charge diameter and excitation intensity on the peak overpressure are analyzed. By comparing with the shock wave overpressure produced by the direct initiation, the explosive charge is estimated, which provides a preliminary theoretical basis for the formulation of explosive safety protection measures.

articleTitle: Ce/Ti element content on SOFC anode conductivity at high temperatures
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: SOFC (Solid oxide fuel cell) was a device to convert chemical energy into electric energy. The low conductivity of fuel battery was the main factor of restricting its development. Looking for anode materials with high conductivity was the first thing. The paper mainly discusses the influence of Ce/Ti element samples on the anode conductivity of SOFC at different time periods at 800°C temperature. Based on 409L took as the test object, a certain amount of rare earth element Ce and stable element Ti were added to the welded joint, so that the conductivity of the sample is much greater than that of the base metal sample, so as to improve the electronic conductivity and then improve the efficiency of the battery.

articleTitle: A multibody dynamics model of rockets incorporating flexibility and control
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: A heavy-lift launch rocket faces a significant challenge that the flexible structure and the controller are coupled. The vibrations of the structure and the swing of the engine may become divergent if the controller parameters are designed unreasonably. It is an urgent task to develop a coupled model of rocket launch dynamics to verify controller parameters. This study presents a multibody model incorporating flexibility and control. The flexible structure of the rocket is discretized into rigid bodies, every two of which are linked by the massless Timoshenko beam. The controller is coupled in the system by simultaneously solving the controller's state space equation and the rocket body's dynamic equation. The multibody model can capture the coupling of the structure and control, and accurately represent the rocket launch dynamics. A high-precision result of rocket launch dynamics can be obtained in a short simulation time using a numerical integration method named backward differentiation formula. A single-stage rocket is used as an example to confirm the effectiveness of the multibody model. The multibody model is an effective tool for rocket design.

articleTitle: Review on mechanic modeling methods and applications of muscles in soft actuations
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The main function of muscles is to contract when receiving electrical signals from nerves, resulting in the movement or deformation of related bones and tissues. Muscles possess the characteristics of flexibility and high efficiency, which are suitable for distributed actuation and human-computer interaction. Recently, bionic actuators, including pneumatic actuators, cable-driven mechanisms, and shape memory alloys/polymers, have been widely used in soft robots. Fundamentally, studying the actuation mechanism of muscles and extracting a simplified model is of great significance for achieving bionic actuation. The core problem of muscle movement is to establish the relationship between length and tension of muscles. Various modeling methods have been proposed for describing mechanics of muscles including fitting methods based on experimental data and simplified theoretical models. Recently, the simulation of muscle contour comes into being with the development of image processing and animation. This paper introduces the development of modeling methods of muscle mechanics including experimental modeling methods and theoretical/simulation modeling methods. Besides, the advantages and disadvantages of these modeling methods and their applications are analysed. Therefore, it has guiding significance for the design of soft robots including pneumatic actuators, cable-driven actuators, etc.

articleTitle: Analysis of thermoelastic damping in the doubly clamped micro-beam with linearly tapered circular cross-section
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Precisely estimating the values of thermoelastic damping (TED) is a significant issue for the design of the variable crosssectional micro-beam resonators operated in vacuum. TED plays an important role in the upper limitation of quality factor (Qfactor) that is applied in estimating the micro-resonator performance. However, most of previous studies were focused on TED modeling and investigation for the uniform rectangular cross-sectional micro-beam resonators. Additionally, the classical Zener's model is not capable to compute TED values of non-uniform beams. Thereby, this work aims to derive a new TED numerical model of non-uniform circular cross-sectional micro-beam resonators. The doubly clamped boundary condition is considered in this study. Modal parameters of the linearly tapered beam with linearly varying radius are calculated by the modified Adomian Decomposition Method (MADM). The length and modal order dependences of TED are explored by the numerical simulation. Meanwhile, the results obtained from the finite element method (FEM) model are also carried out seriously for comparison. The present analyses illustrate that in the relatively high-frequency region, TED values of linearly tapered micro-beams are larger than those of uniform micro-beams, while in the relatively low-frequency region, the former is lower than the latter. Furthermore, the maximum of TED in uniform micro-beams is permanently greater than that of linearly tapered micro-beams.

articleTitle: Sound transmission loss of a micro-perforated muffler with internal spiral structure
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: With sub-millimetre perforation, a micro-perforated muffler (MPM) has a high acoustic resistance and low mass reactance. It can provide considerable noise attenuation effect in low-frequency range. The wave propagation in a coaxial micro-perforated tube muffler is deduced based on the plane wave hypothesis, and the theoretical transmission loss calculation results are compared with finite element method simulation results. Then, a new type of micro-perforated tube muffler with internal spiral structure (MPMISS) is proposed, to improve the noise attenuation effect in middle and high frequency range. The effects of pitch, length, number of lines and micro-perforation of internal spiral structure on acoustic transmission loss is analysed. The CFD is used to calculate the influence of internal spiral structure on aerodynamic characteristics of tube muffler. Although the internal spiral structure slightly increases the pressure loss, it can prevent the direct transmission of middle and high frequency noise, so as to effectively improve the noise attenuation effect in middle and high frequency range.

articleTitle: A new family of explicit integration algorithms for nonlinear railway vehicle dynamics
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In order to develop efficient algorithms for strongly nonlinear problems in railway vehicle dynamics, a new family of explicit time integration algorithms is put forward based on the past acceleration. The new method is a direct integration scheme which employs accelerations as independent variables. It is endowed with controllable numerical dissipation. The train collision problem in railway vehicle dynamics is performed to confirm the performance of the new method. The results manifest that the impact speeds of two colliding trains are symmetric to a horizontal line. The wheel rise which is close to the collision interface is greater than that of other interfaces. The wheel rise is puny at low speeds. The computational speed of the explicit integration algorithm is approximately 3.8 times of that of the Runge-Kutta method in the investigated example. The approach has high efficiency in the train collision simulation. The new method is applicable and robust in nonlinear railway vehicle systems.

articleTitle: A novel bearing fault diagnosis method based on feature fusion and convolutional neural network
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The effective fault diagnosis method is crucial for the engineering. At present, the fault diagnosis methods based on datadriven have achieved much attention. The traditional methods only utilize one sensor or one channel data. However, there are more than one sensor or channel in the data acquisition system. To take full advantage of the connection between different channels data, a bearing fault diagnosis method based on feature fusion and convolutional neural network is put forward in this paper. First, two different channels data are fused to obtain different fault features. Then, convolutional neural network is applied to classify the different faults through the fusion features. Finally, the performance of the proposed approach is verified by the drive train dynamics simulator test.

articleTitle: An algorithm for constraint stabilization of planar multibodys with closed-loop
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The Riccati transfer matrix method for multibody system (RMSTMM) with closed-loops (CLs) with advantages of high computationally efficiency has wide application prospect in multibody dynamics. The RMSTMM establishes Riccati transfer equation on the acceleration level. However, the constraint equations on the displacement and velocity level at the joint are easy to be destroyed. A general planar multibody system with CLs is used to clarify stabilization of constraints on the displacement and velocity levels. The constrained Jacobi submatrices for different type of joints are derived to correct constraints violation. Some numerical examples of the planar system using different type of joint elements are given to demonstrate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Transient analysis for nonlinear dynamics by differential quadrature discrete time transfer matrix method
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Transfer matrix method is a practical tool for dynamics computation of engineering mechanics. In this investigation, a new hybrid method is presented for transient analysis for nonlinear dynamics, and named as differential quadrature (DQ) discrete time (DT) transfer matrix method (TMM), summarized as DQDTTMM. In DQDTTMM, a mechanical system can be divided into many elements according to their natural characteristics. Control equations of the element are determined by classical procedure (such as finite element method) and usually are nonlinear Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs). The DQ method can be used to express the velocities and accelerations in the nonlinear ODEs of the element by the displacements at many sampling grid points in one-time step. The nonlinear algebraic equations can be constructed to determine the relationship between the displacements and forces of the elements. Use Newton's method and the Jacobi matrix, the nonlinear ODEs can be transformed to a set of linear algebraic equations at element level to deduce the transfer equations and transfer matrices of the nonlinear element. It is found that the implicit computational procedure for nonlinear dynamics can be implemented without the global dynamics equation and Jacobi matrix. Several numerical examples verify the DQDTTMM.

articleTitle: Optimal design of an opposite aerostatic thrust bearing considering rarefaction effect
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Aerostatic bearings have been widely used in ultra-precision machine tools. As the key component, the performance of the air bearing has a dramatic impact on the machining accuracy. Traditional static design often takes load-carrying capacity and static stiffness as optimization objectives, while the vibration of the spindle is mainly resisted by the dynamic stiffness in the actual machining process. In this paper, the air film thickness and orifice size are optimized to improve the dynamic stiffness of the aerostatic thrust bearing by using the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm-II (NSGA-II). The orifice diameters of upper and lower thrust plate are independent. As the optimal solutions tend to low air film thickness, the hypothesis of continuum flow between spindle and plate is no longer applicable. Thus, the rarefaction effect is considered by integrating a slip flow model into the Reynolds equation. It is found that the preferable parameters corresponding to static design and dynamic design are different. Compared with the conventional design with same orifice size, both static stiffness and dynamic stiffness can achieve a considerable improvement with independent orifice diameters. The research results are expected to provide suggestions for the design of opposite air thrust bearings.

articleTitle: New dynamic modelling for a ball bearing system with raceway local defect considering the impact characteristics
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Rolling bearing faults bring serious challenges to the operation safety of rotating machinery, and raceway local defects are the mostly seen type. The process of the ball passing through a local defect zone could be divided into the entry event and the exit event. The impacts caused by the local defect are usually modelled though the variation of the clearance between ball and raceway or description of the collision of a ball hitting the defect edge, these two kinds of modelling are treated separately. In this work, the impact excitation was mainly caused by the increase of the clearance between the ball and raceway for the entry event, while the impact excitation included the ball collision to the defect edge as well as the decrease of the clearance between the ball and raceway for the exit event. Then a new model considering the impact characteristics of the local defect was therefore proposed in this paper. In addition, the dynamic model of a ball bearing system with raceway local defect was built, and the fourth-order Runge-Kutta method was used to solve the equations of the dynamic model. The response obtained from simulation was then analysed in time and frequency domain to detect the characteristics such as the transient impulse caused by the local defect. These characteristics matched the basic time-frequency domain concepts of a bearing with a local defect and verified the new model. Additionally, the defect characteristic frequency obtained via the envelope analysis further verified the validity of the model.

articleTitle: Research on modes orthogonality of aero-engine tri-rotor system
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: This paper presents a dynamic model of aero-engine tri-rotor system included both common bifurcation structure and intermediate bearing for modes orthogonality analysis of tri-rotor system. The complex mode method is used to analyze the modes orthogonality of the tri-rotor system under different excitations and deduced the set of conditions for orthogonality. It is found that when the speed ratio of the tri-rotor system is constant and the damping matrix is the main symmetric matrix, the mode shapes of the tri-rotor system under the excitation of their respective frequencies are orthogonal, but there is no orthogonality between the modes from different excitations. Finally, a certain type of aero-engine tri-rotor system is selected as an example to verify the previous conclusion. The discrete finite element method is used to calculate the modes under different excitations when the speed ratio is constant or not, and the modes confidence function is used to evaluate the orthogonality of the calculated modes. The evaluation results is agree well with the previous orthogonality condition set, and it is indicates the reliability of the proposed aero-engine tri-rotor system dynamic model.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of repeated impacts on a steel beam with visco-plastic material behavior
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: This paper presents a numerical study on the dynamic behaviours of an elastic visco-plastic steel beam under repeated mass impacts, with a finite element method. The numerical approach is done through a three-dimensional finite element model and a repeated impact scenario adopted in the numerical simulation is proposed. The study comprises repeated impacts under identical initial conditions, whereby the plastic deformation and resulting residual stresses due to previous impacts are included. The impact process is described through simulations involving the local contact behaviour and structural response, to get a better understanding into the mechanism of repeated impacts. Impact parameters related to the accumulation of plastic deformation, progression of residual stress, wave propagation, and among others are presented and analyzed in detail. From the numerical results, it is found that for current impact system, the impact parameters vary monotonously with impact number, and tend to a saturation state. In addition, the effects of viscoplasticity and impact position on the repeated impact responses are discussed. It is shown that repeated impact behaviours are mainly depend on the initial impact energy, material property and impact number, and the effect of impact position on structural resistance to repeated impacts is negligible.

articleTitle: Bucking analysis of thin plate with general boundary by FSTMM
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: As an efficient technology, FSTMM abbreviated by semi-analytical Finite Strip Transfer Matrix Method has been proposed to analyze the buckling problems of rectangular thin plates with loaded edges simply supported. When loaded ends are clapped or guided or so on, we introduce general stiffness matrices to solve the coupling of buckling modes. Consider the number of buckling modes included in the analysis, general stiffness matrices are assembled accordingly, and then by the transfer matrix method, the general control equations of the strip element of the buckling plate can be rewritten as the general transfer equations. The semi-analytical finite strip transfer matrix method is extended for the buckling analysis of plates with general boundary conditions. The global stiffness matrix of the system is not required to deduce, and the system matrix order is reduced, therefore, the calculation speed is effectively improved. And modal participation of buckling deformation of rectangular thin plates can be obtained for further analysis in the structural design. Compared with Finite Element Method's results under twenty boundary conditions of thin plates, the reliability and high effectiveness of this method is proved by calculating two illustrations of the plates and the ribbed plates.

articleTitle: Study on the dispersal dynamics of terminal sensitive bullet without parachutes and wings
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: A high initial velocity, high rotation velocity, orientational and instantaneous dispersal is the prerequisite for realizing the steady-state scanning motion of the Terminal Sensitive Bullet without parachutes and wings (called TSB in present work). In order to meet this special dispersal requirement of the TSBs (who are carried by airborne dispensers), we firstly designed the inertial kinetic energy dispersal scheme and connection-unfold mechanism between the TSB and the carrier, and theoretically proved the feasibility of the scheme from the perspective of kinematics. Further through the analysis of multi-body dynamics, the relationship between the offset angle of the TSB after unfolded and the initial rotational velocity is obtained. Then, on this basis, a centrifugal unlocking separation mechanism was designed, and a dynamic model of the centrifugal unlocking mechanism was established considering the non-linear factors of friction. By numerically solving the dynamic equations, the effects of stiffness/mass ratio, contact pressure of a sleeve, angular acceleration of the cluster munition system and control parameters of the friction model on the performance of separation mechanism are analysed. And compared with the high-fidelity simulation results obtained by multi-body dynamics solver ADAMS, the reliability of the centrifugal unlocking separation mechanism was verified. The research results can provide some technical supports for the dispersal and separation designs of terminal sensitive cluster munitions.

articleTitle: Adaptive feedback control of stability in an axial flow compressor with circumferential inlet distortion
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The adaptive feedback control of stability with circumferential inlet distortion has been experimentally investigated in a lowspeed axial compressor. Three flat-baffles with different span heights are used to simulate circumferential distorted cases. Compared with auto-correlation and root-mean-square analysis, cross-correlation analysis used to predict early stall warning does not depend on the circumferential distortion position. Hence, the cross-correlation coefficient was used to monitor the stable status of the compressor when suffering from different circumferential distortions and was also selected as the feedback signal in the active control strategy. Based on the stall margin improvement of tip air injection obtained under different distorted intensities and the sensitivity analysis of cross-correlation coefficients to injected momentum ratios, tip air injection was adopted as the actuator for adaptive feedback control. The designed digital signal processing controller was applied to achieve adaptive feedback control in distorted inflow conditions. Results show that the adaptive feedback control on stability can obtain approximately identical stall margin improvement as the steady injection under different distortion intensities with a reduced injection mass flow. Thus, the proposed adaptive feedback control is ideal for the engine operation with circumferential distorted inflow, which frequently occurs in the flight.

articleTitle: A parallel fast multipole boundary element method for acoustic problems in moving flows
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The boundary element method (BEM) has emerged as a powerful computational method for acoustic problems with a quiescent medium. However, the BEM is still in its infancy for large-scale acoustic problems in moving flows. In this paper, the convected BEM based on the direct convected boundary integral equation (BIE) is developed to solve the acoustic problems in a subsonic uniform flow. The fast multipole method (FMM) is implemented to overcome the inherent flaws of the conventional BEM (CBEM). In addition, the parallel computation technique is adopted to accelerate the solution of FMBEM further by taking advantage of modern computers with multicore CPUs. The parallel scheme is implemented with the wellknown OpenMP parallelization standard. Both the parallel schemes of the CBEM and FMBEM are introduced. For the CBEM, the construction of the coefficient matrix, as well as solving process, are drastically accelerated by utilizing a simple columnwise distribution scheme. For the FMBEM, the parallel GMRES iteration including the upward and downward passes is accelerated by distributing the threads to all cells at each level. The developed parallelization scheme for the FMM does not demand much extra memory storage. To illustrate the merits of the proposed method, several numerical examples are performed to validate the accuracy and efficiency of the developed parallel convected BEM.

articleTitle: Concept design and study of a novel hybrid continuum robot for confined space intervention
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: With the long/slender body, the continuum robot is increasing used in a wide range of industrial applications, especially for the confined space intervention. However, due to its slender structure, the stiffness of the continuum robot is usually too low for performing the deep/inside operations. This paper proposes a novel hybrid robot, which is constituted by the stiffening continuum robot and 6-DoF end-effector, to improve the performance of the continuum robot. The working principle is that the continuum robot, which can change its stiffness actively, will deliver the 6-DoF end-effector to the desired inside position, then the 6-DoF end-effector will perform the high accuracy operation in a small region. To obtain the driving force of the six limbs for performing the intended task (e.g., material removal), the static model of 6-DoF manipulator and cutting force model of the material were built. Based on the developed model, the driving force variation of the six limbs that impacted by the structure configuration was studied. It was found that the structure configuration of the 6-DoF manipulator has big influence on the driving forces of the six limbs (32 %).

articleTitle: Design optimization of exit stage with diffuser passage based on NSGA-II and kriging surrogate model
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In this paper, a diffuser passage compressor design is introduced via optimization to improve the aerodynamic performance of the exit stage. An in house design optimization platform is constructed based on non dominated sorting genetic algorithm II and kriging surrogate model to perform the optimization. A pareto front is obtained through optimization, from which optimal designs are selected by comprehensively considering efficiency and stability of the exit stage. The results show that application of diffuser passage design can improve the total pressure ratio by 0.79% and efficiency by 1.56% at the design mass flow rate, and the stall margin can be improved by 6.20%. The database is analyzed to investigate how different parameters affect the performance of the exit stage. The reasons for total pressure ratio increasing of the optimized compressors are expounded by analyzing the velocity triangle. Furthermore, the loss of rotor and stator region are quantized according to the local entropy generation rate model.

articleTitle: Design and control of magnetorheological seat suspension for both shock and vibration mitigation
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In order to effectively improve the ride comfort and safety of armored vehicle seats, a magnetorheological (MR) seat suspension for both shock and vibration mitigation was designed and an effective semi-active control strategy was proposed according to the semi-active characteristics of the MR damper. Firstly, the MR suspension structure scheme of side-mounted seat was proposed. Secondly, the two-stage electromagnetic coil double rod MR damper was designed based on the damping force calculation model and magnetic circuit design principle. And the electromagnetic force coupling model of MR damper was established based on the mechanical test results. Thirdly, according to the design requirements of armored vehicle seat suspension, the overall structure of the MR suspension was designed. Finally, a 3-DOF dynamic model of the seated human and seat was established. And a semi-active control strategy for both shock and vibration mitigation was proposed based on the on-off control method and the effective stroke of the MR damper. The numerical analysis results showed that the designed MR seat suspension system has good ability of vibration reduction and shock resistance, and effectively improves the ride comfort and safety of drivers and passengers.

articleTitle: Vibration response analysis of dual-rotor system in aero-engines
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In order to study dynamic characteristics of a dual-rotor aero-engine, a similar dual-rotor system dynamic model is established. The influence of the high- and low-pressure rotor rotation speed on the vibration response of the co-rotating or counterrotating dual-rotor system in aero-engine is analyzed combine with critical speed diagram, and the vibration characteristics are experimentally verified by dual-rotor test rig system. Both the simulation and experimental results reveal that in the critical speed diagram the total amplitude of the dual-rotor system increases, when the actual speed line gets closer to a level of critical speed curve. The rotor base frequency component corresponding to the critical speed increases, mean while the other rotor base frequency component changes little. The total amplitude of the dual-rotor system decreases when the actual speed line moves away from a level of critical speed curve. The rotor base frequency component corresponding to the critical speed decreases, mean while the other rotor base frequency component changes little. The total amplitude and both of the high- and low-pressure rotor base frequency component are substantially unchanged except the dual-rotor system crosses its critical speeds, when the entire actual speed line is away from the critical speed curve. In order to avoid the dual-rotor system failure caused by an out of range response, the actual speed line shouldn't approach the critical speed curves for a long time, when carrying out a dual-rotor system rotor dynamic experiment.

articleTitle: Flapwise bending vibrations of rotating axially functionally graded variable section beams
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Free flapwise bending vibrations of rotary axially functionally graded (FG) beams with non-uniform cross-section are presented according to the Euler-Bernoulli beam theory. The dynamic equations are derived from the second-kind Lagrange's equations, in which the potential and kinetic energy functions are described by using a set of hybrid deformation variables. The modal characteristics are calculated from the dimensionless eigenvalue equation by the assumed mode approach. The accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed approach are confirmed by comparative and convergence studies. The effects of dimensionless parameters, such as the taper ratios of height and breadth,the hub radius ratio, the angular velocity, and the material gradient parameter, on mode shapes and natural frequencies of tapered rotary beams with axially varying Young's modulus and mass density are studied in detail. The numerical results presented in this work are benefit to the optimization design of rotating tapered non-homogeneous beams.

articleTitle: Buckling analysis of closed and reticular cross-section thin-walled members via finite strip-riccati transfer matrix method
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Nowadays, thin-walled components have been applied in modern engineering structures widely, of which buckling behavior is of great significant for structural research and study. In this article, Riccati transfer matrix method (Riccati TMM) for closed-loop system is introduced in semi-analytical finite strip method (SA-FSM) to analyze the buckling problem of closed-loop member. And the buckling analysis of reticular cross-section thin-walled member with closed loops is conducted by finite strip-Riccati transfer matrix method (Riccati FSTMM), which is developed based on Riccati TMM for multi-body system with closed-loops and SA-FSM. The Riccati FSTMM has a compelling advantage over SA-FSM in computational efficiency because it avoids the global stiffness matrix. In order to verify the efficiency of the proposed methods, several numerical examples with different cross-section are analysed by Riccati FSTMM and the results are compared with the ones by the computation software CUFSM. All results confirm that Riccati FSTMM for buckling analysis of closed and reticular cross-section thin-walled members is reliable and efficient.

articleTitle: Sensitivity analysis for uncertain periodically excited nonlinear systems through kriging based harmonic balance method
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: There exist various indeterministic dynamical systems in practical applications due to various uncertainties in structural geometry, material and loading. It is generally difficult to acquire a priori probabilistic characteristics of these uncertainties based on onsite data later to be used in random dynamical assessments. Therefore, non-probabilistic methods such as interval analysis are suitable for systems carrying uncertain but bounded parameters. Interval analysis method generally resorts to Taylor series expansions of intervallic parameters for estimation of lower and upper bounds of dynamical responses which are solved by perturbation finite element method (PFEM).
