Nevertheless, computational error is inevitably accumulated during temporal integration of the responses as well as evaluation of their derivatives with respect to parameters. To circumvent this drawback, an improved interval analysis approach called Kriging-surrogate-based general harmonic balance method (KGHBM) is proposed in this paper. In this method, harmonics in the Fourier expansion of the dynamical response are solved by the generalized harmonic balance method in the frequency domain. A surrogate response surface of the harmonic coefficients is established in the parameter space for evaluating the sensitivities of the response with respect to the parameters. Compared with the PFEM, the present method provides better bound predictions of uncertain nonlinear dynamical response. KGHBM can be modified with the adoption of second-order derivatives in the Taylor expansion on the Kriging surrogate model to improve the accuracy of the KGHBM predictions.

articleTitle: A hybrid Coyote-Harris Hawks Optimization Algorithm and its application on vehicle parameter identification
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid method using Coyote Optimization Algorithm (COA) and Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO), which is named COAHHO. As stochastic optimization algorithms, these two methods are sometimes easy to fall into local optimum or premature convergence. To mitigate the shortcomings, a hybrid method is presented that considers the HHO as a competitive algorithm for the COA to enhance exploration, exploitation, and the balance between them. First, a set of populations are initialized randomly. Then, those populations are divided into two halves, where the growth mode of COA is applied to the first half, and all operations of HHO are used in the second half. All the populations will take birth, death, transition strategies. Thereafter, the iterative process is continued by the best individual in the union sub-populations. The effectiveness of COAHHO is demonstrated by comparing the results with several well-known algorithms on 23 benchmark functions. The proposed algorithm is suitable for the vehicle parameter identification which objective function is multimodal and complex, and the estimated results of a 2-dof vehicle model show that the COAHHO is extraordinary in solution accuracy.

articleTitle: Study on the boundary stress distribution of elliptical cavity under uniform pressure load
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: By introducing the complex variable function and conformal transformation, the elliptical cavity expansion problem is transformed into the cylindrical cavity expansion problem. Combined with the least square fitting method and Von-Mises yield criterion, the elastic-plastic boundary of the elliptical section cavity under uniform load is determined. The cavity boundary displacement is solved by the mass conservation equation of the plastic zone, and the theoretical calculation model of the static elliptical cavity expansion is established. The results indicated that when the material reaches stability under the load of elliptical cavity boundary, the axis stress value increases gradually from the minor axis to the major axis of the elliptical cavity, showing a similar sinusoidal distribution. Due to this mechanical characteristic, it is more difficult to expand in the major axis direction than in the minor axis direction. With the increase of initial load, the range of stress on the boundary of elliptical cavity decreases, and the average stress on the boundary of cavity tends to a constant value. The majorminor axis ratio of elliptical cavity has significant influence on the stress field distribution of materials, while the initial cavity area has little influence. With the increase of the major-minor axis ratio, the stress rising rate gradually increases, and the stress value gap between major-minor axis gradually increases.

articleTitle: A nonlinear multibody dynamics model for predicting injuries of lower limbs caused by vertical impact
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In order to improve the occupant protection capability of a vehicle, numerical calculation should be carried out to obtain body responses via an accurate anthropomorphic model during the design stage. In this study, a nonlinear two-dimensional multibody model of lower limbs is developed to predict the injury response of shanks under a vertical impact load. Impact experiments for lower limbs were accomplished based on a vertical impact device and the injury response was obtained by a Hybrid III anthropomorphic test device (ATD). Based on the Error Assessment of Response Time Histories (EARTH) metric and test data, parameters of the multi-body model were optimized. Errors about the peak value and the duration of main peak between experimental and numerical results were less than 7%. This paper further analysed the influence of different impact loads on the lower leg injury. It was found that the relationship between the lower tibia force and the compression stroke of the spring which generated the impact appeared to be quadratic. With low computation cost and the ability of predicting injuries of lower limbs under impact load, the model could be applied during the development process of a vehicle considering occupant safety.

articleTitle: An intelligent optimization method of trajectory correction projectile based on design of experiments and stochastic kriging
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Performance optimization of a trajectory correction projectile, a type of precision ammunition, is difficult because of complex nonlinear flight characteristics and unique engineering constraints. To reduce the number of repeated tests and iterations, an intelligent optimization algorithm based on the design of experiments (DOE) and response surface methodology (RSM) is presented in the conceptual design of a trajectory correction projectile. Basic projectile aerobody and related design configurations are defined in the initial design stage. Based on DOE, design variables are mapped to the performance criteria to generate a stochastic kriging (SK) response surface. Also, an artificial neural network (ANN) is trained to identify unstable designs. Then, a multi-population genetic algorithm (MPGA) is used to determine the optimal projectile design. The Pareto frontier reflecting the performance tradeoff can be generated by changing its cost function. A detailed is given to illustrate the efficiency of this methodology. The configuration of a trajectory pulse-correction projectile with stabilized fins is optimized based on multiple criteria, maximizing the correction distance while minimizing energy consumption and the angle of attack. Simulations showed that the optimization method proposed could not only be applied to practical engineering problems for trajectory correction projectiles, but also portable for other smart weapons conceptual performance design.

articleTitle: Isogeometric structural topology optimization using mechanical asymmetrical materials with micromechanics constituents
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Isogeometric analysis (IGA) connects CAE with standard CAD design tools and has been utilized for a decade in structural optimization. FEA has a number of drawbacks, including a lack of linkage between analytic and geometric models, a shortage of continuity between components, and a lack of accuracy for high-order elements. Isogeometric analysis effectively overcomes these obstacles. This paper proposes the isogeometric topological optimization mathematical model depending on the asymmetric constitutive relationship of tension and compression microscopic materials. We provide a new density-based topology optimization formulation in which the design domain is limited to the B-spline space. A rectangular domain with a tensor-product is embedded in a design domain that is arbitrarily shaped. The density field is represented using B-splines. The intrinsic filter provided by the B-spline representation for topology optimization is governed by the degrees of B-spline and the knot spans. This B-spline effectively removes numerical artifacts and controls the minimum feature-length in; when the B-spline basis functions span many analysis elements. Benchmark problems in structural topology optimization are computed through Evolutionary Structural Optimization (ESO) algorithm. Comparisons of the optimal structure topologies using finite element analysis and isogeometric collocation methods are analyzed. The influence of different tension-compression stiffness ratios on the final structure topologies is listed and analyzed. The numerical results show the reliability and performance of the proposed mathematical formulation and asymmetry of natural structure.

articleTitle: Numerical study on the dynamic evolution of cavitation and pressure fluctuation in a centrifugal pump during the startup period
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: This paper investigates the evolution of cavitation and pressure fluctuation characteristics in a centrifugal pump during the startup period. The finite volume method is adopted to simulate the dynamic process. In order to characterize the acceleration characteristics, the rotation speed and flow rate are not constant, but vary with time. First, steady numerical simulation is performed on the external characteristics to verify the accuracy of the numerical procedure. Subsequently, the cavity evolution process and pressure fluctuation varying with time are analyzed in detail. Specifically, the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) method is employed in the post-process considering its advantage for non-stationary signal treatment. The results indicate that both the frequency and amplitude of pressure fluctuation increase with impeller speedup. Also, transient operation makes the average pressure at the inlet of the impeller decrease to evaporation pressure, leading to an increase in vapor volume fraction. Moreover, both impeller-tongue interaction and impeller-diffuser interaction influence the fluctuation of cavitation.

articleTitle: Dynamic modeling of rolling bearing considering local defect edge topographies
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: When the rolling elements pass through the local defect area on the surface of the bearing raceway, there is a complicated contact process, which is closely related to the edge morphology and size of the defect. However, most of the existing studies use rectangular grooves through the raceway to simulate bearing defects, and it is relatively simple to describe the contact process between the rolling elements and local defects, without considering the influence of the edge morphology of the local defects. Therefore, taking the bearing outer ring fault as the research object, firstly, the displacement excitation and impact force action point change when the rolling elements contact with different defect forms are analyzed in detail. Then, based on the time-varying excitation function, a fault excitation function considering the influence of the local defect edge is proposed. Based on the above excitation function, a local fault dynamic model of the outer ring of the deep groove ball bearing is established, and the accuracy of the model established in this paper is verified by the measured signal. Finally, the influence of fault edge morphology on bearing vibration characteristics is analyzed and studied by using the dynamic model, so as to guide the condition evaluation of rolling bearing in practical application.

articleTitle: Enhancing ductility of martensitic steels through cryogenic treatment
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Reversed austenite is effective in enhancing ductility and toughness of low carbon martensitic steels. Despite much research into acquiring reversed austenite through inter-critical tempering, there remains little knowledge of the effect of an additional cryogenic treatment before tempering on the formation of reversed austenite and mechanical properties. The present study investigated the comparison between a cast 0.13C-11Cr-5Ni-5Mo (wt. %) steel under direct quench-temper treatment and that with an additional cryogenic treatment. Results show that cryogenic treatment causes the formation of fine M23C6 carbides which act as nucleation sites for reversed austenite. The amount of reversed austenite is substantially increased after tempering at around 600 °C. Moreover, the reversed austenite turns out to be thin strips instead of commonly observed coarse blocks. As a result, cryogenic treatment improves ductility and strain hardening ability without sacrifice in strength. Our results enhance the understanding of reversed austenite formation under the influence of cryogenic treatment, and provide a guide for the design of heat treatment procedures of low carbon martensitic steels.

articleTitle: Contact mechanical behaviour and model of hydrogel soft structure
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Hydrogel is a soft material with nonlinear and complex contact mechanical behaviour. At present, Hertz contact theory [1] being suitable for small-deformation elastic bodies is controversial in the calculation of the hydrogel contact problem. There are relatively few theoretical analysis methods for the large-deformation contact problem of soft materials. The aim of this paper is to propose an incremental contact model to calculate the contact force when the hydrogel undergoes large deformation. This paper compares the numerical calculation results and the Hertz theoretical calculation results in the large deformation of the hydrogel. The result shows that the Hertz contact theory cannot be directly applied to the calculation of the large deformation contact of the hydrogel. An incremental contact model based on hertz contact formula [2] is proposed in this paper. Through uniaxial compression numerical experiments and spherical compression numerical experiments, the elastic modulus parameters and spherical virtual radius parameters in the incremental contact model are obtained. The results of the incremental contact model are compared with the numerical calculation results, which proves that the incremental contact model can calculate the large deformation contact behaviour of the hydrogel well. At the same time, the results show that the incremental contact model is compatible with different indenter radius and different hydrogel materials.

articleTitle: The installation of a subsea production tree based on a variable-length cable finite element model
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The current paper applies a variable-length cable FEM based on the absolute nodal coordinate formulation with the arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian description to simulate the installation process of a subsea production tree (SPT). The material coordinate is employed together with the global position and position gradients as the state variable. In addition, the movingmesh technology is applied to simulate the deployment of the cable. Two types of elements, including the constant-length and variable-length elements, are defined based on the variation of the material coordinates of the elements. Firstly, the equations of motion of the variable-length cable subjected to the complex environmental loads are derived based on the generalized D'Alembert principle. Second, the obtained differential-algebraic equations are numerically solved by the Backward Euler scheme and a Newton-Raphson iteration solver. Third, the implemented model is validated for both the static and dynamic simulation by comparing the results of the commercial software ProteusDS. Finally, a detailed parametric study is conducted to investigate the deployment behaviour of the subsea production tree under complex environmental loads.

articleTitle: The application and development of container launching technology in rocket launcher
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: With the advent of the era of information war, rocket weapons bear the important mission of army long-range precision attack, is the main means of artillery to carry out rapid and fierce fire attack. Based on the development history of rocket launcher, this paper describes the birth and development of container launching. This paper discusses the application and development of the container launching technology in rocket launcher from the aspects of the characteristics of storage, transportation and launcher technology, the development trend of the rocket launcher platform and the container launching technology.

articleTitle: Equivalent dynamic modeling of functionally graded porous sandwich plates in thermal environment
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Functionally graded porous (FGP) sandwich structures offer unique potential in aircraft, aerospace, flexible electronics, biomedical areas and so on. Understanding the mechanical behaviors of these structures is essential for their successful applications. In this work, free vibration of FGP sandwich plates in thermal environment is theoretically investigated. The gradation is achieved by changing the porosity through the plate thickness, rather than using functionally graded materials (FGMs). Several types of FGP sandwich plates are taken into account. An equivalent single layer (ESL) theory is developed to investigate the natural frequencies and mode shapes of simply supported FGP sandwich plates. The present theory is validated by comparing calculated results with those from the existing literature. Parametric studies are conducted to demonstrate the influences of different porosity distributions, geometric parameters and temperature on the vibration behavior of FGP sandwich plates. This work can provide theoretical reference for design and optimization of FGP sandwich structures.

articleTitle: Stress analysis and structure optimization of mems gyroscope
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The output signal of high-performance MEMS gyroscope is seriously affected by PCB stress. A PCB thermal stress simulation model containing a MEMS gyroscope is established in COMSOL Multiphysics software. The stress distribution of the gyroscope's mounting surface is analyzed. A U-shaped low-stress PCB structure is proposed, and the stress and strain distribution of the PCB are analyzed. The simulation results show that the stress on the gyroscope mechanical mounting surface is reduced from 8.499 MPa to 0.708MPa, which is reduced by 91.7%. The zero-bias stability of the MEMS gyroscope is measured before and after the improvement. The results show that the improved PCB structure can effectively release the stress, and the bias stability of the MEMS gyroscope is improved from 23.64 °/h to 11.31 °/h.

articleTitle: Free vibrarion characteristics of a ship's power-transmission-propulsion system based on MSTMM
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The power-transmission-propulsion system is the core moving component of a ship. In many cases, its vibration is a serious problem, which destroys the stability of the shafting operation and weakens the concealment of the ship. Free vibration characteristics analysis is the basis to investigate the dynamic characteristics of the ship's power-transmission-propulsion system. When the exciting force frequency of the propeller or engine is close to the natural vibration frequency of the systems, resonance will occur and cause catastrophic damage. MSTMM is an unusual modelling strategy for linear multi-body dynamics systems. However, it can deal with large-scale complex rigid-flexible coupling systems but also take into account computational efficiency. Due to the above advantages, the present paper used the automatic derivation theorem to establish the dynamic model, topology, overall transfer equation and characteristic equation for the typical ship power-transmissionpropulsion systems based on MSTMM and ML-MSTMM, respectively. The dynamic model is quite simplified in that the transmission shaft's rotation and the hull's added mass are not considered. The SVs at the boundary contains displacement, angle, moments and forces. The transfer matrices of a plane elastic hinge connecting two plane vibrating rigid bodies are derived. This paper solved the vibration characteristics by the recursive eigenvalue search algorithm. The correctness of the results obtained by MSTMM and ML-MSTMM is verified by comparison with each other.

articleTitle: Simulation of the convective drying for wet polymer materials
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: A large amount of moisture exists in natural polymer materials, which need to be removed by hot air convective drying to ensure the product quality is always superior during long-term storage. In this respect, the present work treats the stack consist of wet polymer grains as a porous fixed bed and investigates the local convective heat transfer between the hot air and the polymer material by adopting a non-equilibrium method. A single drying kinetics equation related to the temperature and the relative humidity is used to evaluate the moisture loss from wet polymer materials. The transient characteristics of the convective drying are captured by using the popular computational fluid dynamics software ANSYS Fluent as the calculation platform for numerical simulation. The hot air absorbs moisture as it flows across the fixed bed, which results in drying or dehydration. The temperature of the polymer material rises as time goes on, while the moisture content inside these grains is reducing gradually. Moreover, the simulation results indicate that the developed drying dynamics model can predict the mass loss from the wet polymer material inside a porous fixed bed and capture the convective heat transfer between the hot air and the polymer material.

articleTitle: Study on the mechanical response of high explosives during deflagration-to-detonation transition
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The deflagration-to-detonation transition (DDT) of high explosives is characterized by highly transient, strongly discontinuous and unsteady. There are always microcracks, micropores and other damages in the actual explosive charge, but the stressstrain constitutive relationship of explosives is neglected in previous researches. In order to study the mechanical response of high explosives during the DDT, this paper combines the viscose-statistical crack mechanics (Visco-SCRAM) model considering plasticity with the gas-solid two-phase flow equations governing the DDT. The space-time conservation element and solution element (CE/SE) method is applied to simulate the DDT of a typical high explosive, and the mechanical parameters such as deviatoric stress and equivalent plastic strain in this process are obtained. By comparing with the reported studies, the feasibility of the coupled method established in this paper is verified, which provides a preliminary calculation means for studying the influence of explosive charge damages on the mechanism of DDT.

articleTitle: Research on bench control technology for performance test of high-power plant
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: To meet the demand of precisely uploading for the performance test of the high-power plant, a bench control frame of the power-test system specially for the high-power plant was proposed. The simulation model of the power-test system including a large-scale dynamic asynchronous motor was developed. The control parameters of the speed feedback control loop in the vector control of the asynchronous motor were optimized based on genetic algorithm off-line. The co-simulation of high-power plant and power-test system was carried out, and the simulation results indicated that the dynamic response of the output torque of the asynchronous motor could meet the dynamic variations of the high-power plant.

articleTitle: Locomotion planning method for spherical multilegged robots using virtual dynamics
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: As a type of mobile robots, the spherical multilegged robot can adapt to complex and diverse terrain environments due to its excellent deformability and high structural symmetry. However, it is still unclear how and when shape changes are supposed to occur, and the current locomotion planning methods for such robots rely heavily on reverse kinematic and elaborate manual intervention. This article proposes a new locomotion planning method for spherical multilegged robots using an artificial dynamic model. Taking into account the centripetal force and slippage between the leg and the ground, this method has a higher trajectory tracking accuracy than the existing locomotion planning methods. This paper details the underlying of this approach and builds a 32-legged spherical multi-legged robot model for dynamics simulation experiments through MSC ADAMS (Automated Dynamic Analysis of Mechanical Systems). Experimental results show that this locomotion planning method can generate a feasible shape changing scheme for the spherical multilegged robot to follow a given trajectory.

articleTitle: Reduced multibody system transfer matrix method for closed-loop systems
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The multibody system transfer matrix method is a rather novel multibody system dynamics method developed in recent 30 years, which has gained great attention and been used widely to solve about 150 kinds of various engineering problems with some advantages over classical dynamics methods, such as low matrix order, high computational speed, and high programmability. To further improve the computational stability of multibody system transfer matrix method for closed-loops, a reduced multibody system transfer matrix method for closed-loops is presented using element transfer matrices by defining a new reduced transformation. As a result, the truncation and accumulation errors are reduced and the computational stability is improved compared with the original version of multibody system transfer matrix method. Further, the Baumgarte stabilization method is introduced to stable the constraint violation during integration process. Applications to some closedloop examples verify the applicability and availability of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Analysis on affecting factors of the fragmentation degree of propellant charge
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: It has been demonstrated in theory and experiments that the breech blow caused by the propellant charge is almost due to the propellant charge fracture. This paper discusses and analyses the effects of temperatures (-40°C, 15°C, 50°C) and packing patterns (random, horizontals and verticals) on fragmentation degree of propellant charge under the given impacting load condition, through utilizing the dynamic compression and fracture test of propellant charge as well as initial dynamic vivacity of propellant charge. The test results reveals that the propellant charge at -40°C has a largest fragmentation degree than other temperatures. Moreover, the fragmentation degree of the propellant charge packed vertically is also larger than horizontal and random packing patterns. The fragmentation degrees of various random packing have no significant differences. This test of launch safety of propellant charge can be repeated easily, which is verified scientific.

articleTitle: A simplified analytical model of equipment-pipe-shell structure
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In addition to being directly connected to the base, the mechanical equipment in the ship is often connected to the shell through attachment elements such as pipelines. There are multiple vibration transmission paths in the system, and there is still a lack of in-depth theoretical research on this type of system. To study the vibration transmission characteristics of the system, a simplified analytical model of equipment-pipe-shell structure is proposed. The equipment and shell are approximated by rigid bodies, and the pipe is represented by an elastic cylindrical shell. In addition to the pipe, the equipment is also connected to the shell through several vibration isolators. Travelling wave solution is used to express pipe response, and the forces on the equipment and the shell can be obtained through the continuity condition at both ends of the pipe and the internal forcedisplacement relationship. By solving the system dynamic equation, the response of any point in the system can be obtained. The comparison of the analytical model calculation results and finite element simulation results verifies the accuracy of this analytical model.

articleTitle: Estimate of chaotic threshold of tristable vibration energy harvesters
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Tristable vibration energy harvesters own excellent energy harvesting performance, which has been verified theoretically and experimentally. Obviously, the response mechanism of an asymmetric tristable vibration energy harvester is more complex than a symmetric bi-stable vibration energy harvester. The ambient vibrations have a great impact on the harvester. Due to the complexities and the lack of analytical solutions, the streamlined design methodologies are inhibited. To facilitate future innovation and research on asymmetric tristable vibration energy harvester, this paper uses Melnikov function and modified Lindstedt-Poincaré method are adopted to study the asymmetric tristable vibration energy harvester which has higher order nonlinear terms in the dynamic equation. Analytical results are consistent with numerical simulation results. The paper uses chaotic dynamical theory to provide a simplified analytical framework for which the deeper insight into the performance of the tristable vibration energy harvester can be obtained.

articleTitle: Analysis of flow field characteristics around the storage and transportation launch case
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In order to deeply analyze the flow field characteristics around the storage and transportation launch box of air drop rocket. In this paper, hot wire anemometer is used to measure the flow field of small gap spacing ratio and equidistant array cylinders with Reynolds numbers of 89833, 196510 and 278483. Then the influence of attack angle on the aerodynamic characteristics of cylinder groups is analyzed by numerical simulation. Through this study, the effects of Reynolds number on the position of free shear layer on both sides of the cylinder group and the velocity distribution behind the cylinder group are obtained. The variation laws of lift coefficient and drag coefficient of cylinder group are clarified.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of high-temperature, high-pressure, and high-speed propellant gas flow eroding barrel material
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The lifespan of an artillery piece highly depends on the erosion of the barrel caused by high-temperature, high-pressure, and high-speed gas flow scouring. The intense mass and heat transfer between the gas and barrel are confirmed as important factors of barrel erosion. Based on this phenomenon, a sectional thermochemical melting model of erosion is established. The erosion of the barrel during the internal ballistic process is computed with a numerical simulation method. The results reveal that the chamber throat is the most severe erosion zone, and corners are more severely eroded than nearby locations, such as the beginning of the rifling. The barrel's erosion is relatively serious around the maximum-pressure position (the axial location of the projectile when the gas reaches maximum pressure). Furthermore, because erosion is temperature sensitive, erosion rises and range widens gradually each shot under the initial temperature of the inner surface increasing in continuous shooting. The numerical simulation contributes to the prediction of artillery lifespan and other associated problems by providing a method for erosion by gas flow scouring.

articleTitle: Quantification and propagation of uncertainty in critical speeds and mode shapes of rotating structures
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Parametric uncertainties are ubiquitous in engineering structures in a variety of forms. Specifically, the most significant sources of uncertainties in rotating structures include the manufacture errors, assemble tolerance, boundary conditions and geometrical properties of critical components. The uncertain parameters have irreducible influences on inherent modal properties of the rotating systems. It is required to consider the variabilities of uncertainties for a robust evaluation of natural characteristics. This paper employed a polynomial surrogate method to track the propagation of parametric uncertainties in an overhung rotating structure. The method is non-probabilistic in nature, which alleviates the hash requirement of strict probabilistic density functions that could be difficult to obtain for real applications. The critical speeds and mode shapes of the rotor-bearing system were investigated based on the surrogate model considering different uncertain parameters. The results were validated with the crude scanning method. It was demonstrated that the surrogate method used has superiority in computation efficiency over traditional methods while maintaining enough accuracy, which will be beneficial for large-scale engineering structures. Moreover, the analysis procedure is adaptable to other uncertain structures with little change.

articleTitle: Nonlinear dynamics and stability of the supercritical tail rotor drive shaft with dry friction damper
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Due to its high power-weight ratio and low maintenance cost, the supercritical tail rotor drive shaft has attracted more and more attention in helicopter design. The dry friction damper is specifically designed to suppress the excessive vibration of the supercritical shaft when passing through the critical speed. The stability of the shaft/damper system and the vibration damping efficiency are affected by the nonlinear rub-impact process between the shaft and the damper. In order to reveal the damping mechanism and the stability of the shaft/damper system, and to guide the design of the damper, a nonlinear dynamic model of the system is established. Typical responses for systems with different rub-impact stiffness, clearance, rub-impact friction coefficients and critical dry friction forces are obtained by numerically solving the nonlinear governing Equations. The dynamic characteristics and stability of the system are investigated by drawing the bifurcation diagrams, whirling orbits and time history diagrams. It is demonstrated that there exists three forms of rub-impact between the shaft and the friction damper, namely, the forward full annular rub-impact, forward local annular rub-impact and backward local annular rub-impact. The unstable backward full annular rub-impact is not present. With an increasing critical dry friction force and rub-impact friction coefficient, the rub-impact system will easily evolve into the backward local annular rub-impact region which decreases the system's stability. A decreasing clearance or an increasing rub-impact stiffness will induce a similar effect, but the influence of rub-impact friction coefficient and critical dry friction force is more obvious. Moreover, the effects of these four device parameters on the transcritical vibration amplitude are also derived, which will give a useful guidance for the design of the dry friction damper.

articleTitle: Coupled vibrational behaviour of CNT reinforced beams with inertial, stiffness and damping adornments
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs), a nanotube formed by rolling graphene, has distinctive mechanical, electrical and physical properties that have attracted a great deal of attention over recent years. This has led to the creation of a range of mechanical, electronic and biomechanical devices with carbon nanotubes as the main component. It has also been found that the mechanical properties of different materials can be improved by introducing CNTs as a reinforcement. A considerable amount of work has been undertaken to understand the effect of CNT reinforcements on strengthening different structures. Thus, the current study focuses on furthering the understanding of dynamics of a Euler-Bernoulli clamped-clamped CNT reinforced beam with mass imperfections connected by a spring and damper. The beam is reinforced in the thickness direction with uniformly distributed (UD) and functionally graded (FG) patterns. Using the rule of mixture to estimate the material properties and the Hamilton principle, the equations of motion of the system are developed and solved. The effect of altering the spring stiffness, damping coefficient and mass imperfections on the natural frequencies of the system are investigated in this paper.

articleTitle: Trajectory optimization for the geostationary-transfer-orbit launch vehicles via improved interior-point method
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In this paper, an improved interior-point method (IPM) solving the online trajectory planning problem for the geostationary transfer orbit (GTO) launch vehicles is presented. As for the GTO launch missions, the position of orbital injection are strictly constrained. In this paper, in order to achieve both the high efficiency of online computation and high precision of orbital injection, a convex algorithm is applied to solve the online trajectory optimization problem. Firstly, according to the dynamical model of launch vehicles and constraints, the original trajectory optimization problem of the launch vehicle is formulated completely as an optimal control one. In order to transform this optimal control problem into a convex one, Gauss pseudospectral discretization method and several convexification techniques are used. This problem is solved by improved interior-point method rapidly and accurately. Finally, simulation results show good accuracy and effectiveness performance of the presented algorithm.

articleTitle: Calculation and analysis of vibration characteristics of IMU isolation system with MRE isolators
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: To improve the dynamical test accuracy of an inertial measurement unit (IMU), the magnetorheological elastomer (MRE) isolators were applied to suppress its vibration. In this paper, the dynamics model of a laser gyro strapdown IMU was developed based on the Riccati transfer matrix method for multibody systems. Combining with different control algorithms, the acceleration of the IMU shell was taken as the control object and the vibration characteristics of system was calculated and analysed. By comparing the root mean square values of the IMU components, it predicts that the effect of vibration reduction by adding control is better than that by passive control. Moreover, different control methods are suitable for different excitations.

articleTitle: Finite element simulation on the band engraving process of a large caliber howitzer under different loading positions and rifling structures
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The band engraving process is a part of the interior ballistic process that cannot be ignored, and has an important impact on the projectile motion in bore. Due to limitations in previous studies which adopted numerical simulation methods based on the classic interior ballistic theory, that is, the band engraving process is ignored, this paper establishes the finite element model of the barrel, projectile and rotating band of a large caliber howitzer by using ABAQUS software. Through ABAQUS / Explicit solver, the dynamic response of the projectile and band in the engraving process is calculated. Changing the loading position and rifling structure, the stress and deformation of the band in different working conditions are obtained, and the influence of different loading positions and rifling structures on the engraving process of the band is analyzed. It is hoped that the research in this article can provide a certain reference for studies on interior ballistics and provide a necessary foundation for further research on the interaction between projectiles and barrels.

articleTitle: A continuous time-varying feedback control of automatic magazine system with disturbance compensation
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Aiming to deal with the poor positioning performance problem of the automatic magazine system, this paper proposes a continuous time-varying feedback control for automatic magazine system with disturbance compensation via utilizing finite time disturbance observer. The control gains change of the proposed control scheme depend on implicit Lyapunov function which is differentiable functions of system error variables. Integrated with backstepping control, the transient performance of the automatic magazine system can be further improved without affecting the conservativeness of the system. And the asymptotic stability of the system is rigidly proved through Lyapunov analysis. In the meanwhile, a finite time disturbance observer is used to estimate most of the lumped disturbances to avoid high gains and compensate in feed-forward channel. In addition, this proposed control scheme has the characteristics of simplicity and practicality, which are beneficial to practical applications. Finally, Simulation experiments verify that the proposed controller is an effective robust control approach for positioning control in the automatic magazine system.

articleTitle: A novel scheme design and numerical study of turbine blade trailing edge base on multi-disciplines of flow, thermal, and strength
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The comprehensive performance of turbine blades is a key factor to judge aero engines. Multi-disciplinary coupled designing methods are imperatively required, for tougher working environment of modern turbine blades. As the thinnest region of turbine blades, the trailing edge is a difficult issue in designing, due to its cooling and strength problems, even the balancing of these two contradictions. Horizontal exhausting trailing edges were applied in the 3rd-gen or 4th-gen aero engines widely. But they are hard to be adopted in the next-gen, considering their flow resistance, cooling efficiency, and structural strength weakness. Naturally, improvements by structure innovation sound urgently. Structure of radially tilted trailing edge and its derivates were proposed in this paper, for the predictable advantages of the passage vortex suppressing, the cooling area enlarging, and the forming of complementary periodical supports. Dimensionless parameters were extracted and formed the comparing benchmarks further, based on the simplifying and parameterizing of trailing edge design models. Numerical simulation methods on flow/thermal/strength were applied, for analysing and comparing between the traditional trailing edge and the novel ones. Mechanisms of multidisciplinary performance strengthen were revealed, by contour analysing of velocity, pressure, temperature, and stress. Base on the same criterion numbers, the performance improvements of the new designed scheme were calculated on detail: the total pressure loss was reduced by about 0.6%, the local cooling efficiency was increased by 1.2%, and the local sectional average stress was reduced by about 6.7%. On the one hand, these research works showed the significances of multidisciplinary methods on turbine blade designing. On the other hand, these advantages indicated the research value of the turbine blade tilted trailing edge slots, and predicted the application prospect also.

articleTitle: Effect of particle diameter on the strength properties of methane hydrate-bearing sandy sediments
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Under the different conditions of confining pressures, temperatures, and sand particle diameter ranges, the effect of particle diameter on the mechanical characteristics of methane hydrates-bearing sediments (MHBS) was conducted by the triaxial compression tests. The stress-strain curves found that all the stress-strain relationship behaved the strain softening tendency. The relationship between the failure intensity and the particle diameter of quartz sand was analyzed, and the results showed that the sediments' shear strength would increase with the rise of the particle diameter. The effects of temperature and confining pressure on the failure strength were consistent with previously published work. Moreover, the sediment strength parameters (cohesion and internal friction angle) were picked up from the Mohr circle curves and their strength envelopes. It suggested that there was no significant change in the cohesion of the sandy sediments with different particle diameter, but the impact of sand particle diameter on the angle of internal friction was great. The internal friction angle within the sediment decreases with decreasing sand grain size. The research could provide the efficient data support for the safe and economic exploitation of gas hydrates in the permafrost region.

articleTitle: Effect of temperature on nanoscale wear behavior of graphene: a molecular dynamics study
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Being a typical two-dimensional layered material, graphene has the fantastic mechanical properties at the nanoscale. However, when nanoscale components work at high velocity, the local temperature change of abrasive particles seriously affects the service life of nano-mechanical devices and the surface quality of workpieces. In this work, we construct a probe-matrix system in atomic force microscope experiment by molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Considering the influence of interfacial temperature, the friction force in the process of abrasive wear is calculated. And the effect of temperature on nanoscale wear behavior of graphene has been investigated. Molecular dynamics simulations show the friction force fluctuates with the increasing of temperature. The effect of interfacial temperature on the atomic kinetic energy significantly determine the nanoscale wear resistance. It is also found that the friction characteristics of graphene will be affected as interfacial temperature increase. The study provides new insights on nanoscale wear considering temperature effect.

articleTitle: Application and dynamics of MR damper in the secondary suspension system of high speed trains
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: With the increasing of the train speed, the dynamic performance of the train continues to deteriorate. Therefore, how to ensure the dynamic performance of trains including the ride comfort and stability is an important issue for engineers. In this paper, how to ensure the ride comfort of high speed trains is researched. The semi-active control technology of secondary lateral dampers is used to improve the ride comfort of the train. Firstly, a full-scale high speed train model is established by using the Universal Mechanism(UM) software, and the traditional LQR(Linear quadratic regulator) algorithm based on a 9 degrees of freedom(dof) model of high speed trains is used to calculate the active control force. Secondly, the magnetorheological(MR) damper model is used to track the control force through a tracking force controller designed in this paper, and then the MR damping force is fed back to the full-scale vehicle model to form a closed-loop system. Finally, the semi-active simulations is performed. The simulation and comparison results show that the semi-active control based on the LQR method can restrain the lateral vibration of the car body and improve the ride comfort of the train obviously. Although it deteriorates the running safety a little, it is still within the allowable range.

articleTitle: Research on the launch safety test of explosive charge under simulated launch environment
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Aiming at the launch safety problems of breech blow caused by the current harsh artillery launch environment, the mechanism of breech blow caused by explosive charges and the current research status of explosive charge launch safety tests are summarized. In order to consider the influence of friction on the ignition of the explosive due to the relative movement between the explosive and the shell caused by the high-speed rotation of the projectile during the launch process, the simulation of the explosive charge launch environment was carried out based on the projectile launch dynamics equations and the internal ballistic equations, and then a new device for the launch safety test of explosive charges is established to comprehensively simulate the longitudinal overload and high-speed rotation launch environment of explosive charges in the bore. The test results show that the test device can simulate the maximum rotating speed of the projectile in the bore and the stress process at the bottom of the explosive charge during the launch process, which truly reproduces the launch environment of explosive charge. The research in this paper provides a new means for the launch safety test and evaluation of explosive charges.

articleTitle: Study on vibration of stirring shaft of vacuum rake dryer
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Stirring shaft in the rotation process prone to bending fracture, in order to solve this problem, this article in view of the cycle motivation under vacuum rake dryer stirring shaft vibration response. Based on Timoshenko beam theory considering shear deformation, the dynamic model of stirring shaft of vacuum rake dryer was established. The stirring shaft under mixing conditions was vibration equation. By using differential quadrature method and numerical calculation by running MATLAB program, the vibration response of stirring shaft of vacuum rake dryer under dynamic conditions was studied. The variation law of the maximum deflection of the mixing shaft with the parameters such as shaft radius, shaft length, shaft radial force and soon is given. The results shown that the maximum deflection of the agitator shaft is mainly concentrated in the smaller shaft radius and the larger slenderness ratio of the agitator shaft. With the increase of shaft radius, the maximum deflection of stirring shaft decreases and finally approaches 0. The maximum deflection of the stirring shaft is larger when the shaft length is 7m and 7.84m , and the other length positions are smaller. The maximum deflection of the agitator shaft fluctuates obviously in the larger shaft length and a smaller range of shaft radius. When the shaft length changes in the range of 7.8m∼7.84m, the maximum deflection of the stirring shaft changes greatly, and the maximum deflection of the stirring shaft fluctuates steadily in the rest positions ,and when the shaft radius changes within 0.06m∼0.073m, the maximum deflection of the stirring shaft changes greatly. The maximum deflection of the agitator shaft was proportional to the radial force of the blade against the shaft. The results woud provide reference for determining reasonable design parameters of stirring shaft.

articleTitle: Continuous control of seven-axis collaborative manipulator based on optimized twin delayed DDPG
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of the autonomous learning control of the seven-axis collaborative manipulator, a deep reinforcement learning control method based on delayed policy update and noise of action and policy was proposed. Firstly, the manipulator simulation environment is established, including seven axis manipulator, target, and workspace. Then the simulation environment and deep reinforcement learning network interacted through state variables. Based on two sets of reward function design with different basis, the performance of the control method based on Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) was compared and analysed. The simulation experiment proves that the time-related reward function has a certain versatility in deterministic gradient (DPG). Finally, it is concluded that the control method based on TD3 has better robustness and control performance.

articleTitle: An improved ellipsoid-ellipsoid discrete element framework algorithm design and code development
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In the simulation of discrete element method, the contact detect algorithm is a key step. For the ellipsoidal element, the intersection, geometric potential, and common normal algorithms are commonly used. But there are two defects in these algorithms: low accuracy of contact geometric information and large iterations. Therefore, an ellipsoid-ellipsoid discrete element framework algorithm was designed in this paper. While improving the Cundall common plane method, the Cundall algorithm framework was followed. Taking the packing process of the ellipsoids as an example, experiment and numerical simulation were carried out. The correctness of the algorithm was verified by identifying the final position of the specific ellipsoid. And compared with the geometric potential method, results showed that the computation efficiency was increased by 15.88%, the iteration was reduced by 25.59%, the maximum contact depth was increased by 32.52%, which was more beneficial on the contact computation of ellipsoidal element.

articleTitle: Motion response analysis of FPSO with single point mooring system based on fully nonlinear method
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The mooring system of FPSO has characteristics of large curvature ratio and high deflection, and the existing hydrodynamic load calculation methods ignore some nonlinear wave factors. In this paper, the mooring system analysis was achieved by using the slender rod theory and finite element method. Based on the boundary element method, the particular auxiliary function and mixed Lagrangian-Euler method were employed to solve the simultaneous hydrodynamic force at each time step. Finally, a hull and mooring coupled motion forecast method was established by integrating the forward two methods and a self-programming code was developed. The model is verified by comparing the numerical results of a FPSO under RAO conditions with experiment data.

articleTitle: Efficiency evaluation of satellite detumbling using a brush type contactor based on flexible multibody dynamics
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Detumbling manipulation to capture a noncooperative space satellite using a brush type contactor is getting more and more attention due to its lower cost and easy implementation. It is important to evaluate the effects of various modal parameters on the detumbling efficiency, including the design of the brush contactor and the manipulation schemes. In this study, a simplified planar multibody dynamic model is established to estimate the detumbling efficiency. An analytical formula is proposed based on some assumptions from the aspect of energy. Several model parameters are considered in the formula including the brush's bending stiffness and length, the contact position and angle. Concerning the numerical strategies, the planar corotational beam element is adopted to discretize the brush contactor undergoing large displacement and large rotations while the motion of the solar panel undergoing small deformation is modelled by the floating frame of reference formulation. The contact force between the brush contactor and the solar panel is described by the Hertz contact law. The results show that the analytical formula can give a rough estimation to the reduced kinetic energy even if dumping forces are considered. It can be found that a short brush contactor with high bending stiffness can improve the detumbling efficiency. Moreover, touching the solar panel near the root of the brush contactor and maintaining a small contact angle are both efficient manipulations.

articleTitle: Identification of stiffness parameters of armoured vehicles based on adaptive genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The identification of stiffness parameters of armoured vehicles is the prerequisite and key to the accurate calculation of armoured vehicle dynamics. A linear multi-rigid-flexible body dynamics model of the armoured vehicle system is developed by using transfer matrix method of multibody system. The overall transfer equation, overall transfer matrix, and characteristics equation of the system are deduced based on the automatic deduction theorem of overall transfer equation of multibody system. Combined with an adaptive genetic algorithm, the objective function is built using the eigenfrequencies obtained from the modal test and simulation to optimize the minimum value. In comparison with the ordinary genetic algorithm, the adaptive genetic algorithm has a faster convergence speed. Numerical simulation and experimental verification show the effectiveness and accuracy of the method. The paper provides an effective method for studying the identification of stiffness parameters of armoured vehicles.

articleTitle: Analysis and research on the bearing capacity of thin-walled cabin section made of carbon fiber reinforced plastics
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The aerospace field puts forward high requirements for aircraft bearing capacity and lightweight. This paper takes a thin-walled cabin structure suitable for small aircraft as the research object, the finite element software ABAQUS is used to model and simulate the thin-walled reinforced compartment. The thin-walled compartments of composite materials (CFRP) and metal materials are modeled separately using shell cells. The mechanical properties of carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) thin-walled cabin and metal thin-walled cabin under the same loading mode are compared by using the nonlinear explicit dynamic analysis method. The results show that after the buckling of CFRP thin-walled cabin structure, the displacement support reaction curve has an upward trend, the structure enters the secondary bearing stage, the bearing capacity decreases not significantly or even increases, while the bearing capacity curve of metal thin-walled cabin decreases significantly after the buckling deformation; The mass of CFRP thin-walled cabin is 86.48% of that of aluminum alloy thin-walled cabin, but the bearing capacity increases by 194.42%.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation on crushing and breakages of particles in a sphere-chain under impact loading
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: To improve the study of dynamic mechanical response of granular materials under impact load, sphere-chain as a specific granular material, are taken as the research object. The crushing and breakages of particles in sphere-chain were numerically simulated in the frame of the ANSYS/LS-DYNA software to identify the dynamic response mechanism of granular materials with different sizes and numbers particles under impact loading. The simulated breaking process and strain changes were compared with the test results to verify the feasibility of the numerical simulation. The displacement and stress evolution law of sphere-chain under axial impact loading is analyzed. The results show that the fracture process and strain variation of the sphere-chain obtained by the numerical simulation are consistent with the test results. The fracture propagation is generated from the contact point and intersects the other contact point, And the degree of breaking is the top, bottom and middle pellet from large to small. Large compressive displacement and compressive stress appear at the contact point and its vertical axial line, while tensile displacement and tensile stress appear on the surface. The degree of breaking is positively correlated with the number of pellets and negatively correlated with the size of pellets.

articleTitle: Simulation and optimization of honeycomb sandwich panel structure under blast
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The honeycomb sandwich structure has attracted much attention with its lightweight advantages in the field of vehicle protection. To understand the anti-explosion performance of honeycomb sandwich panel structure, the effects of geometry, shape and material parameters of different sandwich panel structures were numerically studied, and the anti-explosion performance of the honeycomb sandwich structure was verified by an explosion test. Then, a multi-objective optimization design was carried out basing on the maximum back-plane deformation and the specific energy absorption of the structure mass. The results show that the thickness of the panel, the strength and relative density of the sandwich layer as so as the whole structure height, have significant effects on the anti-explosion performance of the structure. The multi-objective optimization design can well improve the comprehensive anti-explosion performance of the honeycomb sandwich plate structure in the test.

articleTitle: Yaw-roll stability analysis of road vehicles using PWA bifurcation
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The yaw stability analysis and rollover detecting are two of major objects for road vehicle safety control. This paper proposes a method of yaw-roll stability analysis of road vehicles by using the piecewise affine (PWA) bifurcation analysis method. For yaw stability analysis, the stable regions of vehicle yaw dynamics model are obtained by analysing the fixed points under varying steering angle based on the bifurcation analysis method. To estimate the variation of positions and types of all possible fixed points quantitatively, a qualified PWA approximation of lateral tire force model is established. Moreover, a modified load transfer ratio (LTR) is proposed based on lateral dynamics to detect the potential rollover. The fixed points estimation results of PWA bifurcation analysis method is evaluated by plotting the phase planes of original nonlinear yaw dynamic model under multiple varying parameters and the modified LTR is also verified by comparing with several traditional rollover indexes (RIs).

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of typical circuit systems based on the transfer matrix method
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Based on the similarity between the electric system and the mechanical system, this paper extends the transfer matrix method of multibody system, which has the advantages of low matrix order and fast computation speed in the mechanical system, to the field of circuit analysis to establish circuit equations. First, the transfer matrix of the basic circuit elements is derived; then, the transfer matrix of the element interconnection and the active branch is derived; then take the RLC circuit and the reverse amplification circuit as examples to verify the correctness of the transfer matrix derivation; finally, the transfer matrix method is compared with the current mainstream modified nodal approach, which proves that the transfer matrix method has the advantages of low matrix order and small calculation amount in constructing circuit equation.

articleTitle: Study on the generation and propagation mechanism of supersonic jet noise in pipeline
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: When the flow velocity in the pipeline reached high speed, especially the supersonic speed, the strong pipeline aerodynamic noise would be formed, which not only adversely affected the fatigue life of the pipeline structure, but also affected the hearing and comfort of people. In this paper, the pressure recovery system was constructed to simulate the flow of air in the pipeline system, and the influence of different pipeline structures on the noise characteristics was studied by combining numerical simulation and experimental research. The results showed that when the inner diameter of the pipe was equal, the supersonic flow phenomenon was obvious in the nozzle and downstream area of the nozzle, while the flow velocity in the pipe was lower than the sound velocity, which would cause strong aerodynamic noise in the nozzle and downstream area of the nozzle. When the non-equal diameter pipe was set at the inlet of the pipe, the aerodynamic noise intensity decreases with the decrease of the pipe inner diameter. Through mechanism analysis, it was found that the velocity and pressure pulsation values of the nozzle and the nozzle core region were much larger than those of other regions, forming a large gradient. At the same time, according to the results of pressure recovery test, the whole pressure recovery process was an unsteady process, regardless of equal diameter pipeline or non-equal diameter pipeline, the pulsating pressure at the monitoring point displayed a step jump transient characteristic with the change of pressure recovery time. In the pressure recovery system, there were many different loud whistlers, but the non-equal diameter pipeline compared with the equal diameter pipeline, this phenomenon was not so obvious, which was very beneficial to the noise reduction of the pipeline system. The conclusions could provide reference for reducing pipeline noise.

articleTitle: Analysis of coupled flutter mechanism of air rudder with acoustic black hole
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Flutter refers to the self-excited vibration of an elastic body with increasing amplitude under the joint action of aerodynamic force, inertial force and elastic force. When the structure is composed of multiple components, the flutter of the structure is often accompanied by the coupling of different modes, and the vibration response form of the structure will also have great uncertainty, which makes it difficult to effectively control the flutter of the structure. In this paper, the flutter mechanism of an air rudder coupled with an acoustic black hole is studied. Firstly, the bi-directional fluid-structure coupling method is used to solve the flutter of air rudder with EABH in time domain, and the vibration displacement response of the structure under different inflow velocity is obtained. Then, the theoretical calculation results of piston are compared with the time domain calculation results. It can conclude that the flutter process goes through two continuous different stages due to the mode participation of the EABH. When flutter starts to occur, it can be suppressed by increasing the appropriate flow velocity, but flutter will occur sharply when velocity increases to a certain extent.

articleTitle: Study on performance prediction of two-stage cyclone pre-filter
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The cyclone pre-filter is one of the important parts of heavy air filter, which is the key to the long maintenance cycle of the vehicle air filter. In order to study the relationship between the flow field distribution of the cyclone pre-filter and the distribution uniformity of the cyclones, and achieve the design of the high efficiency and low resistance cyclone pre-filter based on high efficiency and low resistance cyclones, the simulation method of multi-cyclones cyclone pre-filter and the performance extraction method of cyclones are obtained in this paper by the simulation analysis carried out on a cyclones cyclone pre-filter. The characteristic relationship between the structure of the prefilter and the flow field of the cyclones is also obtained by detailed flow field characteristics analysis of the prefilter and the flow field of each cyclones in the prefilter in detail. Based on this, the performance prediction method of cyclones prefilter is established and verified by experiments. The results also provide a good basis for the design and optimization of cyclones prefilter.

articleTitle: Analysis of static strength and passive safety performance of second-class on high-speed trains
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: High-speed train seats are usually designed with static load conditions and evaluated after passive safety performance, and may have problems with static strength redundancy and insufficient passive safety performance.Based on the relevant standards, this paper establishes a static load analysis model of a high-speed train second-class seat and a collision scene model with a dummy to evaluate the passive safety performance of the seat by the damage of the dummy in the key parts of the collision. The results show that there is still a lot of redundancy in the skeleton carrying capacity of the seat back, and there is significant lightweight space. Second, in the passive safety analysis, the passenger's head will collide with the seat backrest skeleton, which does not protect the seat. Because the static strength design of the structure is a prerequisite for passive safety analysis, through the improvement of back-to-back static strength, the results of the passive safety experiment will change the results of the passive safety experiment, which in turn will provide reference for the static strength design, the two affect each other, couple each other, and have the theoretical and engineering value of further establishing the parameter model applicable to joint optimization.

articleTitle: Experimental verification of the simplification method of a specific type of dual-rotor aero-engine system dynamic model
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The structure of aero-engines is complex, and the dynamic characteristics are changeable. A reasonable dimensionality simplified model is a crucial issue for studying the dynamics of aero-engines. This paper takes a specific type of aero-engine dual-rotor testbed as the research object and establishes a solid finite element model. The rotor disc, shaft, and support structure are simplified. A simplified model of the dual-rotor aero-engine system is based on the method of structural dimensionality reduction and verifies the dynamics of the dimensionality reduction model through experiments characteristics, thus verifying the effectiveness of the simplified model. An aero-engine dual-rotor system's modal shape and natural frequency are measured experimentally, and the model error is less than 11%. The first-order critical speed error of the simplified model is less than 7.7% when the first-order critical speed is measured by superharmonic resonance. The results show that the solid finite element model and structural dimension reduction methods of the dual-rotor complete machine system are accurate and effective. The verified simplified model of the dual-rotor aero-engine system provides a basis for studying dynamic characteristics.

articleTitle: Additive role of magnetite/copolymer composites on improving rheological performance and sedimentation stability of magnetorheological fluid
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Magnetite/copolymer (Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>/copolymer) composites with nano-size were fabricated by chemical oxidative polymerizaiton and adopted as an additional ingredient in micro-sized carbonyl iron particle (CIP) based magnetorheological fluid (MRF) to improve its dispersion state and rheological performance. Morphologies and magnetic properties of magnetic particles including the composite and CIP were observed by high-resolution scanning electron microscopy and vibrating sample magnetometer. Two types of CIP-based MRFs, with (Bidisperse-MRF) and without (Monodisperse-MRF) magnetite/copolymer composites additive, were prepared using silicone oil as a medium. Rheological performances of Monodisperse-MRF and Bidisperse-MRF were investigated by the steady shear test and oscillatory dynamic test under gradient magnetic field. Flow curves were found to fit the Hershel-Bulkley model well, and the dynamic yield stress and static yield stress were confirmed to follow a universal scaling equation. The sedimentation stabilities of two MRFs were further confirmed using an optical analyzer of Turbiscan. The results shown that the Bidisperse-MRF exhibited improved rheological performance and sedimentation stability, which is attributed to the Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>/copolymer composites filling the free space among the CIPs, thereby inducing stiffer chain structures and a more stable dispersion state.

articleTitle: Dynamic analysis of flexible pendulums based on modal neutral file and Riccati transfer matrix method for multibody systems
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The Modal Neutral File (MNF) is a binary file used to transfer the information of a flexible body from the finite element software to ADAMS, which contains wealthy information of flexible body. The flexible pendulums is composed of the flexible beams with large motion and small deformation and pin hinges. In this paper, the finite element information of the beam is obtained by analyzing the Modal Neutral File of the beam. The floating frame method and the modal synthesis method are used to study the flexible beam with large motion and small deformation. The Riccati transfer equations of the flexible beam with large motion and small deformation and the pin hinge moving in space are derived according to the kinematic equations and the dynamics equations. The flexible pendulums with three bodies are numerically simulated by using the transfer equations and the results are compared and verified with results of ADAMS software.

articleTitle: Dynamics modeling and vibration simulation of planetary gearbox with bearing faults
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Planetary gearbox is a complex power transmission system which contains a large number of nonlinear contact interfaces and coupled vibration transfer paths. The vibration mechanism of planetary gearbox is very complicated and it's difficult to accurately describe its running state by vibration signals. In this paper, a nonlinear multibody dynamic model of planetary gearbox is proposed. Based on the bearing's parameters, the simulated response signal of Inner ring fault is calculated and transformed into fault excitation force. Based on SIMPACK software, the vibration responses of the gearbox model with bearing fault excitation force are obtained. To verify the simulation results, vibration signals at 4 different monitoring points of an actual planetary gearbox with bearing inner ring fault are analysed. The bearing fault characteristic frequency on medium-speed shaft is detected. Finally, the vibration responses of the actual planetary gearbox and the multibody dynamic model are compared. It shows that the main frequency components of the simulated vibration response agree well with the experimental results. The dynamic model of gearbox in this paper can provide guideline for the fault diagnose of planetary gearbox.

articleTitle: A non-traditional dynamic absorber to suppress chatter during face-hobbing process of hypoid gears
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Face-hobbing is a high-efficiency method for manufacturing hypoid gears. However, chatter is highly influencing its precision and quality of gear face. Based on the structure of gear cutting machine and the dynamic characteristics of face-hobbing process, a non-traditional dynamic absorber is proposed to suppress chatter during face-hobbing process in this study. It is a variant of tuned mass damper. The parameters of non-traditional dynamic absorber are given based on the modal parameters of a specific gear cutting machine tool and compared with traditional tuned mass damper. The suppression effect of proposed non-traditional dynamic absorber is 58% better than tuned mass damper for suppressing chatter in gear cutting machine tool.

articleTitle: Surrogate based internal and external ballistic optimization design for solid launch vehicles
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: This research aims to improve the efficiency of the internal and external ballistics integrated optimization design for solid launch vehicles (SLVs).
