The solid rocket motor model and trajectory simulation are established and respectively optimized in series and in parallel. The complete set of conventional serial design process and integrated parallel design process are respectively proposed and compared. In order to effectively improve the efficiency of the optimization design for internal and external ballistics of solid launch vehicles, the sequence approximate optimization method based on the radial basis function surrogate model is proposed to reduce the calling times of the original models with high computational cost. An internal and external ballistic integrated optimization design framework is established by 3 stages: Design of Experiment stage, surrogate modeling stage and updating stage. Besides, a multi-stage adaptive sampling method is applied for surrogate model update. Finally, in comparison with the conventional serial design process, the result shows that the proposed integrated parallel design process effectively reduced the initial mass of the objective 3-stage SLV and greatly reduced the time requirement and computational cost. The research results can provide theoretical and technical support for the integrated design of SLVs and provide reference for the optimization of overall parameters.

articleTitle: Dynamics of a multi-satellite system using elastic separation mechanism
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamics of the separation deployment for a multi-satellite system using elastic ejection mechanisms. To circumvent the difficulties in dynamic modeling of the complex system, a dynamic model is established using the automatic dynamic analysis of mechanical system software. In addition, separation deployment strategies are developed to achieve the non-collision between the satellites. In consideration of the practical engineering, soft ejection mechanisms are utilized to execute the separation manuever. Finally, parametric studies are performed to evaluate the influences of system parameters on the separation and to validate the effectiveness of the proposed separation strategies.

articleTitle: Optimized design of centrifugally driven time-delay microchannels based on Kriging model
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Based on the function of local multidimensional parameters, the Kriging model and particle swarm-genetic algorithm are used to carry out the research on the optimal design of microchannels with long delay performance. The simulation model of the time-delay microchannel is established, and the simulation model is verified through experiments, and it is found that the actual time-delay time of the fluid in the microchannel is more consistent with the simulation time curve, which ensures the reliability of the sample data source of the Kriging model. The flow time of fluid in the microchannel is taken as the research object, and the finite element simulation framework is built to obtain the data of the microchannel structure parameters and the delay time under centrifugal response in batch to form the sample data. A Kriging model is established from the sample data to fit a highly nonlinear mapping function between the design variables and the optimization target, and a particle swarm-genetic algorithm is used to optimize the parameters of the linear mapping function fitted by the Kriging model. The results show that the delay time of the fluid in the microchannel driven by centrifugal force is improved by 26.9% after shape optimization.

articleTitle: Study on the sensor for testing the stress of the projectile band during engraving process
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The movement of the projectile in the bore affects the initial disturbance of the projectile, which affects the accuracy of shooting. Under the conditions of high temperature, high pressure, high speed, high acceleration and high overload, the projectile has experienced high-strength impact and high-speed friction. All this makes it difficult to measure stress of the projectile band dynamically, directly. Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is flexible, resistant to mechanical shock and highlycompatible with the environment, which make it suitable for the measure in the barrel. This paper has designed a PVDF piezoelectric pressure sensors which can be embedded directly into the projectile. The PVDF piezoelectric pressure sensors can meet the needs of experiment well because of their high sensitivity, mechanical flexibility, multi-technology compatibility, and stability and cheaper cost. The sensors were later verified with the following quasi-static experimental. Dynamic and quasi-static calibration methods were carried out for the sensor, and the final experimental data agreed with the results reasoned theoretically. The test accuracy and sensitivity of the sensors are measured and calculated theoretically. The stress of the projectile band under different thickness and engraving speed are measured by using these sensors. This study provides a technical basis for dynamic testing to obtain real-time data of the stress of the projectile band during engraving process.

articleTitle: Development on the multi-DOF micro-vibration simulation test system based on stewart
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Micro-vibration refers to the jitter response with small amplitude and high frequency caused by high-speed rotation of rotating parts on the spacecraft, stepping motion of driving mechanism of large controllable components, etc. Micro-vibration is usually ignored on most spacecraft due to smaller amplitude and higher frequency. But for the high precision spacecraft, it will seriously affect its performance such as payload pointing accuracy, stability and resolution. Therefore, simulation of the micro-vibration environment on the ground test is very important to the high resolution earth observation satellites. Disturbance sources in spacecraft are various. A kind of general micro-vibration environment simulation system is very helpful for evaluating the effect of the micro-vibration on products in the early. Therefore, this paper presents a method of multi-degree-of-freedom (multi-DOF) micro-vibration environment simulation which can generate the micro-vibration excitation as required. Firstly, the overall scheme of this system is introduced. The voice coil linear motor actuator is used as excitation source in a Stewart platform, and a multi-dimensional adaptive control algorithm based on LMS filter is adopted. Furthermore, a prototype is developed and tested, the feasibility and effectiveness of the method of micro-vibration environment simulation proposed in this paper is verified by the experimental results.

articleTitle: Design and experiment of projectile-borne storage testing system with pulsed strong magnetic field
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: To solve the problem of magnetic field measurement during electromagnetic launch, a projectile-borne storage testing system of low frequency and strong magnetic field is proposed. The commercial linear Hall sensor combined with integrated chip is used to realize small volume and high precision data recovery. The testing system is calibrated in the pulsed magnetic field generator of Wuhan National High Magnetic Field Research Center. Moreover, the shielding effectiveness of conductive and magnetic materials is considered, and the shielding effectiveness of common conductive and magnetism material is completed. The results show that the projectile-borne storage testing system can be used to measure the magnetic flux density distribution of ammunition and fuze during electromagnetic launch, which provides a reference for the electromagnetic adaptability design.

articleTitle: Dynamic stiffness calculation and vibration isolation performance analysis of rubber ring isolator of underwater glider
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Rubber ring is a common vibration isolator used in the power system of underwater vehicle. It can effectively isolate mechanical vibration and reduce sound radiation. Autonomous underwater gliders (AUGs) are new type of underwater glider, using the rubber ring to isolate the vibration and protecting the measuring system. Firstly, the rubber ring isolator model is established based on the finite element method. The Mooney Rivlin hyperelastic model is used as the material model to calculate the dynamic stiffness characteristics of rubber ring isolator with different design parameters. Then the single degree freedom vibration isolation system model of the power system of the AUG is established to calculate the vibration transfer rate. The results show that the dynamic stiffness is the main design parameter of the vibration isolation system, which influenced by the material and geometrical parameters. The dynamic stiffness of the rubber ring isolator changes nonlinearly with the frequency. The simulation results provide a reference for the parameter design and vibration isolation evaluation of the rubber ring isolator.

articleTitle: Modelling and path planning of biped robot climbing on space truss
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Climbing robots have promising applications for on-orbit assembly and maintenance of space truss structures. The dynamic process of handling modules by a biped robot climbing on a space truss is modelled and simulated in this work. The absolute nodal coordinate formulation (ANCF) is employed to model the space truss subject to overall motions, large deformations, and the links of the climbing robot. Spring-damping model is adopted to describe the grasping process of the climbing robot. The joint angles of the robot are planned to reduce the lateral vibration of the space truss. The presented model and planning scheme are demonstrated via numerical case studies. Some conclusions are given to conclude this work.

articleTitle: Multibody dynamics sensitivity analysis by discrete time transfer matrix method
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Sensitivity analysis is one of the most important approaches to measure the influence of design variables of complex multibody systems on objective functions (constraints) and guide system design optimization. The main purpose of this paper is to establish an efficient global sensitivity calculation method based on the multibody system discrete time transfer matrix method (MS-DT-TMM) and the Sobol sensitivity algorithm. The system's dynamics model is established and solved by MSDT- TMM, which does not require the global dynamics equation of the system, and avoids the problem that the calculation speed declines rapidly caused by the system scales increasing by the ordinary dynamics methods. Then, the Sobol method is applied for the subsequent global sensitivity solution. As MS-DT-TMM has high calculation efficiency, the proposed method will provide a fast calculation mean for sensitivity analysis and dynamics design of complex mechanical systems.

articleTitle: Modal characteristics analysis for car body of high-speed electric multiple units
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Aiming at the problems that track irregularity and equipment operation cause complex vibration during high-speed train operation, reduce ride comfort, and affect operation safety, the modal characteristics of the vehicle body were analyzed to improve the dynamic response characteristics of the vehicle. The finite element model of the high-speed train body was established to calculate the vibration modes of the body under different mass conditions. The influence of the hanging position and hanging number of equipment under the vehicle on the modal frequency of the vehicle body was analyzed, and the variation law of modal frequency and vibration mode was obtained. Based on finite element calculation, built the vehicle body modal test system, carried out modal tests on the vehicle body, analyzed the differences and reasons between simulation and test results, and verify the correctness of numerical calculation and finite element model. The results show that the modal frequency of the car body met the relevant design standards, and the variation trend of low-order modal modes of the car body with different mass was the same. The hanging position had an obvious influence on the vertical bending of the underframe and the torsional vibration frequency of the car body. The modal frequency of the car body increased with the increase of the number of hanging points of equipment under the vehicle.

articleTitle: Dynamics and vibration suppression of multi-robot collaborative machining system using transfer matrix method for multibody systems
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: With the advantages of high efficiency and great flexibility, multi-robot collaborative machining systems have been gradually applied to the manufacturing and assembly of large-scale structural parts such as aerospace components, wind turbine blades, etc. However, due to the collaborative operation of multiple robotic machining cells, the weakly rigid components are subjected to multiple excitations, resulting in complex vibration, which seriously affects their shape accuracy and surface quality. Therefore, it is necessary to study the dynamics of multi-robot collaborative machining systems for high-precision and high-quality applications. In this paper, the dynamic model including several mobile robotic machining cells as well as a large-scale aerospace component is established using the transfer matrix method for multibody systems (MSTMM). The machining configuration of the robots is optimized using the NSGA-II to improve their machining stiffness. Furthermore, the propagation law of vibration waves generated by multiple machining excitations on the component is studied and the cooperative vibration suppression strategy for parallel machining is proposed, which effectively reduces the vibration response at the target machining position and ensures the machining quality. This paper provides an alternative for the applications of multi-robot machining systems in the field of high-precision manufacturing of large-scale components.

articleTitle: Glass formation, crystallization, and magnetic properties of the FeNiCrNbB amorphous ribbons
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In present work, the glass forming ability (GFA), crystallization, and magnetic properties of the (Fe1-x-yNixCry)65Nb7B28 (x = 0.05, y = 0.05; x = 0.05, y = 0.1; x = 0.1, y = 0.05) alloys under both as-quenched and as-annealed state were studied. The results show that the introducing Ni and Cr significantly improves the GFA and thermal stability, while it decreases the soft magnetic properties for the as-quenched (Fe1-x-yNixCry)65Nb7B28 alloys. The Fe68Nb4Cr8Nb5B15 alloys were regarded as good glass-former with Δ - Tx = 59 K and Tx1 = 846 K. Isothermally annealing treatment were carried out on the (Fe1-xyNixCry) 80Nb5B15 alloys. The crystallization products are α --Fe and Cr3B4 phases for alloys annealed at low temperature, while mixed structure of α - Fe, Fe2B, Fe3B, Ni3B4 and Cr3B4 phases are identified for alloys annealed at high temperature. Besides, increasing annealing temperature deteriorates their soft magnetic properties. Annealing above Tp1 decreases the saturation magnetization. However, further increase of annealing temperature (> Tp2) makes the soft magnetic properties almost disappear.

articleTitle: Numerical research on the connection stiffness of hinge-locked structures for a folding wing
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Hinge-locked structures of the folding wing for high-speed vehicle contain gaps, contact and friction effects, and these factors increase the complexity of solving the local connection stiffness. In this paper, a finite element model and displacement vector equations of the folding structure are established, which provides a direct simulation method of connection stiffness. The influence of flexible deformation of the airfoil and the deflection of wing root are considered in the displacement vector equation. The effect of the clearance on the connection stiffness is discussed by adjusting the clearance between the shaft and sleeve. The load effect on stiffness is studied by varying the load distribution on the out-wing surface. The stiffness analysis method is finally established and meets the requirements of engineering design. The results show that the deformation of the hinge-locked structure is several times than that of the monolithic structure under the same load, which means that the stiffness is significantly reduced; the tension and compression asymmetric stiffness characteristics are also investigated; in addition, the increase of clearance between the hinge-locked structure shaft and wing holes decrease the connection stiffness; the load distribution on out-wing surface has no significant effect on the connection stiffness.

articleTitle: Autonomous separation strategies for in-orbit stacked satellites
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The multi-satellite launch mode is increasingly adopted in space missions. As the last stage of a rocket launch mission, multisatellite separation influences the success of the launch mission. An efficient autonomous separation strategy for in-orbit stacked satellites of 12 satellites in one launch vehicle is proposed in this paper. According to rigid-body dynamics, the dynamic equations of satellite separation are derived, and its dynamic model is established using software ADAMS. Three separation schemes are proposed for the multi-satellite separation in terms of initial spin angular velocity, mass eccentricity, and spring forces applied between satellite layers. The feasibilities and effectiveness of these schemes are evaluated by performing parametric studies.

articleTitle: A conceptual management framework of multi-source data in R&D process
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: It has been 10 years since the digital thread concept was brought up. By connecting various data in different fields, digital thread is expected to solve the problem of “information silos” in the R&D process and different fields such as design and manufacturing, potentially generating an average annual output value of tens of billions of dollars for the industry. However, due to various factors such as multi-source heterogeneous data, and complex production environments, there is still no unified framework that can adapt to different scenarios. In addition, traditional data storage architectures are difficult to cope with massive amounts of data throughout the product lifecycle. To solve the problem, a conceptual management framework of multi-source data is developed based on digital thread technology, where multi-source structured data are converted into JSON data format and stored in a unified storage mode. For unstructured data, only their addresses are stored in databases. At the same time, to improve the quality of data management, the meta-database is used to store meta information related to the data. In addition, front-end and back-end data interaction and 3D model visualization are achieved based on the Django framework. The conceptual framework is demonstrated by using an illustrative case of a part design.

articleTitle: Research on active disturbance rejection control in stability control of tank gun system
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: This paper focuses on an active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) scheme for tank gun aiming and stability control of the marching vehicles. At the same time, both the 3-DOF angular motion and 3-DOF linear motion of the vehicles are considered, which have a great impact on the tank gun of marching vehicles. Firstly, the tank gun dynamics models are established as a coupled, nonlinear and uncertain dynamic system, including two interrelated subsystems in horizontal and vertical directions. Secondly, as the ADRC can compensate the system changes caused by the unmodeled part of the system and other factors, active disturbance rejection control is proposed for the horizontal and vertical tank gun servo system respectively, so as to make the horizontal subsystem and vertical subsystem achieve practical stability. Finally, it is proved that the ADRC can make the tank gun servo system achieve high-precision stability control and tracking control under different input conditions.

articleTitle: Intelligent path planning of robotic arm considering dynamics properties
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In order to improve the intelligence of robotic arm, this paper investigates an intelligent path planning method based on Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient. The dynamics model of a 2 degree-of-freedom robotic arm is established first. On this basis, the joint driven torque is chosen as the action space, and the set of joint angle, joint angular velocity and the vector from the end-effector position to the target position is chosen as the state space. Considering the continuous characteristics of the action space and the state space, Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient method is adopted to train the robotic arm agent. The training results prove that this method can improve the intelligence of the robotic arm.

articleTitle: Parameter identification of contact model for tracked vehicles
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: As the main weapons in the ground combat, tracked vehicles have very powerful attack capabilities, can quickly and safely pass through a variety of complex road conditions. Meanwhile, considering the complex structure of a tracked vehicle and the huge cost of a real vehicle test, it is urgent to establish an accurate dynamic model and use technical means to conduct a dynamic simulation. In the process of driving and fighting, due to the working environment of the track system is extremely harsh, and there is a serious collision between the track shoes and various components, so it is very necessary to establish the contact models between track shoes and road wheels, sprockets, idlers, supporting rollers, respectively. In this paper, the authors build a virtual prototype model of a tracked vehicle based on the multi-body dynamics method and validate it through dynamics simulation. It is well known that two components in contact with each other begin to separate when the contact force is zero. However, the deformation still exists after separation. At this time, there are two situations: one is the restoration of the original state of the component, and the other is that the component undergoes irreversible plastic deformation. Traditional collision models often use approximate theories to describe collisions, which often have large errors in actual collisions. Therefore, in this paper, a novel optimization model is established to ensure that the actual recovery coefficient of two colliding components is close to the ideal recovery coefficient, and the damping coefficient of each continuous contact model is obtained based on the proposed optimization process. The test results show that the identified damping coefficient is closer to the actual situation and has excellent engineering application value.

articleTitle: Modeling of instantaneous angular speed variation of large clearance cylindrical roller bearing with local defects in rolling element
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The instantaneous angular speed (IAS) has been gradually applied to bearing fault identification. The IAS of the fault bearing have periodic disturbance by bearing dynamic modeling and fault simulation experiment in some studies. However, few of them has involved the local characteristics of IAS periodic disturbance, especially the large clearance bearing, which may lead to misdiagnosis. In this paper, a bearing rolling element fault dynamic model is proposed by considering the contact stiffness between the rolling elements and races based on the Hertzian contact theory. Moreover, A fault with 0.25 mm width and 0.2 mm depth was seeded on the roller of the bearing using the laser to verify the validity of simulation results. The results show that the periodic impulse is observed in the IAS, which is mainly due to the sudden change of torque when the defect of the rolling element contacts the raceway, especially in the load area.

articleTitle: Active optimization control of structure acoustic using genetic algorithm based on acoustic radiation mode in time-domain
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: For the acoustic radiation of plate structures, the acoustic radiation modes in time domain, whose radiation operator is built by Rayleigh integral formula, is given. These radiation modes can radiate sound power independently and the sound power of the first-order radiation mode is dominant in acoustic power radiated from the vibrating structure. Based on these conclusions, the active structures acoustic control system is designed to cancel the amplitude of first-order radiation mode by means of optimal control method. The genetic algorithm with global searching property is used to find the optimal value of the weight matrixes of the controller. Finally, the simulation verifies that the proposed method can effectively suppress the transient structural acoustic radiation and improve the efficiency and robustness of the control system.

articleTitle: Research on the protective performance of polytetrafluoroethylene for the fuze during the impact
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In response to the demand for buffering and protection when the fuze is subjected to the high overload in the process of the warhead penetrating the target, the research on the buffering performance of polytetrafluoroethylene is carried out. A vertical air hammer test device in the laboratory is used to simulate the dynamic collision process of the projectile body. And a test device is designed to simulate fuze and output acceleration signals simultaneously for comparative study of buffering performances of the material. The buffering mechanism of polytetrafluoroethylene is analyzed by using the stress wave transmission mechanism, and the effect of its thickness on the buffering performance is studied. The comparison tests of aluminum foam with polytetrafluoroethylene are conducted in multiple impacts. The results show that polytetrafluoroethylene has good buffering performance when the impact overload exceeds 40000g, and it is effective to improve the buffering performance by increasing the thickness of the buffering material. However, with the increase of thickness, the buffering performance improves fast at first and then slow. And the buffering performance of PTFE is superior to that of aluminum foam in the process of multiple impacts.

articleTitle: Study on dynamic optimization design of tank gun recoil mechanism
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Tank is one of the main weapons of modern land warfare, known as the king of land warfare. Tank gun is a typical complex mechanical system. Under the conditions of high temperature, high pressure, high velocity, high acceleration and high frequency, the gun system will produce complex dynamic response in the firing process. Therefore, it is of great significance to research on the launch dynamics of tank guns to improve it service life and firing accuracy. Recoil mechanism is known as the core of the gun system. Due to the existence of recoil mechanism, the huge force of the gun's bore when firing is greatly reduced when it is finally transmitted to the vehicle body. By rationally designing the recoil mechanism, the force and movement of the gun can be effectively controlled during firing. This paper takes a certain type of tank as the research object to study the recoil mechanism. Based on multibody dynamics theory and optimization design method, the dynamic model of the gun is established, and the optimal solution of structural parameters is obtained. The simulation results show that the maximum recoil force is reduced by 26.3% compared with the traditional gun in the recoil stroke range. The optimization design method is feasible to be applied to the recoil system of tank guns.

articleTitle: A method of constructing distributed heterogeneous simulation farm based on cloud computing
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In the paper we proposed a method to construct distributed heterogeneous CPU&GPU resource farm for high-performance simulation and rendering. First of all, computing and rendering pools are formed based on private cloud-computing techniques and connected mutually with RDMA network to construct the main farm. Secondly, CCSS(Coordination Computing & Schedule System) monitors the status of clusters and tasks, DevOps, and takes charge of the Robustness(reliability, high availability, measurability) and Scalability. Then JBS(Job Breakdown System) handles job breakdown and task scheduling. It also deals with dynamic load balance when necessary. Finally a portal is established for user interaction. The farm can be used to distributed high-performance simulation, animation rendering and deep learning.

articleTitle: Suspension dynamics analysis based on gyroscopic effect of in-wheel motor
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The application of in-wheel motor makes the unspring mass increase sharply. During the high-speed driving of the vehicle, a large gyroscopic torque will be generated when excited by steering, ground unevenness, etc. In this paper, the classical mechanics theory is used to introduce the electric wheel gyro effect into the suspension dynamic model. Firstly, the mechanism of gyroscopic effect, and the magnitude of its force on the suspension dynamic are analyzed theoretically. Then, it is verified by multi-body dynamic software. The results show that the introduce of gyro effect can reduce the force on the suspension system, but the force on the steering linkage increases and causes wheel shimmy.

articleTitle: Multi-degree-of-freedom waist-assisted exoskeleton design and model-free adaptive fault-tolerant impedance control based on time-delay estimation
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In this paper, in order to provide various waist motion assistance, a 4-SPS/SC parallel based waist-assisted exoskeleton and a time-delay estimation based model-free adaptive fault-tolerant impedance control (TDE-MFAFTIC) is proposed to achieve precise trajectory tracking and assist effects. Firstly, the mechanical structure of the exoskeleton is constructed in SolidWorks, which can assist multiple human motions. Secondly, the conversion of body position information and push rod motor position is accomplished by inverse kinematics. Thirdly, the TDE-MFAFTIC is designed not only to realize the effective trajectory tracking and human-robot interaction, but also to ensure good operation when failures occur. The inner loop of TDE-MFAFTIC is position control, where time-delay estimation (TDE) is utilized to obtain an ultra-local model to estimate the unknown dynamic information by using input and output data, which can realize the model-free based trajectory tracking with less error. In addition, taking into account the partial failure of the actuator, the adaptive fault-tolrtant (AFT) control is added to realize error control and to enhance the robustness of the algorithm. For the outer loop control, the theory of impedance control is adopted to achieve effective control of output force and to realize inclination based torque compensation by using upper body inclination, human-robot interaction and exoskeleton position. Finally, the co-simulation with SolidWorks and MATLAB/Simulink is realized to to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Dynamical influences of different aneurysm sizes on rupture risk of abdominal aorta
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The current clinical index for surgical intervention of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA) is mainly based on measuring its maximum diameter. However, ruptures in AAAs do not necessarily occur at this location and conditions of rupture are still unclear. This study focuses on the understanding of the aneurysms rupture mechanisms. A set of fluid-structure interaction (FSI) models is developed to investigate the AAAs expansion into low wall shear stress (WSS) regions. 3D model geometries for different clinical stages are acquired from the literature including the final stage just before rupture. Blood is simulated as non-Newtonian fluid and dymanic boundary conditions are enforced to simulate blood pulsations. Local and averaged WSS, which are the critical parameters affecting rupture conditions, are evaluated based on the computational results. It is demonstrated that both averaged and local WSS correlate well with the rapid expansion of AAA as well as with rupture locations. From the present FSI study, blood recirculation is one of the main mechanism leading to a decrease in the WSS, which significantly increase the risk of rupture. The latter agrees with the outcomes of previous studies.

articleTitle: Dynamics of circular thin membrane solar arrays based on ground zerogravity simulation test
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Our country's asteroid prober will use circular thin membrane solar arrays, which is the first time for China to use this technology. In this paper, the dynamics of the deployment of the circular thin-film solar arrays in space and under the simulated zero-gravity environment are compared. Firstly, the kinematics and dynamics of the circular solar thin-film arrays in zero gravity and low gravity environment are analyzed based on ADAMS. Results indicate the importance of gravity compensation accuracy in the ground experiment. This step is necessary as a reference for subsequent analysis. Besides, the zero-gravity compensation system is designed carefully for the circular solar arrays, which mainly uses the passive support method based on the air-pad to compensate for the gravity of the solar arrays. The normal deployment of the solar arrays will certainly be affected by the disturbing force generated by the zero-gravity test system. These effects are measured experimentally and introduced into ADMAS. A comparison of the kinematics & dynamics of the circular thin-film solar arrays between the real and the simulated zero-gravity environments shows the feasibility and limitations of this zero-gravity compensation system, which can guide engineering practice.

articleTitle: Influence of non-uniform flow on hysteresis effect of pitching hydrofoil
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The hysteresis effect of pitching hydrofoil in uniform and non-uniform incoming flow are investigated theoretically and numerically. The numerical method is validated through the experimental results under steady uniform conditions. It has been shown that the simulation can capture the hysteresis effect of pitching hydrofoil. The added force caused by the pitching motion is an important factor of hysteresis phenomenon. When the sinusoidal periodical perturbations of incoming flow are carried, the hysteresis loop of lift coefficient curve are enlarged. According to the variation of the incoming flow, the lift coefficient curve are divided into four stages: S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>(α+=5.0°∼α+=10.0°), S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>(α+=10.0°∼α+=15.0°), S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>(α-=15.0°∼α-=10.0°) and S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>(α-=10.0°∼α-=5.0°). The flow structure and corresponding hydrodynamics of four stages under uniform and non-uniform conditions are compared and analyzed. Due to the non-uniform incoming velocity, the positive added lift increases in S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> stage and declines in S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> stage, thus leading to the increase of hysteresis loop. For the S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> stage, the “+” TEV is advanced because of the variational incoming flow. In S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> stage, the formation and development mode of “-” TEV are changed.

articleTitle: Thermo-mechanical coupling simulation of PBX explosive charge in launch environment
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The distribution of internal stress and temperature of explosive charge in launch environment is significant to determine the launch safety of explosive charge. PBX is composed of energetic particles, binder and metal powder, hence it can perform the viscoelastic mechanical properties under the external force loading condition. The generalized Maxwell constitutive equation is embedded into LS-DYNA program by secondary development technology, and verified rational after the simulation of launch safety experiment of explosive charge. Utilizing the constitutive equation and considering the influence of viscoelastic work and chemical reaction heat, the distribution of internal stress and temperature of explosive charge in launch environment is acquired. The results indicate that the viscoelastic work and chemical reaction heat produce a 4K highest temperature rise of explosive charge, the explosive charge without defects cannot ignite in the launch process. The results provide a certain guiding significance for the launch safety evaluation of explosive charge.

articleTitle: High performance on-orbit boundary simulation for large spacecraft microvibration environment test
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Micro-vibration environment test is aimed at evaluating the weak mechanical signal that may remarkably affect the imaging quality of the astronomical telescope. Through the micro-vibration environment test, not only the vibration response can be obtained, but also the satellite modal as well as the load transfer path(LTP). They are useful references for improving the telescope's imaging quality. In order to achieve the on-orbit free boundary in the laboratory, it is necessary to develop large bearing test fixture with low rigidity. This paper provides a model describing the satellite-boundary binary structure in a concise manner: (1) give a completed design recipe for developing free boundary fixture, (2) introduce the large deformation modal analysis theory into the frequency characteristic analysis; (3) compare the indicators between typical fixture design with the practical test. Result shows that the current CAE method that used to design the micro-vibration test fixture is valid in satellite environmental engineering. The method suggested in this paper has been applied to verify several optical satellites in China, to help them guarantee the stability of optical axis with high resolution. Such large-bearing low-rigidity boundary design ideology can also be useful reference for other facilities in many fields, to help get them a much more precise simulation outcome.

articleTitle: Design and simulation of linear transverse flux eddy current damper for vehicle suspension
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: An eddy current damper, which partially converts vibration energy to heat one in order to reduce vibration, is studied and applied in fields of mechanism, vehicle etc. This paper presents a novel Linear Transverse Flux Eddy Current Damper(LTFECD), which is used in vehicle suspension system. The transverse flux, which means the direction of up-and-down movement of plunger is vertical relatively to the plane of magnetic field, is a highlight of the design. It facilitates the mechanical structure, and the volume space is used effectively and sufficiently. The copper winding is applied, which provides an enhanced force combined with eddy current damping force. The copper winding can also adjust the damping force accordingly. A three-dimensional model is designed and electromagnetic simulation with finite element software is performed. The model of a single wheel vehicle suspension is built and simulated with the LTFECD. The result of design and simulation shows that the LTFECD characteristics can meet the requirement of vehicle suspension, and the suspension with LTFECD can reduce the vertical acceleration of sprung mass body. The improvement of design is discussed for engineering application.

articleTitle: Structural design and intelligent control of lower limb knee rehabilitation exoskeleton based on motion intention estimation method
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In modern society, physical disabilities induced by knee related diseases are gaining attentions, where demand for rehabilitation exoskeletons for single knee joint assisted treatment is increasing. Meanwhile, most rehabilitation exoskeletons of medical industry are designed based on entire lower extremity of human body, and there are relatively few exoskeleton robots for single joint rehabilitation. In this paper, the structure of exoskeleton based on actual motion characteristics of human knee joint is designed by Solidworks, and a virtual prototype through joint simulation with Simscape Multibody is generated to provide a platform for building control system later. The generated virtual prototype is validated by an intelligent controller which is based on an ultra-local model, a linear extended state observer (LESO) and a sliding mode sub-controller (SMC). Finally, considering factors like actual control system and human-machine interaction, a joint angle estimation model based on surface electromyography (sEMG) signal is used to obtain predicted angle as desired input in control system to further validate the rationality of human-machine interaction (HCI).

articleTitle: Fatigue reliability calculation of track supporting structure based on vehicle dynamic analysis
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Under cyclic loading, fatigue failure often occurs in the track supporting structure, which is welded on the side deck of the vehicle body. In this paper, the fatigue reliability of track supporting structure is calculated by the track dynamic analysis, welding seam damage modeling , and random sampling method. First, the digital model of typical pavement roughness is established; then, a design plan for the fatigue simulation test of the track supporting structure is proposed, the dynamic analysis of the track supporting structure is carried out, and the fatigue damage response surface model is constructed; finally, the fatigue reliability of the supporting structure under random working conditions is calculated by Monte Carlo random sampling method. In that case, the influence of road grade and vehicle speed to fatigue characteristics are obtained. Results show that the pavement roughness is positively correlated with the fatigue reliability of the track supporting structure, while the driving speed has opposite trend. Therefore, in the track supporting structure design, the influence of random combination characteristics of working conditions must be fully considered, and the reliability analysis can be executed by dynamic simulation and random data drive technology.

articleTitle: Modified reduced transfer equations for linear multibody system dynamics
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The transfer matrix method for multibody systems (MSTMM) has been extensively applied in various engineering practices, pursuing a high computational efficiency. Partitioning the state vector of each connecting point into two complementary reduced state vectors and relating them by a point-wise linear formulation leads to a reduced form of the MSTMM. In this way, sequential multiplications of the transfer matrices of the components will be avoided, and the numerical stability of the MSTMM gets better. According to existing manners, the original transfer matrices of all the body components should be obtained first in the context of the reduced MSTMM. Modified reduced transfer equations for linear multibody systems independent from the original transfer equations are proposed in this paper to eliminate useless operations relating to zero operands in the transfer matrices and consistence matrices for multi-input body components. The modified reduced transfer equations for linear multibody systems is verified by comparing the computational results with those obtained by using the original reduced transfer equations as well as finite element method.

articleTitle: Strain-rate-dependent model for elastoplastic normal repeated impacts of a sphere on a beam
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Normal repeated impacts are common phenomena in machine dynamics. When repeated impacts occur, the plastic deformation from previous collisions can affect the behavior of following collisions. To increase the efficiency of calculation and analysis, in this paper a hybrid model (analytical-numerical model) is developed to analysis of the impact transient response of a flexible beam, driven by normal low-velocity repeated transverse impact of a sphere. The hybrid model include a refined contact model and a combined discretization model. The dependence of material strain rate is considered in both the sub-models. During each impact, the sphere strikes the beam at the same position. In subsequent impacts the accumulated contact plastic deformation of the beam remains. The transient responses of repeated impacts of beam simulated by the hybrid model is validated using experimental test and 3D finite element (FE) model. The comparisons of the results of hybrid model with the results of finite element (FE) analysis and experimental show that the hybrid model is valid which can accurately predict the transient response of normal repeated impacts. The calculating efficiency comparison between hybrid model and the FE model shows that the hybrid model is suitable and highly efficient for parametric study.

articleTitle: Study on vacuum diffusion welding process of cold plate for small channel assembly
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: This paper introduces a high efficiency cooling T/R module small channel cold plate structure, and explores the vacuum diffusion welding technology suitable for the forming of small channel cold plate. According to the case of water leakage of a small channel cold plate of a certain type of component, the vacuum diffusion welding process is studied. The vacuum diffusion welding technology is optimized by improving the welding surface quality, refining welding parameters and solid solution aging parameters. The process test piece is designed to verify the process parameters and the heat dissipation performance of the test piece is tested. The results show that the optimized process is used to form the small channel cold plate, which meets the requirements of water tightness and heat dissipation, and improves the production qualification rate.

articleTitle: Analysis and experimental validation of air resistance changing trend under all-climate condition
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The extreme low-temperature environment can affect the electrified components of electric vehicles, leading to significantly reduced driving range. Besides, driving resistance is also a crucial factor, especially the air resistance, that influences the overall performance. However, some core parameters are usually regarded as constant values (e.g., air density, air viscosity), even calculating the accurate air resistance under all-climate conditions. Such hypotheses have not been validated well in a wide temperature range, resulting in potential deviation when considering the dynamic and economic issues. To solve this problem, a convenient and universal calculation method to find out the accurate value of air resistance force under all-climate conditions is proposed in this paper. The basic principle that how temperature affects air resistance is elucidated based on aerodynamic analysis, and the formula for calculating air resistance force at different temperatures is redefined. By using interpolation methods, the curve of air resistance with temperature at a certain place is presented. Eventually, the theoretical calculation results are compared with experimental data from an electric passenger vehicle under low-temperature conditions, which verifies the correctness of the conclusions. It is concluded that the air resistance force cannot be regarded intuitively as a certain constant. In detail, the air resistance force increases by about 4% on average for every 10°C drop in temperature, and the lower the temperature the faster the air resistance increases.

articleTitle: Study on prediction of vertical target dispersion of vehicle-mounted artillery weapon
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Vertical target dispersion is the main parameter to measure the firing efficiency of artillery weapon systems which directly determines the combat capability of the artillery on the battlefield. In order to accurately evaluate the battlefield capability of vehicle-mounted artillery weapons, a simulation model of the whole vehicle-mounted artillery dynamic system is established. The whole system is simplified into multi-rigid-body system, such as constraint between the wheel and the ground into contact constraint and constraint between the front, middle and rear axles and the wheel into rotating hinge constraint. The influence on the vehicle attitude under the conditions of lateral consecutive high rate firing is analyzed, and the vertical target dispersion can be studied using trajectory simulation, which provides important theoretical support for the prediction of artillery vertical target dispersion.

articleTitle: Review on the dispersion characteristics and damage assessment of fuel-air explosive
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: We reviewed the detonation development of fuel-air explosive mainly including dispersal process mechanism, dispersion characteristics, theoretical simulation methods and damage assessment, which is helpful to deepen the understanding of detonation effect of fuel-air explosive. The dispersal process and diffusion of fuel-air explosive are easily affected by the fuel material properties, experimental devices and the ratio of central explosives. What's more, the energy release process of fuelair explosive is different with that of commonly used energetic materials, which includes longer overpressure-impulse compound damage model, larger damage radius and wider area of action. In conclusion, the fuel-air explosive would be extensively applied to broad-scale attack and destroy various middle weak targets, and plays an important role in future military application.

articleTitle: VMD method based on frequency domain correlated kurtosis and its application in multi-fault diagnosis of wheelset bearing
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Parameter-adaptive VMD method is often used in rolling bearing fault diagnosis. The two key parameters K and α of VMD can be determined adaptively by using an intelligent optimization algorithm. The working environment of wheelset bearing is complex, and the existing parameter-adaptive VMD method is difficult to accurately extract the fault information of wheelset bearing. To solve this problem, a parameter-adaptive VMD method guided by the envelope power spectrum correlated kurtosis is proposed. Correlated kurtosis has strong directivity and is not affected by impact noise and cyclic stationary noise. Meanwhile, at low SNR, the frequency domain correlated kurtosis is more stable than the time-domain correlated kurtosis. Therefore, taking the local maximum envelope power spectrum correlated kurtosis as the objective function, and using the global searching ability of PSO, the optimal parameter combination of VMD can be adaptively determined. VMD is used to analyze the signal, calculate the envelope power spectrum correlated kurtosis of each component, and select the largest one for envelope spectrum analysis. Through simulation and experimental analysis, it is verified that this method can accurately extract the fault characteristics of wheelset bearing under complex interference.

articleTitle: Mechanical behaviour of TA2 titanium under dynamic uniaxial compression
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Titanium alloy is widely used in aerospace, aviation and military industry. However, titanium alloy is sensitive to adiabatic shear damage due to its low density and low thermal conductivity, and it is easy to produce adiabatic shear band under impact. In this paper, the dynamic mechanical properties and deformation failure characteristics of TA2 titanium were studied by using Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar (SHPB). The experimental results show that TA2 titanium exhibits strain rate sensitivity and thermal softening effect. At the same time, the microstructure and metallographic analysis of the recovered sample showed that the adiabatic shear band was in the opposite biconical shape in space, and the crack propagated along the adiabatic shear band when the sample was destroyed.

articleTitle: Jump angle modeling and dispersion simulation for gun firing evaluation
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In order to obtain relatively accurate firing angle and direction, a special jump angle evaluation is typically carried out in the firing table test. In the jump angle evaluation, the gun barrel is typically kept horizontal. The bullet dispersion of vertical target is measured at a certain distance from the gun muzzle to the target when the jump angle is calculated. In this paper, a six-degree-of-freedom rigid external ballistic model of projectile was established. Based on the principle of flat launch jump angle test, the simulation model of flat launch jump angle evaluation was obtained. Based on the Bootstrap calculation method of small sample was used to calculate the mean and variance of test results to improve robust property. The simulation was in good agreement with the experimental results. A kind of calculation and simulation code of jump angle was developed, which could be used for dispersion simulation of jump angle under different firing conditions.

articleTitle: On the natural frequency of elastic contact for curved rough interface based on fractal theory
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Based on the fractal theory, a pure elastic contact model of the rough interface is proposed to bridge the relationship between the contact force and equivalent deformation. The explicit expression of equivalent deformation of the rough surface is derived, and the contact force is deduced by the continuity of asperity base diameter. Accordingly, a single-degree-of-freedom undamped free vibration model is established to analyze the natural frequency characteristics of the rough contact interface. Effects of surface topography on the contact force and natural frequency are investigated. Results show that the natural frequency of the rough contact interface is affected by the initial conditions. A rougher interface corresponds to a stronger nonlinearity. The natural frequency of the system is gradually stabilized with the increment of fractal dimension, i.e. a smoother contact interface. Therefore, it is necessary to consider the surface rough morphology for the dynamic analysis of mechanical structure.

articleTitle: Vibration analysis of elastically supported graphene strengthened beams
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Vibrations of a functionally graded graphene strengthened Euler-Bernoulli beam with a vertical spring support is investigated in this study. The main objective of this work is to examine how the vibrational behaviour of a graphene strengthened beam of different graphene distributions and boundary conditions is affected by the addition of an intermediate spring attached to it vertically. The distribution functions for the continuous variations of graphene nanoparticles' weight fraction in the thickness direction are defined such that the overall graphene amount in each beam of different distribution patterns is fixed. The reinforcement effects of graphene on the material properties of the beam structure are considered using a modified twodimensional Halpin-Tsai micromechanics model and a rule of mixtures. The deformation of the beam is modelled utilising the Euler-Bernoulli beam theory. The spring is introduced to the system by employing a Dirac delta function. The differential equation of motion is obtained utilising Hamilton's principle, which is then solved for natural frequencies using an assumed eigen-function method for different boundary conditions. The influences of the location and stiffness of the spring on the natural frequencies of beams reinforced with various graphene distributions are explored and discussed.

articleTitle: Dynamics control for complex mechanical systems with nonlinear actuators using the transfer matrix method for linear multibody systems
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Smart actuators, such as magnetorheological dampers, piezoelectric actuators et al., are increasingly being explored for various nano-positioning and vibration control applications. However, those actuators reduce control performance due to the existence of inherent hysteresis nonlinearities between the input and the output. The nonlinearities may cause undesirable inaccuracies, oscillations, poor control performance even leading to instabilities of the closed-loop system. In order to accurately model complex mechanical systems with such nonlinear actuators, a comprehensive mathematical model, which uses the transfer matrix method for linear multibody systems (linear MSTMM) to model the linear dynamics properties and the hysteresis model to describe the hysteresis nonlinearities, is presented. And then a hysteresis observer based on the hysteresis model is established to compensate the hysteresis nonlinearity of actuators. Then, a hybrid controller combining the proposed linearization and PID control for complex mechanical systems based on the comprehensive model is proposed and explored. The experimental results show that the proposed hybrid control method can achieve precise control of the complex mechanical systems with nonlinear actuators.

articleTitle: Sensitivity analysis method for frequency response function based on extended transfer matrix method for linear multibody systems
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The sensitivity analysis for frequency response function is of great importance in the areas of system identification, model updating, dynamic optimization, vibration control and structural damage detection, et al. In allusion to the problems resulting from the prohibitive computational cost using the direct method and the modal truncated errors using the modal superposition method, a novel sensitivity analysis method for frequency response function based on the extended transfer matrix method for linear multibody systems is proposed. The sensitivity transfer equations of elements and system are established utilizing the direct differentiation method, from which the frequency response function sensitivity can be accordingly obtained. The results are also used to the sensitivity analysis for random vibration response. The proposed strategy is analytically and numerically validated by examples, indicating that it not only inherits the advantages of transfer matrix method for multibody systems that the system global dynamics equations are not needed, the system matrix order is low, the solution procedure is highly stylized, and the computational speed is high, but also achieves accurate computation of frequency response function sensitivity without modal truncation and the assumption of proportional damping.

articleTitle: The study on the nonlinear variation law of power MOSFET's environmental thermal resistance
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: As an important component in the electromechanical control system, power MOSFET has been widely used in important fields such as electric power, transportation and aerospace. Environmental thermal resistance exists between the shell and the environment of power MOFSET, and its numerical variation has a significant impact on the thermal safety and residual life of power MOFSET. In order to explore the variation law of the environmental thermal resistance, this paper uses the power MOFSET temperature rise experimental platform and the junction-environment thermal network model to measure and analyze the environmental thermal resistance under natural convection and forced air cooling conditions. The experimental results show that under natural convection conditions, the thermal resistance of the power MOFSET environment decreases power exponentially with the increase of the steady-state shell temperature. Under forced air cooling condition, the thermal resistance of power MOFSET environment increases exponentially with the decrease of ambient wind speed. The exponential function that accurately describes the variation law of the above environmental thermal resistance can be obtained through data fitting, which provides important theoretical support for the development of thermal safety assessment and life prediction methods of power devices.

articleTitle: Characterizing the bond-slip behaviours of steel bar in concrete under dynamic loading using a modified high-speed tensile testing device
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: This study conducted pullout tests to characterize the bond-slip behaviors of plain steel bars in concrete under dynamic loading. In the pullout tests, we adopt the high-speed tensile testing device to measure the bond-slip curves for plane steel bar and concrete at dynamic strain rate varying from 3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> to 103 mm/s. By increasing the strain rate, the results show a significant increase in bond strength at the interface of steel bar and concrete. We also observe that the failure mode generally changes from pullout to splitting with increasing strain rate. The strain-rate effect on the tensile strength of concrete and steel bar is further evaluated by comparing dynamic increase factor (DIF) with strain rate. The results show a significant increase in DIF at high strain rate compared with that at low strain rate, suggesting a more pronounced strain-rate effect on bond strength at high strain rate.

articleTitle: Study on test of oil gap and damping of diesel reel spring-type torsional vibration damper
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Torsional vibration damper plays an important role in reducing torsional vibration of diesel crankshaft. Reel spring-type torsional vibration damper is widely used in high-power diesel with medium-high speed. By using this kind of damper, shaft natural frequency can be greatly adjusted, and the torsional amplitude of crankshaft free end can be reduced. Crankshaft stress can be decreased as well. The inertia, stiffness, and damping are the characteristic parameters on reel spring-type damper design. Especially, damping is a significant parameter closely related to structure dimension to reducing torsional vibration. In this paper, a free modal test of reel spring-type damper is carried out, and it is concluded that the damping of reel spring-type damper decreases with the increase of the side plate oil gap. By establishing the damping calculation model of the damper, using fluid theory and CFD simulation analysis method, the accuracy of the test results is proved. This conclusion provides a basis for the design and optimization of reel spring-type torsional vibration damper.

articleTitle: Effect of initial impact energy on contact stiffness in linear contact law of low velocity elastic-plastic impact
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In this paper, the loading force-indentation curve of low-velocity impact between an elastic-plastic plate and an elastic-plastic sphere by finite element (FE) analysis is investigated. The impactor mass and impact velocity are varied to cover a wide range of initial impact energies. The comparisons between the linear contact law using theoretical contact stiffness and the FE results show much difference. Based on the observation of FE data, the practical contact stiffness is strongly affected by the initial impact energy due to the nonlinearity of practical contact stiffness in the elastic-plastic impact. The definition of the equivalent contact stiffness is proposed to obtain the practical contact stiffness for the elastic-plastic impact accurately. The relations between theoretical and equivalent contact stiffness are massively calculated by FE covering a wide range of initial impact energies. Based on the FE results of the relations, a coefficient to revise the theoretical contact stiffness is suggested and a piecewise expression of the coefficient is presented by curve-fitting approach. It is demonstrated that the revised contact stiffness agrees well with the practical contact stiffness. This revised contact stiffness is of great value in predicting the maximum impact force in low velocity elastic-plastic impact between elastic-plastic bodies.

articleTitle: A method of normal contact force calculation between spherical particles for discrete element method
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: The contact force calculation model plays an important role in the discrete element method (DEM), but the existing models have a large deviation from the actual situation when calculating the normal contact force of brittle materials. The Volume model, a new normal contact force calculation model, is established based on the overlap between two particles in collision contact. When the geometric features and contact depth δ are specified, other contact parameters are automatically followed, including contact direction, contact point and force magnitude. Due to the geometrical symmetry of spherical particles, the results can be simplified. Based on the theory of Volume model, the formula for calculating the normal contact force of spherical particle element is derived. Comparing with the existing normal contact force calculation models, the Volume model has higher accuracy in brittle materials. In addition, the complete discrete element method algorithm is developed in this paper. Taking concrete spherical particles as an example, the spherical particle experiment is designed by embedding the contact model into the program. The results show that the Volume model has higher accuracy in calculating the normal contact force of brittle materials.

articleTitle: Dynamics modeling and simulation on single-base propellant deterrent coating process
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: In order to study the influence of the deterrent coating process parameters of single-base propellant on its deterrent coating mass uniformity, based on the Discrete Element Method (DEM), the dynamics model of the deterrent coating process is established. The effect of different deterrent coating process parameters (such as drum speed, drum inclination and spray angle, etc.) on the coating mass uniformity of the propellant is simulated. The results show that within a certain range, the greater the rotating drum speed, the coating mass uniformity of the propellant is better; the larger the drum inclination angle, the coating mass uniformity of propellant is better; under the condition of a certain spray flow, the larger the spray angle, the coating mass uniformity of propellant is better. This study provides a strong theoretical basis for studying the deterrent manufacturing process of single-base propellant.

articleTitle: Frequency domain response characteristics of flow induced vibration on NACA0009 hydrofoil
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Hydrofoils have been widely used in ocean and offshore structures. The related research on their elastic response in turbulent flow is numerically challenging and of great interests for further engineering application. In this paper, the fluid-structure coupling numerical simulation of three-dimensional elastic hydrofoil is performed. The simulation is achieved using commercial Star CCM+. The SST (Shear Stress Transfer) k-ω turbulence model is used to simulate the vortex shedding and near-wall flow characteristics under different velocities. Then by coupling the FVM (Finite Volume Method), the elastic response of the hydrofoils is analyzed. The frequency domain characteristics of the flow induced vibration are analyzed by using fast Fourier transform. The natural frequency and corresponding vibration mode of the hydrofoil at low frequency are used to explain the co-effect of the natural frequency of the hydrofoil and the lift oscillation frequency on the coupled vibration state. Thus, the cavitation simulation based on Schnerr-Sauer model is carried out for FSI analysis. The dynamic response regime transformation is observed, subsequent frequency domain analysis and flow field characteristics are also presented.

articleTitle: Dynamics simulation and performance evaluation of a spaceflight complex load-bearing magnesium-lithium alloy module
publicationTitle: 1st International Conference on Mechanical System Dynamics (ICMSD 2022)
abstract: Achieving lightweight manufacturing of spacecraft and improving cost-efficiency ratio is one of the strategic goals of space technology development in the 21st century. As an ultra-light alloy, magnesium-lithium alloy has high specific strength, specific stiffness, excellent vibration resistance and high-energy particle penetration resistance, and is one of the best materials for manufacturing spacecraft hull. Combined with the actual working condition, the dynamics simulation of the magnesiumlithium alloy module was carried out, and the forming process was optimized, the heat treatment of the prefabricated billet was compounded with the superplastic extrusion forming process, and the heat treatment was carried out after the completion of the superplastic extrusion deformation to realize the heat treatment in the mold, which reduced the input of the heat treatment tooling and ensured the effective cooperation between the heat treatment tooling and the workpiece; the performance of the formed cavity was verified through the static experiment, and the module test piece was subjected to the load given in the outline. The strength of the module test piece meets the design requirements under the load given in the outline, and achieves the near-net forming of complex components of ultra-light magnesium-lithium alloy, which meets the urgent demand for complex components of ultra-light alloy for spacecraft.
